
### EmailLayout

The 560px email shell that holds header, body, cards and footer.

Compose an email preview from `EmailHeader`, `EmailCard`, `EmailButton` and `EmailFooter` inside it, and wrap the whole thing in `EmailPreviewFrame` to show subject and sender. These parts render a preview in the app; inline the styles before sending real mail.

- Name: `email-layout` (component, Email)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/email-layout` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { EmailLayout } from "@/components/ui/email-layout"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/email-layout"`)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | `React.ReactNode` |  | Email sections, top to bottom. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<EmailLayout>
  <EmailHeader brand="Lumen" />
  <EmailCard title="Invoice INV-2041">$12,400.00 due Nov 30.</EmailCard>
  <div className="px-6 pb-6"><EmailButton href="https://app.example.com">Pay invoice</EmailButton></div>
  <EmailFooter />
</EmailLayout>
```

### EmojiPicker

A compact grid of emoji buttons for reactions, with arrow-key navigation and one tab stop.

Use inside a `Popover` from a reaction button, or inline under a message. For a row of existing reaction counts use `ReactionBar`. Arrow keys move through the grid, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter or Space picks.

### EmptySearch

The "no results" state for a search or filtered list, echoing the query back.

Use when a search or filter returns nothing. For a list that has no data yet use `EmptyState` or `EmptyTable`; for a failed request use `ErrorState`.

- Name: `empty-search` (component, Feedback)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/empty-search` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { EmptySearch } from "@/components/ui/empty-search"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/empty-search"`)

- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/empty-search (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/empty-search.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| query? | `string` |  | The search text, quoted in the title. |
| description? | `string` | `"Try a different query or clear filte...` | Hint under the title. |
| onClear? | `() => void` |  | When set, shows a "Clear search" button that calls it. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<EmptySearch query={query} onClear={() => setQuery("")} />
```

### EmptyState

A centred placeholder for a page or panel with nothing in it yet: icon, title, hint and one action.

Use for first-run screens ("No invoices yet"). For an empty table body use `EmptyTable`; for zero search results use `EmptySearch`; for a failure use `ErrorState`; for a missing page use `NotFoundState`.

- Name: `empty-state` (component, Feedback)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/empty-state` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { EmptyState } from "@/components/ui/empty-state"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/empty-state"`)
- Uses: button
- Related: empty-table, empty-search, error-state, not-found-state, offline-state, retry-block, server-error-state, welcome-screen
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/empty-state (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/empty-state.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `string` |  | One short line saying what is empty. |
| description? | `string` |  | What to do next. |
| actionLabel? | `string` |  | Label of the primary button. The button only renders when this is set. |
| onAction? | `() => void` |  | Called by the primary button. |
| icon? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Decorative icon above the title. A quiet placeholder tile renders when omitted. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<EmptyState
  icon={<ReceiptIcon className="size-6" />}
  title="No invoices yet"
  description="Create your first invoice to start getting paid."
  actionLabel="New invoice"
  onAction={() => router.push("/invoices/new")}
/>
```

### EnvSwitcher

A Dev / Staging / Prod segmented control for scoping a console to one environment.

Use in a dashboard header or settings page to choose which environment's keys, logs or config are shown. To label a single environment use `EnvBadge`; for other option sets use `SegmentedControl` directly.

- Name: `env-switcher` (component, Dev tools)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/env-switcher` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { EnvSwitcher } from "@/components/ui/env-switcher"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/env-switcher"`)
- Uses: segmented-control
- Related: env-badge, segmented-control
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/env-switcher (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/env-switcher.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value? | `string` |  | Controlled environment: "dev", "staging" or "prod". |
| defaultValue? | `string` | `"prod"` | Initial environment when uncontrolled. |
| onChange? | `(v: string) => void` |  | Called with "dev", "staging" or "prod". |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
const [env, setEnv] = React.useState("prod")
<EnvSwitcher value={env} onChange={setEnv} />
```

### ErrorState

A centred failure message for a panel or page that could not load, with an optional retry.

It is a role="alert" region, so screen readers announce it when it appears. Use when a fetch fails. For a 5xx page use `ServerErrorState`; for a 404 use `NotFoundState`; for an inline form error use `InlineAlert`; for "no data yet" use `EmptyState`.

- Name: `error-state` (component, Feedback)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/error-state` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ErrorState } from "@/components/ui/error-state"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/error-state"`)
- Uses: button
- Related: server-error-state, not-found-state, inline-alert, empty-state, empty-search
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/error-state (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/error-state.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title? | `string` | `"Something went wrong"` | One short line saying what failed. |
| description? | `string` | `"Try again in a moment."` | What happened and what to try. |
| onRetry? | `() => void` |  | When set, shows a retry button that calls it. |
| retryLabel? | `string` | `"Try again"` | Label of the retry button. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ErrorState description="We couldn't load invoices." onRetry={() => refetch()} />
```

### EventCalendar

A week and day event scheduler with overlap layout, an all-day row, a current time line and click to create.

Use for meeting and shift schedules. Events are plain objects with Date `start` and `end`; `calendars` set their colours. Click an empty slot (or focus a day column and use Up/Down then Enter) to fire `onCreate`. For a month grid use `CalendarMonth`; for a list of upcoming events use `CalendarAgenda`; for project timelines use `GanttChart`.

- Name: `event-calendar` (component, Dashboard)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/event-calendar` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { EventCalendar } from "@/components/ui/event-calendar"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/event-calendar"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Uses: button, segmented-control
- Related: calendar-month, calendar-agenda, gantt-chart, calendar
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/event-calendar (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/event-calendar.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| events? | `CalendarEvent[]` |  | Events to place. Defaults to a sample Lumen work week around today. |
| calendars? | `CalendarSource[]` | `CALENDARS` | Calendars that colour events and fill the legend. |
| view? | `CalendarView` |  | Controlled view. |
| defaultView? | `CalendarView \| "auto"` | `"auto"` | "auto" picks Day under 600px of width and Week above. |
| onViewChange? | `(view: CalendarView) => void` |  | Called when the Week/Day control or a day header changes the view. |
| defaultDate? | `Date` |  | Any date inside the first week or day shown. Defaults to today. |
| onDateChange? | `(date: Date) => void` |  |  |
| weekStartsOn? | `0 \| 1` | `1` | 0 for Sunday, 1 for Monday. |
| scrollToHour? | `number` | `8` | Hour the grid scrolls to on mount. |
| hourHeight? | `number` | `48` | Pixel height of one hour row. |
| height? | `number` | `520` | Pixel height of the scrolling time grid. |
| slotMinutes? | `number` | `30` | Minutes a click on an empty slot snaps to. |
| onCreate? | `(range: { start: Date; end: Date }) => void` |  | Called when an empty slot is clicked or chosen with the keyboard. |
| onEventClick? | `(event: CalendarEvent) => void` |  | Called when an event block is clicked or activated with the keyboard. |
| locale? | `string` | `"en-US"` | BCP 47 locale for dates and times, e.g. "en-GB". |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<EventCalendar
  events={[{ id: "1", title: "Sprint planning", start: new Date(2026, 10, 16, 11), end: new Date(2026, 10, 16, 12), calendar: "eng" }]}
  calendars={[{ id: "eng", label: "Engineering", tone: "info" }]}
  onCreate={({ start, end }) => openNewEvent(start, end)}
  onEventClick={(ev) => openEvent(ev.id)}
/>
```

### ExpandableRow

A bordered row whose header toggles a details panel underneath (a disclosure).

Use for one collapsible block of extra detail, like a log entry or an invoice line. For several mutually exclusive sections use `Accordion`; for an unstyled show/hide use `Collapsible`.

Controlled: `<ExpandableRow open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="…">`.

| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Content of the details panel. |

| defaultOpen? | `boolean` | `false` | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| onOpenChange? | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called with the next open state. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx

</ExpandableRow>
```

### ExportData

A settings row that explains a data export and offers one button to request it.

Use on account or workspace settings pages (GDPR exports, backups). It only calls `onExport`: building the file and showing progress are yours, through `description` and `actionLabel`. For a destructive action use `DangerZone`; for a download list use `FileList`.

| actionLabel? | `string` | `"Request export"` | Button label. |

```tsx
<ExportData onExport={() => requestExport()} />
```

### FeedbackThumbs

A pair of thumbs up / thumbs down toggle buttons for rating an answer or article.

Use under AI responses and help articles. Pressing the active thumb again clears the vote (value becomes null). For message actions like copy and retry use `MessageActions`; for star ratings use `Rating`; for up/down vote counts use `VoteControl`.

- Name: `feedback-thumbs` (component, AI chat)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/feedback-thumbs` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { FeedbackThumbs } from "@/components/ui/feedback-thumbs"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/feedback-thumbs"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Related: message-actions, rating, vote-control
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/feedback-thumbs (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/feedback-thumbs.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value? | `"up" \| "down" \| null` |  | Controlled vote. null means no vote. |
| defaultValue? | `"up" \| "down" \| null` | `null` | Initial vote when uncontrolled. |
| onChange? | `(v: "up" \| "down" \| null) => void` |  | Called with the new vote, or null when cleared. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<FeedbackThumbs onChange={(v) => track("answer_feedback", { vote: v })} />
```

### FileDropzone

A drag-and-drop upload zone with accept/reject drag states, type and size validation, and a file list with progress, retry and remove.

Click, Enter or Space opens the file picker; dropping works too. Pass `upload` to stream progress per file; without it files are listed as done at once and handed to `onFiles`. For a single avatar use `AvatarUpload`; for an image with preview and crop use `ImageUpload` or `ImageCropper`; for listing existing files use `FileList`.

GOLD STANDARD COMPONENT. Four designed states (rest, hover, drag-accept, drag-reject); the hairline dashed border is SVG so the dashes stay crisp and march while dragging.

- Name: `file-dropzone` (component, Forms)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/file-dropzone` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { FileDropzone } from "@/components/ui/file-dropzone"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/file-dropzone"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Related: avatar-upload, image-upload, image-cropper, file-list, attachment-chip, bulk-user-import, file-row, media-library
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/file-dropzone (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/file-dropzone.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onFiles? | `(files: File[]) => void` |  | Called with accepted files every time files are added. |
| onRemove? | `(file: File) => void` |  | Called with the file when someone removes it from the list. |
| upload? | `(file: File, onProgress: (p: number) => void) => Promise<void>` |  | Optional uploader. Call onProgress(0..1) as bytes go out; throw to fail. Without it, files are listed as done immediately. |
| accept? | `string` |  | Same syntax as <input accept>: MIME types, wildcards and extensions, e.g. "image/*,.pdf". |
| multiple? | `boolean` | `true` | Allow several files at once. When false, a new file replaces the previous one. |
| maxSize? | `number` |  | Largest accepted file, in bytes. Larger files are listed with an error. |
| maxFiles? | `number` |  | Most files the list will hold. Extra files are ignored. |
| disabled? | `boolean` |  |  |
| showList? | `boolean` | `true` | Show the file list under the zone. |
| label? | `string` | `"Drop files to upload"` | Main line inside the zone. |
| hint? | `string` |  | Secondary line. Defaults to the accepted types and max size. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<FileDropzone
  accept="image/*,.pdf"
  maxSize={10 * 1024 * 1024}
  upload={(file, onProgress) => uploadToS3(file, onProgress)}
  onFiles={(files) => console.log(files)}
/>
```

### FileList

A stack of file rows with name, metadata and an optional download action.

Use for attachments, exports and documents on a record. For one row use `FileRow`; for uploading use `FileDropzone`; for a folder hierarchy use `FileTree`.

- Name: `file-list` (component, Media)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/file-list` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`

- Uses: file-row

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| files? | `FileItem[]` | `SAMPLE_FILES` | Files to list. Defaults to a few Lumen documents. |
| onDownload? | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called with the file id. When present, each row shows a download button (the sample files show one regardless). |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<FileList
  files={[{ id: "f1", name: "INV-2041.pdf", meta: "PDF · 184 KB" }]}
  onDownload={(id) => download(id)}
/>
```

### FileTree

A code editor style file explorer with file icons, git status, a filter field and full tree keyboard support.

Use for repos, artifacts and agent workspaces. Folders are nodes with a `children` array (even empty); files have none. Paths passed to `onSelect` are names joined by "/". Keyboard follows the WAI-ARIA tree pattern. For a generic nested list without file semantics use `TreeView`; for a single file citation use `FileReference`.

- Name: `file-tree` (component, Dev tools)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/file-tree` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { FileTree } from "@/components/ui/file-tree"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/file-tree"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Related: tree-view, file-reference, file-list, json-viewer, media-library
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/file-tree (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/file-tree.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| data? | `FileTreeNode[]` | `SAMPLE` | Nested files and folders. Paths are built from names joined by "/". |
| defaultExpanded? | `string[]` | `["app", "app/dashboard", "components"]` | Folder paths open on first render. |
| selected? | `string` |  | Controlled selected path. |
| defaultSelected? | `string` | `"app/dashboard/page.tsx"` |  |
| activePath? | `string` |  | The file open in the editor. Defaults to the last selected file. |
| onSelect? | `(path: string) => void` |  | Called with the path of a file or folder when it is selected. |
| searchable? | `boolean` | `true` | Show the filter field above the tree. |
| showStatus? | `boolean` | `true` | Show git status letters and folder change dots. |
| sort? | `boolean` | `true` | Sort folders first, then names alphabetically. |
| title? | `string` | `"lumen-web"` | Header title, usually the project name. Pass an empty string to hide the header. |
| aria-label? | `string` |  |  |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<FileTree
  title="lumen-web"
  data={[{ name: "app", children: [{ name: "page.tsx", status: "M" }] }, { name: "package.json" }]}
  defaultExpanded={["app"]}
  onSelect={(path) => openFile(path)}
/>
```

### FilterBar

A toolbar strip with a filter text field, slots for filter controls and an optional Clear button.

Use above a list or table. Put `Select`, `ChipFilter` or `MultiSelect` controls in `children`. For a full table toolbar with bulk actions use `TableToolbar`; for audit logs use `AuditFilterBar`.

- Name: `filter-bar` (component, Tables)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/filter-bar` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { FilterBar } from "@/components/ui/filter-bar"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/filter-bar"`)
- Uses: button, search-input
- Related: select, chip-filter, multi-select, table-toolbar, audit-filter-bar, query-builder
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/filter-bar (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/filter-bar.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Filter controls rendered after the text field. |
| query? | `string` |  | Controlled filter text. Leave out for an uncontrolled field. |
| onQueryChange? | `(query: string) => void` |  | Called with the filter text on every keystroke and when cleared. |
| placeholder? | `string` | `"Filter…"` | Placeholder of the text field. |
| onClear? | `() => void` |  | When set, shows a "Clear" button at the end that calls it. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
const [q, setQ] = React.useState("")
<FilterBar query={q} onQueryChange={setQ} onClear={() => setQ("")}>
  <Select ... />
</FilterBar>
```

### FloatingActionButton

A round, fixed-position primary button in the bottom-right corner of the viewport.

Use for the one primary action of a mobile or canvas screen ("New invoice"). Takes every `Button` prop, and `aria-label` is required so an icon-only FAB always has a name. For an inline primary action use `Button`; for a sticky bottom action bar use `StickyBar`.

- Name: `floating-action-button` (component, Buttons)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/floating-action-button` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { FloatingActionButton } from "@/components/ui/floating-action-button"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/floating-action-button"`)
- Uses: button
- Related: button, sticky-bar
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/floating-action-button (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/floating-action-button.md)

Props (also accepts Button props):

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| aria-label | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<FloatingActionButton aria-label="New invoice" onClick={create}>
  <PlusIcon />
</FloatingActionButton>
```

### FloatingLabelInput

A text field whose label rests inside the input and floats onto the top border on focus or once filled.

Pass `label` for one field (input, or textarea with `multiline`). Without `label` it renders a small sign-up form built from `fields`. The label is a real <label>; `error` sets aria-invalid and is announced. For a classic label-above field use `Input` inside `FormField`; for passwords use `PasswordInput`; for formatted values use `MaskedInput`.

- Name: `floating-label-input` (component, Forms)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/floating-label-input` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { FloatingLabelInput } from "@/components/ui/floating-label-input"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/floating-label-input"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Uses: button
- Related: input, form-field, password-input, masked-input
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/floating-label-input (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/floating-label-input.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label? | `string` |  | The field label. When omitted, the `fields` form is rendered instead. |
| multiline? | `boolean` | `false` | Render a textarea instead of an input. |
| rows? | `number` | `4` | Textarea rows when `multiline`. |
| type? | `string` | `"text"` | Input type, e.g. "email", "tel", "url". Ignored when `multiline`. |
| value? | `string` |  | Controlled text. |
| defaultValue? | `string` | `""` | Initial text when uncontrolled. |
| onChange? | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called with the new text on every keystroke. |
| onBlur? | `() => void` |  | Called when the field loses focus, e.g. React Hook Form's `field.onBlur` to mark it touched. |
| icon? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon shown at the start of the field (inputs only). |
| hint? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the field, linked with aria-describedby. |
| error? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Error message. Marks the field invalid and replaces the hint. |
| disabled? | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| required? | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| id? | `string` |  |  |
| name? | `string` |  |  |
| autoComplete? | `string` |  |  |
| fields? | `FloatingLabelField[]` | `FIELDS` | Fields of the sample form rendered when no `label` is passed. |
| onSubmit? | `(values: Record<string, string>) => void` |  | Called with the form values when the sample form is submitted and valid. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
const [email, setEmail] = React.useState("")
<FloatingLabelInput label="Work email" type="email" value={email} onChange={setEmail} error={emailError} />
<FloatingLabelInput label="Notes" multiline rows={3} />
```

### FooterMega

A multi-column site footer: brand and tagline on the left, titled link columns across the rest.

Use at the bottom of marketing sites with many links. Each column is a labelled nav landmark. For a single row of links use `FooterNav`.

- Name: `footer-mega` (component, Landing pages)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/footer-mega` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { FooterMega } from "@/components/ui/footer-mega"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/footer-mega"`)
- Uses: link
- Related: footer-nav
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/footer-mega (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/footer-mega.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| columns? | `Col[]` | `SAMPLE_COLUMNS` | Link columns after the brand block. Defaults to three Lumen columns. |
| brand? | `string` | `"Lumen"` | Brand name shown in the first column. |
| tagline? | `string` | `"Invoicing and payments for teams tha...` | Short line under the brand name. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<FooterMega
  brand="Lumen"
  tagline="Invoicing for teams that close their books every day."
  columns={[{ title: "Product", links: [{ label: "Pricing", href: "/pricing" }] }]}
/>
```

### FooterNav

A one-line site footer: brand on the left, a row of quiet links on the right.

Use for app and docs footers with a handful of links (docs, status, privacy, terms). The links wrap onto a second line on narrow screens. `brand` is plain text and links have no `target`, so edit the file for a logo or new-tab links. For a marketing footer with titled link columns use `FooterMega`.

- Name: `footer-nav` (component, Navigation)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/footer-nav` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { FooterNav } from "@/components/ui/footer-nav"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/footer-nav"`)
- Uses: link
- Related: footer-mega
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/footer-nav (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/footer-nav.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| links? | `FooterLink[]` | `SAMPLE_LINKS` | Links in the footer nav. Defaults to a typical set for Lumen. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| brand? | `string` | `"Lumen"` | Brand name on the left. |

```tsx
<FooterNav brand="Lumen" links={[{ label: "Docs", href: "/docs" }, { label: "Status", href: "https://status.example.com" }]} />
```

### ForgotPasswordForm

An auth card asking for an email address to send a password reset link to.

A real <form>: Enter submits, the browser checks the email format, and `onSubmit` receives the trimmed address. For setting the new password use `ResetPasswordForm`; for passwordless sign-in use `MagicLinkForm`.

- Name: `forgot-password-form` (component, Auth)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/forgot-password-form` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ForgotPasswordForm } from "@/components/ui/forgot-password-form"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/forgot-password-form"`)
- Uses: auth-card, button, form-field, input
- Related: reset-password-form, magic-link-form
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/forgot-password-form (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/forgot-password-form.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onSubmit? | `(email: string) => void \| Promise<void>` |  | Called with the email address on submit. Return a promise to show a pending state until it settles; if it rejects, the form shows "Something went wrong. Try again." |
| title? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Forgot password"` | Card heading. |
| description? | `React.ReactNode` | `"We'll email you a link to reset it."` | Line under the heading. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ForgotPasswordForm onSubmit={async (email) => await sendResetLink(email)} />
```

### FormField

A label, a control, and a description or error message stacked with the right spacing and wiring.

Pass the control's `id` as `id`. When the child is a single element, FormField links it to the description or error with `aria-describedby` and sets `aria-invalid` while there is an error, so screen readers read the message. Use around `Input`, `Textarea`, `Select` and friends. For a label that floats inside the input use `FloatingLabelInput`.

- Name: `form-field` (component, Forms)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/form-field` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { FormField } from "@/components/ui/form-field"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/form-field"`)
- Uses: label
- Related: input, textarea, select, floating-label-input, auth-card, combobox, currency-input, date-picker
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/form-field (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/form-field.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id? | `string` |  | The control's id; the label points at it. |
| label? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Visible label. |
| description? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Help text under the control. Hidden while there is an error. |
| error? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Error message. Replaces the description and marks the control invalid. |
| required? | `boolean` |  | Adds a visual asterisk. Also set `required` on the control itself. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| children | `React.ReactNode` |  | The control, usually one element with the same `id`. |

```tsx
<FormField id="email" label="Work email" description="We send invoices here." error={errors.email} required>
  <Input id="email" type="email" required />
</FormField>
```

### FunnelChart

A funnel chart with stage bars laid out horizontally or vertically, conversion rates and drop-off between stages, an optional comparison series and bars that spring to new values when the data changes.

Use for signup and checkout funnels. Pass `stages` for one series, or `datasets` to add a segmented switch between them. Screen readers get a full data table. For a compact list of bars use `FunnelSteps`; for flows that branch use `SankeyChart`.

- Name: `funnel-chart` (component, Charts)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/funnel-chart` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { FunnelChart } from "@/components/ui/funnel-chart"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/funnel-chart"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Uses: segmented-control
- Related: funnel-steps, sankey-chart
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/funnel-chart (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/funnel-chart.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| stages? | `FunnelStage[]` |  | Stages from the top of the funnel down. |
| datasets? | `FunnelDataset[]` | `DATASETS` | Datasets to switch between with a segmented control. Ignored when `stages` is set. |
| orientation? | `"horizontal" \| "vertical" \| "auto"` | `"auto"` | "auto" is horizontal when the container is at least 480px wide, vertical below that. |
| title? | `string` | `"Visitors to paid"` | Chart title; also the figure's accessible name. |
| compareLabel? | `string` | `"Last month"` | Legend text for the comparison series. |
| format? | `(value: number) => string` | `defaultFormat` | Formats values in the bars and the table. |
| showCompare? | `boolean` | `true` | Draw the comparison outline when stages carry `compare`. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<FunnelChart
  title="Visitors to paid"
  stages={[
    { label: "Visitors", value: 48200, compare: 44100 },
    { label: "Signed up", value: 12840, compare: 11200 },
    { label: "Paid", value: 1464, compare: 1210 },
  ]}
/>
```

### FunnelSteps

A compact conversion funnel as stacked bars, each sized against the largest step.

Use in a card or sidebar for a quick funnel readout. For a full chart with step conversion rates, drop-off, a comparison period and dataset switching use `FunnelChart`; for arbitrary categories use `HorizontalBarChart`.

- Name: `funnel-steps` (component, Charts)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/funnel-steps` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { FunnelSteps } from "@/components/ui/funnel-steps"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/funnel-steps"`)
- Related: funnel-chart, horizontal-bar-chart
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/funnel-steps (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/funnel-steps.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| steps? | `Step[]` | `SAMPLE_STEPS` | Funnel stages, top to bottom. Defaults to a Lumen signup funnel. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<FunnelSteps steps={[{ label: "Visited", value: 12840 }, { label: "Signed up", value: 3210 }, { label: "Paid", value: 464 }]} />
```

### GanttChart

A project timeline with day and week scales, a today line, progress fills, dependency arrows, a sticky task column and focusable bars.

Use for launch plans and delivery schedules. Tasks take Date objects or ISO day strings; `end` is inclusive. Tasks with the same `group` share a heading and colour; `dependsOn` draws arrows. For a single plain bar row use `GanttRow`; for calendar events by the hour use `EventCalendar`; for request spans use `TraceWaterfall`.

- Name: `gantt-chart` (component, Charts)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/gantt-chart` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { GanttChart } from "@/components/ui/gantt-chart"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/gantt-chart"`)
- Uses: segmented-control
- Related: gantt-row, event-calendar, trace-waterfall
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/gantt-chart (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/gantt-chart.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tasks? | `GanttTask[]` |  | Tasks to plot. Defaults to a six week Lumen launch plan built around today. |
| scale? | `GanttScale` |  | Controlled zoom level. |
| defaultScale? | `GanttScale` | `"day"` | Initial zoom level when uncontrolled. |
| onScaleChange? | `(scale: GanttScale) => void` |  | Called when the Day/Week control changes the scale. |
| today? | `Date \| string` |  | The date the today line marks. Defaults to the current date. |
| padDays? | `number` | `2` | Empty days drawn before the first and after the last task. |
| title? | `string` | `"Launch plan"` | Heading above the chart. Empty hides the header row. |
| nameWidth? | `number` | `176` | Width of the sticky task column in px. |
| onTaskClick? | `(task: GanttTask) => void` |  | Called when a bar is clicked or activated with the keyboard. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<GanttChart
  title="Launch plan"
  tasks={[
    { id: "design", name: "Landing page design", start: "2026-11-02", end: "2026-11-09", progress: 60, group: "Design" },
    { id: "build", name: "Checkout flow", start: "2026-11-10", end: "2026-11-20", group: "Engineering", dependsOn: ["design"] },
  ]}
  onTaskClick={(task) => openTask(task.id)}
/>
```

### GanttRow

One labelled timeline row with a bar placed from `start` to `end` on a 0..max scale.

Use for a lightweight schedule built from a few rows (sprints, rollouts) where positions are plain numbers such as day indexes or percentages. For real dates, dependencies, scales and a today line use `GanttChart`; for nested spans of a trace use `TraceWaterfall`.

- Name: `gantt-row` (component, Workflow)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/gantt-row` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { GanttRow } from "@/components/ui/gantt-row"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/gantt-row"`)
- Related: gantt-chart, trace-waterfall
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/gantt-row (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/gantt-row.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `string` |  | Task name in the left column. |
| start | `number` |  | Bar start on the 0..max scale. |
| end | `number` |  | Bar end on the 0..max scale. |
| max? | `number` | `100` | Length of the whole scale. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<GanttRow label="Billing API" start={10} end={45} />
<GanttRow label="QA" start={20} end={26} max={30} />
```

### GaugeChart

A half-circle dial filled to a percentage of `max`, with the percentage inside and a caption below.

Use for one bounded score (health, quota, NPS-style index). For a full ring use `DonutChart`; for a goal ring with a target use `GoalRing`; for a linear labelled bar use `Meter`.

- Name: `gauge-chart` (component, Charts)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/gauge-chart` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { GaugeChart } from "@/components/ui/gauge-chart"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/gauge-chart"`)
- Related: donut-chart, goal-ring, meter
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/gauge-chart (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/gauge-chart.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | `number` |  | Current value, clamped to 0..max. |
| max? | `number` | `100` | Value that fills the dial. |
| label? | `string` | `"Gauge"` | Caption under the dial; also used in the accessible name. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<GaugeChart value={72} label="Uptime score" />
<GaugeChart value={41} max={50} label="Seats" />
```

### GoalRing

A circular progress ring for one goal, with the percentage in the centre and a caption below.

Use it for a single target read at a glance (weekly goal, quota met). For a linear bar use Progress, for a bounded measurement use Meter, and for several values in one ring use RadialChart.

- Name: `goal-ring` (component, Dashboard)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/goal-ring` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { GoalRing } from "@/components/ui/goal-ring"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/goal-ring"`)
- Related: progress, meter, radial-chart, gauge-chart, waffle-chart
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/goal-ring (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/goal-ring.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value? | `number` | `72` | Progress from 0 to 100. Values outside the range are clamped. |
| label? | `string` | `"Weekly goal"` | Caption under the ring; also the accessible name. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<GoalRing value={72} label="Weekly goal" />
```


### HeatmapCell

One square of a heatmap, tinted from sunken to accent by intensity.

Use it to build custom grids (activity by hour, usage by day): map your data into a CSS grid and pass each count normalised to 0..1 as `intensity`, with a `label` such as "Tue 14:00, 42 runs". For a ready year of daily cells use StreakCalendar; for a single ratio use DonutChart or Meter.

- Name: `heatmap-cell` (component, Charts)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/heatmap-cell` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { HeatmapCell } from "@/components/ui/heatmap-cell"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/heatmap-cell"`)
- Related: streak-calendar, donut-chart, meter
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/heatmap-cell (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/heatmap-cell.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| intensity? | `number` | `0` | Strength from 0 to 1; clamped. 0 is the sunken surface, 1 is full accent. |
| label? | `string` |  | Accessible name and tooltip, for example the date and count. Defaults to the intensity as a percentage. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<HeatmapCell intensity={0.6} label="Tue 14:00, 42 runs" />
```

### Hero

A centred marketing headline with an optional eyebrow, description and up to two calls to action.

Use it at the top of a landing or product page. For an in-app page title use PageHeader, for a mid-page section intro use SectionHeader, and for a closing call to action use CtaBanner.

- Name: `hero` (component, Landing pages)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/hero` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { Hero } from "@/components/ui/hero"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/hero"`)
- Uses: button
- Related: page-header, section-header, cta-banner, heading, hero-spotlight, cta-glow
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/hero (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/hero.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| eyebrow? | `string` |  | Short line above the title, for example a release or category. |
| title | `string` |  | The headline, rendered as the page's h1. |
| description? | `string` |  | One or two sentences under the headline. |
| primaryAction? | `HeroAction` |  | Solid ink button. |
| secondaryAction? | `HeroAction` |  | Outline button beside the primary one. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<Hero
  eyebrow="New in 2.4"
  title="Invoices that chase themselves"
  description="Reminders, retries and receipts on autopilot."
  primaryAction={{ label: "Start free", href: "/signup" }}
  secondaryAction={{ label: "Book a demo", onClick: openDemo }}
/>
```

### HorizontalBarChart

Labelled horizontal bars scaled to the largest value, for ranking categories at a glance.

Use it for top-N lists with long labels (customers, pages, endpoints). For values over time use BarChart or AreaChart, and for parts of a whole use StackedBarChart or DonutChart.

- Name: `horizontal-bar-chart` (component, Charts)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/horizontal-bar-chart` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { HorizontalBarChart } from "@/components/ui/horizontal-bar-chart"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/horizontal-bar-chart"`)
- Related: bar-chart, area-chart, stacked-bar-chart, donut-chart, funnel-steps
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/horizontal-bar-chart (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/horizontal-bar-chart.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| data? | `Bar[]` | `SAMPLE_DATA` | One bar per entry, in display order. Defaults to invoices per customer. |
| format? | `(value: number) => string` | `String` | Formats the value shown at the end of each bar. Defaults to the plain number. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| label? | `string` | `"Horizontal bar chart"` | Accessible name for the chart. |

```tsx
<HorizontalBarChart label="Invoices by customer" data={[{ label: "Northwind", value: 124 }, { label: "Globex", value: 52 }]} />
```

### HoverCard

A rich preview that opens when the pointer rests on, or focus lands in, its trigger.

Built on Base UI Preview Card: it waits before opening, stays open while the pointer moves onto the card, flips to stay on screen and closes on Escape. Use it for supplementary detail (a person, a record, a link). Anything the user must act on belongs in a Popover; a short text hint belongs in a Tooltip. The trigger should be a link or button so keyboard users can reach it.

- Name: `hover-card` (component, Overlays)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/hover-card` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { HoverCard } from "@/components/ui/hover-card"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/hover-card"`)
- Dependencies: @base-ui/react
- Related: card, popover, tooltip, link-preview
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/hover-card (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/hover-card.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| trigger | `React.ReactNode` |  | The element that opens the card, ideally a link or button. |
| children | `React.ReactNode` |  | Card content. |
| side? | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right"` | `"bottom"` | Which side of the trigger the card opens on. It flips if there is no room. |
| align? | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | `"start"` | Alignment along that side. |
| delay? | `number` | `400` | Milliseconds to wait before opening. |
| closeDelay? | `number` | `200` | Milliseconds to wait before closing once the pointer leaves. |
| open? | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state. |
| onOpenChange? | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the card opens or closes. |
| className? | `string` |  | Classes for the card panel. |

```tsx
<HoverCard trigger={<a href="/people/maya">Maya Chen</a>}>
  <p className="font-medium text-fg">Maya Chen</p>
  <p className="text-xs text-fg-muted">Finance lead</p>
</HoverCard>
```

### IconButton

A square Button that holds only an icon and requires an aria-label.

Use it for toolbar and row actions (close, more, delete). When the action needs a visible word, use Button with an icon and text instead; pair an IconButton with a Tooltip when the icon alone is not obvious.

- Name: `icon-button` (component, Buttons)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/icon-button` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { IconButton } from "@/components/ui/icon-button"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/icon-button"`)
- Dependencies: class-variance-authority
- Uses: button
- Related: button, tooltip
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/icon-button (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/icon-button.md)

Props (also accepts Button props):

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| aria-label | `string` |  | Required: the icon has no text, so this is the button's only name. |
| size? | `"icon-xs" \| "icon-sm" \| "icon" \| "icon-lg"` | `"icon"` | Square size: 28, 32, 36 (default) or 44px. |
| children | `React.ReactNode` |  | The icon, for example a lucide-react icon. Sized to the button automatically. |

```tsx
<IconButton aria-label="Delete invoice" variant="ghost" size="icon-sm"><TrashIcon /></IconButton>
```

### ImageCropper

Crop an image inside a frame: drag to pan, zoom with the slider, wheel or pinch, pick an aspect, mask to a circle and rotate in 90° steps.

Use it before uploading a cover, avatar or product photo. onCrop reports the crop in source pixels; getCroppedBlob(src, rect, opts) renders it to a Blob for upload. For picking a file without framing use ImageUpload, and for a round avatar picker use AvatarUpload. Keyboard: arrows pan (Shift for bigger steps), + and - zoom, R rotates, 0 resets.

- Name: `image-cropper` (component, Media)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/image-cropper` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ImageCropper } from "@/components/ui/image-cropper"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/image-cropper"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Uses: button, segmented-control, slider
- Related: image-upload, avatar-upload, file-dropzone
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/image-cropper (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/image-cropper.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| src? | `string` | `SAMPLE_SRC` | Image URL or data URI. Remote images need CORS headers for getCroppedBlob. |
| alt? | `string` | `"Lumen sample landscape"` |  |
| aspects? | `Aspect[]` | `["1:1", "4:3", "16:9"]` | Aspect presets offered, as "w:h". |
| defaultAspect? | `Aspect` | `"4:3"` |  |
| defaultCircle? | `boolean` | `false` | Start with the circular avatar mask on. |
| allowCircle? | `boolean` | `true` | Offer the circular mask toggle. |
| maxZoom? | `number` | `4` | Largest zoom, as a multiple of the size that just covers the frame. |
| showPreview? | `boolean` | `true` | Show the live preview and crop details beside the frame. |
| onCrop? | `(rect: CropRect, info: { aspect: Aspect; circle: boolean }) => void` |  | Called with the crop in source pixels once an interaction settles. |
| fileName? | `string` | `"lumen-cover.png"` | File name used by the export button. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
const [rect, setRect] = React.useState<CropRect | null>(null)
<ImageCropper src={url} aspects={["1:1", "16:9"]} onCrop={(r) => setRect(r)} />
const blob = await getCroppedBlob(url, rect!, { type: "image/webp", width: 1200 })
```

### ImageGallery

A square-tile image grid, two columns on phones and three from the small breakpoint up.

Use it for a static set of photos or screenshots. For mixed heights use MasonryGrid, for a swipeable row use Carousel, and to let visitors open a tile larger render each image as an ImageLightbox in your own grid.

- Name: `image-gallery` (component, Media)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/image-gallery` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ImageGallery } from "@/components/ui/image-gallery"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/image-gallery"`)
- Uses: aspect-ratio
- Related: masonry-grid, carousel, image-lightbox
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/image-gallery (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/image-gallery.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| images? | `GalleryImage[]` | `SAMPLE_IMAGES` | Images to tile, each with alt text. Defaults to six illustrated landscapes. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ImageGallery images={[{ src: "/a.jpg", alt: "Front of the store" }, { src: "/b.jpg", alt: "Checkout counter" }]} />
```

### ImageLightbox

A thumbnail that opens the full image in a modal viewer.

Built on Base UI Dialog: focus moves into the viewer and returns to the thumbnail on close, Escape and a click on the backdrop close it, and the page behind does not scroll. Use it to enlarge one image; for a grid of tiles use ImageGallery, and for paging through many images use Carousel.

- Name: `image-lightbox` (component, Media)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/image-lightbox` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ImageLightbox } from "@/components/ui/image-lightbox"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/image-lightbox"`)
- Dependencies: @base-ui/react, lucide-react
- Uses: button
- Related: dialog, image-gallery, carousel
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/image-lightbox (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/image-lightbox.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| src? | `string` | `SAMPLE_IMAGE` | Image URL or data URI, used for both the thumbnail and the full view. |
| alt? | `string` | `"Preview"` | Describes the image; also names the viewer for screen readers. |
| open? | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state. |
| onOpenChange? | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the viewer opens or closes. |
| className? | `string` |  | Classes for the thumbnail wrapper. |

```tsx
<ImageLightbox src="/receipt.png" alt="Scanned receipt for INV-2041" />
```

### ImageUpload

A single-image picker: a drop zone that turns into a preview with a remove button.

Use it for one cover, logo or photo. For a round profile picture use AvatarUpload, for several files of any type use FileDropzone, and to let the user frame the picture before saving use ImageCropper.

The preview uses an object URL that the component revokes when the image is replaced, removed or unmounted; upload the File from onChange, not the URL.

- Name: `image-upload` (component, Forms)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/image-upload` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ImageUpload } from "@/components/ui/image-upload"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/image-upload"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Uses: file-dropzone
- Related: avatar-upload, file-dropzone, image-cropper, signature-pad
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/image-upload (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/image-upload.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value? | `string \| null` |  | Current image URL (controlled). Pass null to show the drop zone. |
| onChange? | `(url: string \| null, file?: File \| null) => void` |  | Called with a local preview URL and the File when an image is chosen, and with (null, null) when it is removed. |
| maxSize? | `number` | `5 * MB` | Largest accepted file in bytes. Defaults to 5 MB. |
| alt? | `string` | `"Upload preview"` | Alt text for the preview image. |
| disabled? | `boolean` |  |  |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ImageUpload value={coverUrl} onChange={(url, file) => { setCoverUrl(url); if (file) upload(file) }} />
```

### ImpersonationBanner

A full-width strip that tells a support agent whose account they are viewing, with an Exit button.

Mount it at the very top of the app shell while impersonating. For system incidents use IncidentBanner, for trials use TrialBanner, and for general announcements use AnnouncementBar.

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| user | `string` |  | Name or email of the account being viewed. |
| onExit? | `() => void` |  | Called when the Exit button is pressed; end the impersonation session here. |
| exitLabel? | `string` | `"Exit"` | Text of the exit button. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ImpersonationBanner user="maya@northwind.com" onExit={stopImpersonating} />
```

### IncidentBanner

A full-width strip announcing an ongoing incident, its severity, and a link to the status page.

Use it at the top of an app or dashboard during an outage. For a dismissible product announcement use AnnouncementBar, for a message inside a page use InlineAlert or Callout, and for a service's current state use HealthIndicator.

- Name: `incident-banner` (component, Feedback)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/incident-banner` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { IncidentBanner } from "@/components/ui/incident-banner"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/incident-banner"`)
- Uses: status-dot
- Related: announcement-bar, inline-alert, callout, health-indicator, impersonation-banner, uptime-bar, status-page, status-marketing
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/incident-banner (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/incident-banner.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title? | `string` | `"Elevated API errors in us-east"` | One line describing the incident. |
| severity? | `IncidentSeverity` | `"major"` | Sets the dot colour: minor is accent, major is warning, critical is danger. |
| href? | `string` | `"#"` | Status page URL; the link is hidden when empty. |
| linkLabel? | `string` | `"Status page"` | Text of the status page link. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<IncidentBanner severity="critical" title="Payments are failing in eu-west" href="https://status.example.com" />
```

### InfiniteScroll

A scrolling list that loads the next page when a sentinel near the end comes into view.

It uses IntersectionObserver, never fires twice for the same page, shows a loading row and an end-of-list message, keeps a real "Load more" button as the accessible fallback, and offers Retry when a page fails. Use it for feeds of unknown length. For thousands of rows already in memory use VirtualList, and for numbered pages use Pagination.

- Name: `infinite-scroll` (component, Tables)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/infinite-scroll` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { InfiniteScroll } from "@/components/ui/infinite-scroll"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/infinite-scroll"`)
- Uses: button, spinner
- Related: virtual-list, pagination, virtualized-list
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/infinite-scroll (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/infinite-scroll.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| loadMore? | `(page: number) => Promise<{ items: T[]; hasMore: boolean }>` |  | Fetch a page (0-based); return its items and whether more remain. Throw to show Retry. |
| renderItem? | `(item: T, index: number) => React.ReactNode` |  | Renders one item. Each is wrapped in an li. |
| rootMargin? | `string` | `"240px"` | How far before the end to start loading, as a CSS margin. |
| label? | `string` | `"Results"` | Accessible name for the focusable scroll box and the list inside it. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<InfiniteScroll
  loadMore={async (page) => {
    const res = await fetch(`/api/orders?page=${page}`).then((r) => r.json())
    return { items: res.orders, hasMore: res.hasMore }
  }}
  renderItem={(order) => <OrderRow order={order} />}
/>
```

### InlineAlert

A bordered message inside the page flow, with a tone icon, an optional title and body text.

Use it next to the thing it is about (a form, a settings section). For a tinted aside in prose use Callout, for a page-wide strip use Banner or AnnouncementBar, and for a transient confirmation use Toast.

Danger and warning alerts use role="alert" so screen readers announce them when they appear; neutral and success use role="status", which is polite.

- Name: `inline-alert` (component, Feedback)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/inline-alert` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { InlineAlert } from "@/components/ui/inline-alert"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/inline-alert"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Related: callout, banner, announcement-bar, toast, error-state, incident-banner, well
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/inline-alert (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/inline-alert.md)

Props (also accepts <div>):

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Bold first line. |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Body text or inline content. |
| tone? | `InlineAlertTone` | `"neutral"` | Sets the icon, the icon colour and the border colour. |

```tsx
<InlineAlert tone="warning" title="Action needed">Add a payment method to keep access.</InlineAlert>
```

### InlineCellEdit

A table cell value that turns into a text field on click; Enter or blur saves, Escape cancels.

Use it for quick edits inside DataTable or Table rows. For a heading edited in place use EditableHeading, and for multi-field edits open a Dialog or Sheet with a form.

- Name: `inline-cell-edit` (component, Tables)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/inline-cell-edit` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { InlineCellEdit } from "@/components/ui/inline-cell-edit"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/inline-cell-edit"`)
- Uses: input
- Related: data-table, table, editable-heading, dialog, sheet, data-grid
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/inline-cell-edit (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/inline-cell-edit.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | `string` |  | The saved value shown when not editing. |
| onChange? | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called with the new text when the edit is committed (Enter or blur), only if it changed. |
| label? | `string` | `"Edit cell"` | Accessible name for the button and the field, for example the column name. |
| placeholder? | `string` | `"Edit"` | Shown when the value is empty. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<InlineCellEdit value={row.name} label="Customer name" onChange={(name) => save(row.id, { name })} />
```

### InlineCodeDiff

One removed line above one added line, for showing a small code or config change.

Use it in reviews, changelogs and agent tool results to show a single edit. For a whole file or several hunks use DiffView.

```tsx
<InlineCodeDiff before='timeout: 30' after='timeout: 60' />
```

### InputAffix

A text Input with icons or text fixed inside the field before or after the value.

Use it for a search icon, a currency sign, a unit, a domain suffix or a trailing button. For money with formatting use CurrencyInput, for a search field with clear and results use SearchInput, and for a plain field use Input. All Input props (value, onChange, size, aria-invalid…) pass to the inner input.

- Name: `input-affix` (component, Forms)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/input-affix` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { InputAffix } from "@/components/ui/input-affix"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/input-affix"`)
- Uses: input
- Related: input, currency-input, search-input
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/input-affix (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/input-affix.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| leading? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Content before the value: an icon or short text such as "$" or "https://". |
| trailing? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Content after the value: an icon, a unit, a suffix or a small button. |
| containerClassName? | `string` |  | Classes for the outer field box; className goes to the inner input. |

```tsx
<InputAffix leading={<SearchIcon />} placeholder="Search invoices" aria-label="Search invoices" />
<InputAffix trailing=".minidev.pro" defaultValue="acme" aria-label="Subdomain" />
```

### Input

A single-line text field on Base UI Input, with hover, focus halo, invalid, disabled and read-only states.

Use it for any short text, email, number or password value; give it a Label (or wrap it in FormField) or an aria-label. For icons or units inside the field use InputAffix, for multi-line text use Textarea, and for specialised values use PasswordInput, SearchInput, NumberInput, CurrencyInput or OtpInput. Mark errors with aria-invalid so the border turns danger.

- Name: `input` (component, Forms)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/input` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { Input } from "@/components/ui/input"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/input"`)
- Dependencies: @base-ui/react, class-variance-authority
- Related: label, form-field, input-affix, textarea, password-input, search-input, number-input, currency-input
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/input (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/input.md)

Props: <input>.

```tsx
<Label htmlFor="email">Email</Label>
<Input id="email" type="email" placeholder="you@company.com" aria-invalid={!!error} />
```

### Inset

A sunken, bordered well that sets content below the surrounding surface.

Use it inside a card or panel to hold secondary content (a code sample, an embedded preview, read-only details). For a raised container use Card, and for a padded note block with body text styles use Well.

- Name: `inset` (component, Layout)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/inset` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { Inset } from "@/components/ui/inset"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/inset"`)
- Related: card, well
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/inset (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/inset.md)

```tsx
<Inset><p className="text-sm text-fg-muted">No payouts yet.</p></Inset>
```

### IntegrationCard

A third-party integration with its name, a one-line description, a Connected or Available badge and a Connect or Manage button.

Use it in an integrations or app directory grid. For an account the user has already linked (with its identity and a disconnect action) use ConnectedAccount, and for single sign-on providers use SsoProviderCard.

- Name: `integration-card` (component, Settings)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/integration-card` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { IntegrationCard } from "@/components/ui/integration-card"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/integration-card"`)
- Uses: badge, button
- Related: connected-account, sso-provider-card, webhook-list
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/integration-card (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/integration-card.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name? | `string` | `"Linear"` | Integration name, also used to name the action button for screen readers. |
| description? | `string` | `"Sync issues into the engineering gal...` | One line about what the integration does. |
| icon? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Logo or icon shown before the name. |
| connected? | `boolean` | `false` | Connected shows "Manage"; otherwise "Connect". |
| onConnect? | `() => void` |  | Called by the Connect button. |
| onManage? | `() => void` |  | Called by the Manage button. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<IntegrationCard name="Slack" description="Post invoice events to a channel." icon={<SlackLogo />} connected onManage={openSettings} />
```

### InteractiveAreaChart

An area chart you scrub with the pointer or arrow keys; a crosshair pins the value and its change against a comparison line.

Use it for one headline series over time with an optional "last period" line (revenue, signups). For a static area use AreaChart, for several lines use LineChart, and for a tiny inline trend use StatSparkline. Keyboard: Left and Right step through points, Home and End jump to the ends.

- Name: `interactive-area-chart` (component, Charts)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/interactive-area-chart` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { InteractiveAreaChart } from "@/components/ui/interactive-area-chart"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/interactive-area-chart"`)
- Uses: area-chart
- Related: area-chart, line-chart, stat-sparkline, scatter-chart
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/interactive-area-chart (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/interactive-area-chart.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| data? | `Point[]` | `SAMPLE` | Points in order, left to right. Defaults to twelve months of revenue. |
| format? | `(n: number) => string` | `(n: number) => `$${n.toLocaleString()}k`` | Formats values in the header and for screen readers. |
| label? | `string` | `"Revenue"` | Series name, shown in the header and legend and used as the accessible name. |
| compareLabel? | `string` | `"Last year"` | Name of the comparison series. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<InteractiveAreaChart
  label="Revenue"
  compareLabel="Last year"
  format={(n) => `$${n}k`}
  data={[{ label: "Jan", value: 42, compare: 38 }, { label: "Feb", value: 47, compare: 40 }]}
/>
```

### InviteMembers

A card with an email field that sends workspace invites and lists the ones still pending.

Use it in team settings or onboarding. For managing existing members and seats use SeatManager or TeamMemberRow, for CSV uploads use BulkUserImport, and for the invitee's side use JoinWorkspace.

Works uncontrolled out of the box; pass `pending` and handle `onInvite` to keep the list in your own state.

- Name: `invite-members` (component, Settings)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/invite-members` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { InviteMembers } from "@/components/ui/invite-members"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/invite-members"`)
- Uses: badge, button, input
- Related: seat-manager, team-member-row, bulk-user-import, join-workspace
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/invite-members (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/invite-members.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title? | `string` | `"Invite members"` | Card title. |
| description? | `string` | `"They get free UI access. Premium unl...` | One line under the title. |
| pending? | `string[]` |  | Pending invite emails (controlled). |
| defaultPending? | `string[]` | `["sam@acme.co", "lee@north.io"]` | Initial pending emails when uncontrolled. |
| onInvite? | `(email: string) => void` |  | Called with a valid, new email when the form is submitted. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<InviteMembers pending={invites} onInvite={(email) => api.invite(email)} />
```

### InvoiceDetail

One invoice as a card: number, dates and status on top, line items below, total at the foot.

Use it on an invoice page or in a side panel. For many invoices use InvoiceList, for a payment confirmation use Receipt, and for a cart before payment use OrderSummary or CheckoutSummary. Amounts are preformatted strings so you control currency and locale.

- Name: `invoice-detail` (component, Billing)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/invoice-detail` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { InvoiceDetail } from "@/components/ui/invoice-detail"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/invoice-detail"`)
- Uses: status-badge
- Related: invoice-list, receipt, order-summary, checkout-summary
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/invoice-detail (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/invoice-detail.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id? | `string` | `"INV-2041"` | Invoice number. |
| date? | `string` | `"Issued Sep 24, 2026 · Due Oct 8, 2026"` | Issue date, already formatted. |
| amount? | `string` | `"$12,400.00"` | Invoice total, already formatted. |
| status? | `InvoiceStatus` | `"open"` | paid is success, open is warning, void is neutral. |
| lines? | `InvoiceLine[]` | `SAMPLE_LINES` | Line items. Defaults to a Northwind invoice from Lumen. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<InvoiceDetail id="INV-2041" status="paid" amount="$1,246.00" lines={[{ label: "Growth plan", amount: "$1,246.00" }]} />
```

### IpAllowlist

An editable list of IP addresses and CIDR ranges allowed to reach an account or API key.

Type an IPv4 or IPv6 address, optionally with a /prefix, and press Enter or Add; bad and duplicate entries are rejected with a message. Use it in security settings. For free-form tags use TagsInput; for API keys use ApiKeyList. Always validate again on the server.

- Name: `ip-allowlist` (component, Settings)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/ip-allowlist` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { IpAllowlist } from "@/components/ui/ip-allowlist"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/ip-allowlist"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Uses: button, icon-button, input
- Related: tags-input, api-key-list, admin-console
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/ip-allowlist (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/ip-allowlist.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value? | `string[]` |  | Allowed entries (controlled). |
| defaultValue? | `string[]` | `["203.0.113.10"]` | Initial entries when uncontrolled. |
| onChange? | `(ips: string[]) => void` |  | Called with the full list after an add or remove. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<IpAllowlist value={ips} onChange={setIps} />
```

### JsonViewer

A collapsible JSON tree with syntax colours, item counts, copy value and copy path, search highlighting and full keyboard navigation.

Use it for API responses, webhook payloads, tool-call results and debug panels. For JSON as plain highlighted text use CodeBlock, for tabular results use SqlResultTable, and for a file hierarchy use FileTree. Keyboard: arrows walk and fold the tree, Home and End jump, Enter toggles, C copies the focused value and P copies its path.

- Name: `json-viewer` (component, Dev tools)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/json-viewer` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { JsonViewer } from "@/components/ui/json-viewer"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/json-viewer"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Related: code-block, sql-result-table, file-tree, tool-result-panel
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/json-viewer (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/json-viewer.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value? | `unknown` | `SAMPLE` | Any JSON serialisable value. Defaults to a Lumen invoice API response. |
| title? | `string` | `"GET /v1/invoices/inv_8f3a2c"` | Label shown in the header, for example the request that produced the data. Pass an empty string to hide the header. |
| rootName? | `string` | `""` | Key shown on the root row. Empty hides it. |
| defaultExpandDepth? | `number` | `1` | Containers at or above this depth start open. The root is depth 0. |
| defaultExpanded? | `string[]` | `["$.customer", "$.lines", "$.lines[0]"]` | Extra container paths that start open, in `$.a.b[0]` form. |
| toolbar? | `boolean` | `true` | Show the search field and expand or collapse all buttons. |
| maxStringLength? | `number` | `64` | Longest string shown inline before it is cut with an ellipsis. |
| onCopy? | `(text: string, kind: "value" \| "path", path: string) => void` |  | Called after a value or path is copied. |
| aria-label? | `string` |  |  |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<JsonViewer value={response} title="GET /v1/invoices/inv_8f3a2c" defaultExpandDepth={1} />
```

Columns of cards in a horizontally scrolling board, each column headed by its title and card count.

Use it to show work by stage from plain data. It is read-only; to compose your own columns with custom cards use KanbanColumn and IssueCard, and for reordering within one list use SortableList.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| columns? | `KanbanColumn[]` | `SAMPLE_COLUMNS` | Columns left to right, each with its cards. Defaults to a Lumen engineering board. |
| aria-label? | `string` |  | Accessible name for the focusable, scrolling board. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<KanbanBoard columns={[{ id: "todo", title: "To do", cards: [{ id: "1", title: "Export payouts", meta: "LUM-418" }] }]} />
```

### KanbanColumn

One titled column of a board with an optional count badge; you supply the cards as children.

Use it to compose a custom board with your own cards (often IssueCard). For a board rendered from data in one call use KanbanBoard.

| className? | `string` |  |  |

### Kbd

A physical keycap for a key name or symbol: surface, hairline and a 1px key edge.

Use it inline in text, menus and tooltips to show a shortcut; group a combo with KbdGroup. For a searchable list of every shortcut use KeyboardShortcuts or ShortcutCheatSheet.

- Name: `kbd` (component, Dev tools)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/kbd` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { Kbd, KbdGroup } from "@/components/ui/kbd"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/kbd"`)
- Related: keyboard-shortcuts, shortcut-cheat-sheet, badge
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/kbd (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/kbd.md)

Props: <kbd>.

```tsx
<KbdGroup><Kbd>⌘</Kbd><Kbd>K</Kbd></KbdGroup>
```

### KeyboardShortcuts

A searchable shortcuts cheat sheet in a dialog, opened with the ? key or a trigger button, showing the right modifier glyphs for the viewer's platform.

Shortcuts are grouped, filtered as you type, and written once with portable names (mod, shift, alt, enter) that render as ⌘ ⇧ ⌥ ↵ on a Mac and Ctrl, Shift, Alt, Enter elsewhere; screen readers hear the key names. The platform is read after mount, so server and client markup match. For a static, always-visible list use ShortcutCheatSheet; for one key inline use Kbd.

- Name: `keyboard-shortcuts` (component, Overlays)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/keyboard-shortcuts` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { KeyboardShortcuts } from "@/components/ui/keyboard-shortcuts"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/keyboard-shortcuts"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Uses: button, dialog, input, kbd
- Related: shortcut-cheat-sheet, kbd
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/keyboard-shortcuts (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| groups? | `KeyboardShortcutGroup[]` | `SAMPLE_GROUPS` | Shortcut groups, shown as titled columns. Defaults to a sample invoicing app. |
| title? | `string` | `"Keyboard shortcuts"` | Dialog title. |
| hotkey? | `string` | `"?"` | Key that opens the sheet from anywhere on the page, outside text fields. Empty disables it. |
| open? | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state. Leave undefined for internal state. |
| onOpenChange? | `(open: boolean) => void` |  |  |
| showTrigger? | `boolean` | `true` | Render the built-in trigger button. |
| triggerLabel? | `string` | `"Keyboard shortcuts"` | Text of the built-in trigger button. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<KeyboardShortcuts
  groups={[{ title: "Invoices", shortcuts: [{ keys: ["mod", "enter"], label: "Send invoice" }, { keys: ["N"], label: "New invoice" }] }]}
/>
```

Use it at the top of a dashboard for three to six metrics. For one metric with more detail use StatCard, for a metric with a trend line use StatSparkline, and for a slim inline band use StatsStrip.

### Label

The caption for a form control; point htmlFor at the control's id so clicking it focuses the field.

Use it beside Input, Textarea, Checkbox, Switch and friends. It dims when a native `peer` control before it is `:disabled` or a `group` ancestor has data-disabled="true"; Base UI controls (Checkbox, Switch, Radio) render a span, so use the `group` wrapper for those. For a label with description and error text wired up for you use FormField.

- Name: `label` (component, Forms)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/label` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { Label } from "@/components/ui/label"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/label"`)
- Related: input, textarea, checkbox, switch, form-field, combobox, currency-input, date-picker
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/label (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/label.md)

Props: <label>.

```tsx
<Label htmlFor="email">Email</Label>
<Input id="email" type="email" />
```

### LanguagePicker

A grid of language choices where exactly one is selected, each written in its own language.

Works as a radio group: Tab enters at the selected language, arrow keys move and select, Home and End jump to the ends. Use it in settings or onboarding for a handful of languages. For long lists use Select or Combobox; for regions use RegionPicker.

- Name: `language-picker` (component, Settings)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/language-picker` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { LanguagePicker } from "@/components/ui/language-picker"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/language-picker"`)
- Related: select, combobox, region-picker, timezone-select
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/language-picker (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/language-picker.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value? | `string` |  | Selected language id (controlled). |
| defaultValue? | `string` | `"en"` | Initial language id when uncontrolled. |
| onChange? | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called with the chosen language id. |
| options? | `LanguageOption[]` | `LANGS` | Languages to offer. Defaults to English, Spanish, German and Japanese. |
| label? | `string` | `"Language"` | Accessible name for the group. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<LanguagePicker value={lang} onChange={setLang} options={[{ id: "en", label: "English" }, { id: "fr", label: "Français" }]} />
```

### LatencyBadge

A small monospace badge for a response time, coloured fast, slow or very slow.

Under `fast` ms is success, under `slow` ms is warning, anything above is danger. Use it in endpoint lists, traces and status tables. For a trend over time use StatSparkline, and for a waterfall of spans use TraceWaterfall.

- Name: `latency-badge` (component, Dev tools)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/latency-badge` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { LatencyBadge } from "@/components/ui/latency-badge"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/latency-badge"`)
- Related: stat-sparkline, trace-waterfall
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/latency-badge (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/latency-badge.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ms | `number` |  | Response time in milliseconds. |
| thresholds? | `{ fast: number; slow: number }` | `{ fast: 100, slow: 400 }` | Upper bounds in ms for the success and warning colours. Defaults to 100 and 400. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<LatencyBadge ms={182} />
<LatencyBadge ms={950} thresholds={{ fast: 300, slow: 1000 }} />
```

### LightProvider

The page's single light source: it follows the pointer, drifts when idle, and every shadow and sheen in the kit falls away from it.

Optional: without it shadows fall from a fixed light. Render it once near the root (it renders nothing and only touches `document` in an effect, so it is SSR safe). Pick a material with MaterialSwitcher or by setting data-material on <html> or any subtree.

- Name: `light-provider` (component, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/light-provider` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { LightProvider, MaterialSwitcher, MATERIALS } from "@/components/ui/light-provider"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/light-provider"`)
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/light-provider (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/light-provider.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| idle? | `boolean` | `true` | Drift when the pointer is idle or absent. |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Rendered as-is. Without children the root provider renders nothing visible. |

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
<body>
  <LightProvider />
  {children}
</body>
```

### LineChart

Several smooth series on a hairline grid, each in a chart colour with a dot at its latest value.

Use it to compare a few series over the same periods (MRR, expansion, churn). For one series with scrubbing use InteractiveAreaChart, for a filled single series use AreaChart, and for a tiny trend use StatSparkline. Add a ChartLegend to name the series visually; `seriesLabels` names them for screen readers.

- Name: `line-chart` (component, Charts)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/line-chart` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { LineChart } from "@/components/ui/line-chart"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/line-chart"`)
- Uses: area-chart
- Related: interactive-area-chart, area-chart, stat-sparkline, chart-legend, chart-card, scatter-chart
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/line-chart (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/line-chart.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| series? | `number[][]` | `SAMPLE_SERIES` | One array of values per series; all series share the x axis. |
| seriesLabels? | `string[]` |  | Name of each series, in the same order; added to the accessible description with each series' latest value. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| label? | `string` | `"Line chart"` | Accessible name for the chart. |
| grid? | `boolean` | `true` | Draw the dashed horizontal grid. |

```tsx
<LineChart label="MRR by month" seriesLabels={["Total", "Expansion"]} series={[[12, 14, 17, 19], [4, 5, 6, 8]]} />
```
