### Progress

A thin determinate progress bar built on Base UI, with optional label and value text.

Use it for uploads, onboarding steps and long tasks with a known end. Pass `value={null}` for an indeterminate bar. For a compact ring use ProgressCircle; for usage against a limit use QuotaBar. Children render above the track, so put ProgressLabel and ProgressValue inside.

- Name: `progress` (component, Feedback)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/progress` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { Progress, ProgressTrack, ProgressIndicator, ProgressLabel, ProgressValue } from "@/components/ui/progress"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/progress"`)
- Dependencies: @base-ui/react
- Related: progress-circle, quota-bar, account-setup-progress, coverage-meter, donut-chart, goal-ring, meter, spinner
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/progress (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/progress.md)

Props: ProgressPrimitive.Root props.

```tsx
<Progress value={42}>
  <ProgressLabel>Uploading</ProgressLabel>
  <ProgressValue />
</Progress>
```

### PromptInputAttachments

A PromptInput with an attach row above it for file uploads.

Use it when attachments are a first-class part of the prompt and deserve their own row. Otherwise pass `onAttach` to PromptInput and use its built-in paperclip. Takes every PromptInput prop; `onAttach` goes to the top button only, so the inner PromptInput shows no paperclip.

- Name: `prompt-input-attachments` (component, AI chat)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/prompt-input-attachments` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { PromptInputWithAttachments, PromptInputAttachments } from "@/components/ui/prompt-input-attachments"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/prompt-input-attachments"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Uses: button, prompt-input
- Related: prompt-input, attachment-chip
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/prompt-input-attachments (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/prompt-input-attachments.md)

```tsx
<PromptInputWithAttachments value={prompt} onChange={setPrompt} onSubmit={send} onAttach={() => fileInput.current?.click()} hint="PDF or CSV, up to 10 MB" />
```

### PromptInput

The AI chat composer: grows with content, sends on Enter, Shift+Enter for a newline.

The whole shell takes the focus halo.

Use it at the bottom of any AI chat. Controlled (`value` + `onChange`) or uncontrolled (`defaultValue`); either way `onSubmit` receives the current text. Enter while an IME is composing does not send. The paperclip only shows when you pass `onAttach`. For a plain multi-line field use Textarea.

- Name: `prompt-input` (component, AI chat)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/prompt-input` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { PromptInput } from "@/components/ui/prompt-input"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/prompt-input"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Related: textarea, ai-composer, chat-thread, comment-composer, context-chip, context-pill, markdown-editor, prompt-input-attachments
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/prompt-input (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/prompt-input.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value? | `string` |  | Controlled text. |
| defaultValue? | `string` |  | Starting text when uncontrolled. |
| onChange? | `(v: string) => void` |  | Fires with the new text on every keystroke. |
| onSubmit? | `(value: string) => void` |  | Fires with the text on Enter or the Send button, only when it is not blank. |
| onAttach? | `() => void` |  | Shows a paperclip button that calls this; open your file picker here. Without it there is no attach button. |
| disabled? | `boolean` |  |  |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| placeholder? | `string` | `"Message…"` |  |
| toolbar? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Optional left-side toolbar content (model picker, chips…). |
| aria-label? | `string` |  | Accessible name of the text area. |

```tsx
const [prompt, setPrompt] = React.useState("")
<PromptInput value={prompt} onChange={setPrompt} onSubmit={(text) => { send(text); setPrompt("") }} />
```

### PromptLibrary

A searchable list of saved prompts, each a card with a title, tag and two-line preview.

Use it in an AI app's sidebar or a "/" picker so people can reuse prompts. Search filters by title, body and tag as you type; clicking a card calls `onSelect`. For command style search across actions use a command palette instead.

- Name: `prompt-library` (component, AI chat)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/prompt-library` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { PromptLibrary } from "@/components/ui/prompt-library"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/prompt-library"`)
- Uses: search-input
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/prompt-library (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/prompt-library.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| prompts? | `Prompt[]` | `SAMPLE_PROMPTS` | Saved prompts to list and search. |
| onSelect? | `(p: Prompt) => void` |  | Fires with the prompt whose card was clicked. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<PromptLibrary prompts={[{ id: "sum", title: "Summarize thread", body: "Summarize this thread in five bullets.", tag: "Writing" }]} onSelect={(p) => setPrompt(p.body)} />
```

### Prose

Wrap rendered markdown or plain HTML elements in it and they get the kit's headings, spacing, links, lists, code and quotes. For single headings or paragraphs in app UI use Heading and Text.

```tsx
<Prose>
  <h2>Install</h2>
  <p>Add components with <code>npx shadcn add</code>.</p>
</Prose>
```

### PublishBar

A status badge, a save note and Preview / Publish buttons for a CMS or editor.

Use it pinned above or below an editor to show draft, scheduled or published state. For a floating unsaved-changes prompt use a toast or a save bar instead.

- Name: `publish-bar` (component, Workflow)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/publish-bar` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { PublishBar } from "@/components/ui/publish-bar"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/publish-bar"`)
- Uses: button, status-badge
- Related: sticky-cta-bar
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/publish-bar (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/publish-bar.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| status? | `PublishStatus` | `"draft"` | Current state, shown as a badge. |
| note? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Changes save automatically"` | Muted line next to the badge. |
| onPublish? | `() => void` |  | Fires when Publish is pressed. |
| onPreview? | `() => void` |  | Fires when Preview is pressed. |
| publishing? | `boolean` | `false` | True while publishing: the button is disabled and reads "Publishing…". |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<PublishBar status="draft" onPreview={openPreview} onPublish={publish} publishing={isPending} />
```

### QrCode

A QR code that needs no library. The encoder is in this file: byte mode, versions 1 to 40, all four error correction levels, Reed-Solomon codewords and spec penalty masking. Modules draw as one SVG path in `currentColor`, so the code follows your tokens; a logo can sit in a cleared well at level H; and Download SVG writes a standalone file.

- Name: `qr-code` (component, Media)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/qr-code` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { QrCode } from "@/components/ui/qr-code"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/qr-code"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Uses: button
- Related: two-factor-setup
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/qr-code (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/qr-code.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value? | `string` | `"https://ui.minidev.pro"` | Text to encode, as UTF-8 bytes. URLs, Wi-Fi strings, payment payloads, anything. |
| size? | `number` | `200` | Rendered width and height in px. The SVG scales without blur. |
| level? | `QrLevel` | `"M"` | Error correction level. L 7%, M 15%, Q 25%, H 30% of codewords recoverable. The logo well needs H. |
| fg? | `string` | `"currentColor"` | Module colour. Any CSS colour; defaults to the current text colour so it follows your tokens. |
| bg? | `string` | `"transparent"` | Background colour behind the modules and quiet zone. |
| margin? | `number` | `2` | Quiet zone in modules on each side. The spec asks for 4; 2 is fine on a plain surface. |
| logoScale? | `number` | `0.24` | Width of the cleared centre well as a fraction of the symbol, used when a logo is passed. |
| mask? | `number` |  | Force a mask pattern (0 to 7) instead of picking the lowest penalty one. |
| caption? | `string` |  | Caption under the code. Defaults to the host of a URL value or the value itself. Pass an empty string to hide. |
| download? | `boolean` | `true` | Show the Download SVG button. |
| fileName? | `string` | `"qr-code.svg"` | File name for the download. |
| bare? | `boolean` | `false` | Render the bare SVG with no card, caption or button. |
| title? | `string` |  | Accessible name. Defaults to "QR code for <value>". |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Logo or icon placed in a cleared centre well. Only rendered when `level` is "H". |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

### QuantityStepper

Minus and plus buttons around a number, clamped between `min` and `max`.

Use it for cart quantities, seat counts and guest numbers where people nudge a small integer. For free numeric entry use NumberInput; for a continuous range use Slider.

- Name: `quantity-stepper` (component, E-commerce)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/quantity-stepper` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { QuantityStepper } from "@/components/ui/quantity-stepper"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/quantity-stepper"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Uses: button
- Related: number-input, slider, currency-input
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/quantity-stepper (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/quantity-stepper.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value? | `number` |  | Controlled quantity. |
| defaultValue? | `number` | `1` | Starting quantity when uncontrolled. |
| min? | `number` | `1` | Lowest allowed value; the minus button disables there. |
| max? | `number` | `99` | Highest allowed value; the plus button disables there. |
| step? | `number` | `1` | Amount each press adds or removes. |
| onChange? | `(n: number) => void` |  | Fires with the clamped new value. |
| disabled? | `boolean` |  |  |
| aria-label? | `string` |  | Names the group and the buttons, e.g. "Tickets" gives "Decrease tickets". |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| name? | `string` |  | Submits the quantity in a hidden input under this name. No name by default. |

```tsx
const [qty, setQty] = React.useState(1)
<QuantityStepper value={qty} onChange={setQty} min={1} max={10} aria-label="Tickets" />
```

### QueryBuilder

Rows of "field / operator / value" filter clauses joined by AND, with add and remove.

Use it for advanced filters on issue lists, tables and logs. Controlled with `value` + `onChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultValue`. For quick one-tap filters use FilterBar or ChipFilter.

- Name: `query-builder` (component, Tables)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/query-builder` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { QueryBuilder } from "@/components/ui/query-builder"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/query-builder"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Uses: button, icon-button
- Related: filter-bar, chip-filter
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/query-builder (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/query-builder.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value? | `Clause[]` |  | Controlled clauses. |
| defaultValue? | `Clause[]` | `SAMPLE` | Starting clauses when uncontrolled. |
| onChange? | `(clauses: Clause[]) => void` |  | Fires with the full clause list after every edit, add or remove. |
| fields? | `string[]` | `["status", "assignee", "priority"]` | Field names offered in the first select. |
| operators? | `string[]` | `["is", "is not", "contains"]` | Operators offered in the second select. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
const [clauses, setClauses] = React.useState<Clause[]>([{ id: "1", field: "status", op: "is", value: "open" }])
<QueryBuilder value={clauses} onChange={setClauses} fields={["status", "assignee", "label"]} />
```

### QuotaBar

A labelled usage meter that reads "used / max" and fills to the percentage.

Use it on billing and usage pages for anything metered against a limit. The fill turns warning at `warnAt` percent and danger once the limit is reached. For task progress toward a finish use Progress; for many quotas at once use ResourceQuotaGrid.

- Name: `quota-bar` (component, Billing)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/quota-bar` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { QuotaBar } from "@/components/ui/quota-bar"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/quota-bar"`)
- Related: progress, resource-quota-grid, coverage-meter, meter, usage-breakdown
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/quota-bar (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/quota-bar.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label? | `string` | `"API requests"` | What is being metered; also the meter's accessible name. |
| used? | `number` | `72400` | Amount consumed. |
| max? | `number` | `100000` | The limit. |
| format? | `(n: number) => string` | `(n: number) => en.format(n)` | Formats `used` and `max` for display. Defaults to en-US grouping, so server and client render the same text. |
| warnAt? | `number` | `90` | Percent at which the fill turns to the warning tone. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<QuotaBar label="Seats" used={18} max={25} />
<QuotaBar label="Storage" used={46.2} max={50} format={(n) => `${n} GB`} />
```

### RadarChart

A filled polygon over concentric rings, one axis per label.

Use it to compare five to eight scores on the same 0 to 1 scale, like a vendor or skill scorecard. The shape glides to new values on the data spring. For goals against targets use RadialChart; for exact comparisons use a bar chart.

- Name: `radar-chart` (component, Charts)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/radar-chart` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { RadarChart } from "@/components/ui/radar-chart"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/radar-chart"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Related: radial-chart
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/radar-chart (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/radar-chart.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| labels? | `string[]` | `SAMPLE_LABELS` | One axis per label, drawn clockwise from the top. |
| values? | `number[]` | `SAMPLE_VALUES` | One value per label, from 0 to 1. Missing values count as 0. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| label? | `string` | `"Radar chart"` | Accessible name. The spoken label also lists every axis and its score. |

```tsx
<RadarChart labels={["Speed", "Cost", "Support", "Docs", "Uptime"]} values={[0.8, 0.6, 0.9, 0.7, 0.95]} label="Vendor scorecard" />
```

### RadialChart

A radial bar chart of concentric progress rings, each labelled at its start, with a legend and a centre total. Rings sweep to new values on the data spring when the data changes and the total rolls. Pass a single item to get a full radial progress ring.

- Name: `radial-chart` (component, Charts)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/radial-chart` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { RadialChart } from "@/components/ui/radial-chart"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/radial-chart"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Uses: segmented-control
- Related: donut-chart, goal-ring, progress-circle, radar-chart
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/radial-chart (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/radial-chart.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| data? | `RadialDatum[]` |  | Rings, outermost first. One item renders a single radial progress ring. |
| periods? | `RadialPeriod[]` | `PERIODS` | Datasets to switch between with a segmented control. Ignored when `data` is set. |
| title? | `string` | `"Goals progress"` |  |
| centerLabel? | `string` |  | Label under the centre total. |
| centerValue? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Override the centre value. Defaults to the average progress of all rings. |
| thickness? | `number` |  | Ring thickness in chart units (the chart is 240 wide). |
| gap? | `number` | `6` | Gap between rings in chart units. |
| showLegend? | `boolean` | `true` |  |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

### RadioGroup

Accessible single choice radios on Base UI, with arrow-key navigation built in.

Use it for two to six mutually exclusive options shown at once, each with a Label. For a compact switcher use SegmentedControl; for long lists use Select. Base UI's `onValueChange` receives `(value, eventDetails)`.

- Name: `radio-group` (component, Forms)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/radio-group` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from "@/components/ui/radio-group"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/radio-group"`)
- Dependencies: @base-ui/react
- Related: label, segmented-control, select, checkbox-group, choice-card, facet-filter, priority-picker, region-picker
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/radio-group (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/radio-group.md)

Props: RadioGroupPrimitive props.

```tsx
<RadioGroup defaultValue="card" aria-label="Payment method" onValueChange={(v) => setMethod(v as string)}>
  <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
    <RadioGroupItem value="card" id="pm-card" />
    <Label htmlFor="pm-card">Card</Label>
  </div>
  <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
    <RadioGroupItem value="bank" id="pm-bank" />
    <Label htmlFor="pm-bank">Bank transfer</Label>
  </div>
</RadioGroup>
```

### RangeSlider

A two-thumb slider for picking a low and high value. Both value bubbles show while either thumb is dragged.

Use it for price, date or size ranges. For one value use Slider. Values are plain number arrays `[low, high]`; `onValueCommitted` fires once on release, which is the place to query.

- Name: `range-slider` (component, Forms)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/range-slider` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { RangeSlider } from "@/components/ui/range-slider"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/range-slider"`)
- Uses: slider
- Related: slider
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/range-slider (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/range-slider.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value? | `number[]` |  | Controlled `[low, high]`. |
| defaultValue? | `number[]` | `[25, 75]` | Starting `[low, high]` when uncontrolled. |
| onValueChange? | `(value: number[]) => void` |  | Fires on every move with `[low, high]`. |
| onValueCommitted? | `(value: number[]) => void` |  | Fires once when the user releases the thumb. |
| min? | `number` | `0` |  |
| max? | `number` | `100` |  |
| step? | `number` | `1` | Snap interval. |
| disabled? | `boolean` |  |  |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| aria-label? | `string` |  | Accessible name. Defaults to "Range" unless `aria-labelledby` is set. |

```tsx
<RangeSlider defaultValue={[20, 80]} min={0} max={200} step={5} aria-label="Price" onValueCommitted={([lo, hi]) => setPrice({ lo, hi })} />
```

### Rating

A row of stars people click or arrow through to give a 1 to `max` score.

Use it for reviews and feedback prompts. It is a radio group: Tab lands on the current star, arrow keys move and select, hover previews. Pass `readOnly` to display an average without input. For a numeric scale with labels use SegmentedControl.

- Name: `rating` (component, Forms)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/rating` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { Rating } from "@/components/ui/rating"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/rating"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Related: segmented-control, feedback-thumbs
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/rating (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/rating.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value? | `number` |  | Controlled score, 0 for none. |
| defaultValue? | `number` | `0` | Starting score when uncontrolled. |
| onChange? | `(value: number) => void` |  | Fires with the picked score. |
| max? | `number` | `5` | Number of stars. |
| disabled? | `boolean` |  |  |
| readOnly? | `boolean` |  | Show the score without letting people change it. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| name? | `string` |  | Submits the score (0 when unrated) in a hidden input under this name. No name by default. |
| aria-label? | `string` |  | Accessible name of the group. |

```tsx
const [score, setScore] = React.useState(0)
<Rating value={score} onChange={setScore} aria-label="Rate your onboarding" />
<Rating value={4} readOnly aria-label="Average rating, 4 out of 5" />
```

### ReactionBar

Emoji reaction pills with counts; the ones you pressed get the accent border.

Use it under comments, chat messages and changelog posts. Without `onToggle` it keeps its own counts; with it, you own the data and pass back updated `reactions`. Each pill is a toggle button with `aria-pressed`.

- Name: `reaction-bar` (component, Feedback)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/reaction-bar` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ReactionBar } from "@/components/ui/reaction-bar"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/reaction-bar"`)
- Related: emoji-picker, vote-control
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/reaction-bar (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/reaction-bar.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| reactions? | `Reaction[]` | `SAMPLE_REACTIONS` | Pills to show, in order. |
| onToggle? | `(emoji: string) => void` |  | Called with the emoji that was pressed. Omit it and the bar toggles its own counts. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ReactionBar reactions={[{ emoji: "👍", count: 3, active: true }, { emoji: "🎉", count: 1 }]} onToggle={(emoji) => toggleReaction(messageId, emoji)} />
```

### ReadReceipt

One tick for sent, two for delivered, two accent ticks for read.

Use it next to a message timestamp in chat bubbles. It carries a spoken label ("Read"), so it is not silent for screen readers. For a full delivery timeline use a status list.

### ReasoningBlock

The model's thinking, folded by default; the title shimmers while active and reports how long it took when done.

Use it above an assistant message to hold chain-of-thought or tool reasoning. Folded content is inert, so it is skipped by Tab and screen readers until opened. Controlled with `open` + `onOpenChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultOpen`. For generic disclosure use Collapsible.

- Name: `reasoning-block` (component, AI chat)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/reasoning-block` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ReasoningBlock } from "@/components/ui/reasoning-block"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/reasoning-block"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Related: collapsible, thinking-block
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/reasoning-block (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/reasoning-block.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title? | `string` | `"Thinking"` |  |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Compared density against the table s...` | The reasoning text or nodes shown when expanded. |
| defaultOpen? | `boolean` | `false` | Start expanded when uncontrolled. |
| open? | `boolean` |  | Controlled expanded state. |
| onOpenChange? | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Fires with the new expanded state when the header is pressed. |
| active? | `boolean` | `false` | True while the model is still thinking. |
| duration? | `string` |  | e.g. "4s" — renders "Thought for 4s" when not active. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ReasoningBlock active={isThinking} duration="4s">{reasoningText}</ReasoningBlock>
```

### Receipt

A monospaced receipt card with an id, itemised lines and a ruled total.

Use it in order confirmations, billing history and chat answers that show a charge. Amounts are display strings, so format money before passing it, and `total` is shown as given. For a bill with a status and due date use `InvoiceDetail`; for the emailed version use `EmailReceipt`.

- Name: `receipt` (component, Billing)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/receipt` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { Receipt } from "@/components/ui/receipt"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/receipt"`)
- Related: invoice-detail, email-receipt
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/receipt (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/receipt.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id? | `string` | `"RCP-2041"` | Receipt number shown in the header. |
| lines? | `ReceiptLine[]` | `SAMPLE_LINES` | Itemised lines, in order. |
| total? | `string` | `"$104.76"` | Formatted grand total. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<Receipt id="RCP-1042" lines={[{ label: "Pro plan", amount: "$49.00" }, { label: "Tax", amount: "$3.92" }]} total="$52.92" />
```

### RegenerateBar

A "Not quite right?" footer under an AI answer with Regenerate and an optional Edit prompt button.

Use it at the end of an assistant message. For per-message copy, like and retry icons use a message actions row instead.

- Name: `regenerate-bar` (component, AI chat)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/regenerate-bar` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { RegenerateBar } from "@/components/ui/regenerate-bar"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/regenerate-bar"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Uses: button
- Related: message-actions, message-branch
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/regenerate-bar (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/regenerate-bar.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onRegenerate? | `() => void` |  | Fires when Regenerate is pressed. |
| onEdit? | `() => void` |  | Shows an Edit prompt button when set. |
| label? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Not quite right?"` | Muted prompt on the left. |
| pending? | `boolean` | `false` | True while a new answer streams: Regenerate is disabled and its icon spins. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<RegenerateBar onRegenerate={retry} onEdit={() => setEditing(true)} pending={isStreaming} />
```

### RegionPicker

A grid of selectable region cards, each with a name and a latency hint.

Use it in deploy and project setup flows to choose a data region. It is a radio group: Tab lands on the selected card, arrow keys move and select. For a plain list of options use RadioGroup or Select.

- Name: `region-picker` (component, Settings)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/region-picker` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { RegionPicker } from "@/components/ui/region-picker"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/region-picker"`)
- Related: radio-group, select, language-picker
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/region-picker (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/region-picker.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| regions? | `Region[]` | `SAMPLE_REGIONS` | Regions to offer. |
| value? | `string` |  | Controlled region id. |
| defaultValue? | `string` |  | Starting region id when uncontrolled. Defaults to the first region. |
| onChange? | `(id: string) => void` |  | Fires with the picked region id. |
| aria-label? | `string` |  | Accessible name of the group. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
const [region, setRegion] = React.useState("eu-west")
<RegionPicker value={region} onChange={setRegion} regions={[{ id: "eu-west", label: "EU West", latency: "42ms" }, { id: "us-east", label: "US East" }]} />
```

### RelativeTime

A time element that reads "3h ago" and carries the exact ISO timestamp for machines.

Use it in feeds, comments, activity logs and table cells. Hover shows the full local date. Set `live` to refresh the label every minute. Server and client may disagree by a minute, so the text is hydration-safe. An invalid date renders nothing. For a fixed date use a formatted string in a time element.

- Name: `relative-time` (component, Dev tools)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/relative-time` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { RelativeTime } from "@/components/ui/relative-time"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/relative-time"`)
- Related: due-date-chip, notification-item
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/relative-time (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/relative-time.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| date? | `string \| Date` |  | The instant to describe: a Date or any string `new Date()` parses (ISO 8601 is safest). Defaults to three hours ago. |
| live? | `boolean` | `false` | Re-render once a minute so the label stays current. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<RelativeTime date={comment.createdAt} />
<RelativeTime date="2026-11-14T09:30:00Z" live />
```

### ResetPasswordForm

A "set a new password" card with confirm field and a mismatch check.

Use it on the page a password reset email links to. It checks the two fields match and meet `minLength` before calling `onSubmit`; send the token and password to your server there. For the "email me a link" step use a forgot password form.

- Name: `reset-password-form` (component, Auth)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/reset-password-form` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ResetPasswordForm } from "@/components/ui/reset-password-form"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/reset-password-form"`)
- Uses: auth-card, button, form-field, input
- Related: forgot-password-form
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/reset-password-form (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/reset-password-form.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onSubmit? | `(password: string) => void` |  | Called with the new password once both fields match. |
| minLength? | `number` | `8` | Minimum password length enforced by the browser. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ResetPasswordForm onSubmit={(password) => resetPassword({ token, password })} />
```

### ResizablePanels

Split panes for editors, inspectors and dashboards. Drag a handle to resize; the hairline swells to accent under the hand. Arrow keys move it, Shift jumps, Home and End slam it, Enter collapses a collapsible pane and a double click resets the pair. Controlled or uncontrolled sizes, nothing is persisted. With no children it renders a three pane editor demo.

- Name: `resizable-panels` (component, Layout)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/resizable-panels` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ResizablePanels, ResizablePanel, ResizableHandle } from "@/components/ui/resizable-panels"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/resizable-panels"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Related: split-pane
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/resizable-panels (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/resizable-panels.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Panels and handles: `ResizablePanel` and `ResizableHandle` children, nestable. Leave empty for the editor demo. |
| orientation? | `Orientation` | `"horizontal"` | Direction the panels are laid out in. |
| sizes? | `number[]` |  | Controlled sizes in percent, one per panel. |
| defaultSizes? | `number[]` |  | Starting sizes in percent when uncontrolled. Overrides each panel's `defaultSize`. |
| onSizesChange? | `(sizes: number[]) => void` |  | Fires with the new sizes on every drag, key press or snap. |
| keyboardStep? | `number` | `2` | Percent moved per arrow key. Shift multiplies by five. |
| left? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Two panel shorthand: content of the first panel. |
| right? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Two panel shorthand: content of the second panel. |
| initial? | `number` | `50` | Two panel shorthand: starting size of the first panel in percent. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ResizablePanels left={<p className="text-sm text-fg-muted">Left pane</p>} right={<p className="text-sm text-fg-muted">Right pane</p>} />
```

### ResourceQuotaGrid

A responsive grid of quota cards, one bar per metered resource, for plan and usage pages.

Use on a plan or usage page to show every metered limit at once: seats, API calls, storage. Each card is a QuotaBar, so bars turn warning at `warnAt` (90% by default) and danger at the limit. Two columns from `sm`. For a single meter use QuotaBar directly.

- Name: `resource-quota-grid` (component, Dashboard)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/resource-quota-grid` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ResourceQuotaGrid } from "@/components/ui/resource-quota-grid"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/resource-quota-grid"`)
- Uses: quota-bar
- Related: quota-bar, usage-breakdown, admin-console
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/resource-quota-grid (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/resource-quota-grid.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items? | `Quota[]` | `SAMPLE_QUOTAS` | Metered resources to show. Defaults to a Lumen workspace on the Scale plan. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ResourceQuotaGrid items={[{ label: "Seats", used: 18, max: 25 }, { label: "Storage", used: 38, max: 50, format: (n) => `${n} GB` }]} />
```

### RetryBlock

A danger alert explaining what failed, with a Try again button under it.

Use it where a fetch, upload or AI request failed and retrying might work. The alert is a live region, so the failure is announced. For a whole empty page use an error state or EmptyState.

- Name: `retry-block` (component, Feedback)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/retry-block` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { RetryBlock } from "@/components/ui/retry-block"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/retry-block"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Uses: button, inline-alert
- Related: empty-state
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/retry-block (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/retry-block.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title? | `string` | `"Request failed"` | Bold first line of the alert. |
| description? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Check your connection and try again."` | What happened and what to do. |
| onRetry? | `() => void` |  | Fires when Try again is pressed. |
| retrying? | `boolean` | `false` | True while the retry runs: the button is disabled and its icon spins. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<RetryBlock title="Could not load invoices" description="The server did not answer." onRetry={refetch} retrying={isFetching} />
```

### ReviewRequestCard

A pull request awaiting your review: title, repo, author avatar and Review / View diff buttons.

Use it in inboxes, dashboards and notification panels for code review requests. For a full PR row with checks and labels use a list item of your own.

- Name: `review-request-card` (component, Dev tools)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/review-request-card` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`

- Related: engineering-console

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title? | `string` | `"Premium motion elevation"` | Pull request title, rendered as an h3. |
| repo? | `string` | `"lumen/web"` | Repository the PR lives in. |
| author? | `string` | `"Maya Chen"` | Author name; the avatar shows its initials. |
| onReview? | `() => void` |  | Fires when Review is pressed. |
| onViewDiff? | `() => void` |  | Fires when View diff is pressed. |

```tsx
<ReviewRequestCard title="Add invoice export" repo="lumen/web" author="Maya Chen" onReview={() => router.push(prUrl)} onViewDiff={openDiff} />
```

### RichTextToolbar

A formatting bar (bold, italic, link, bullet and numbered lists) for a text editor.

Use it above a Textarea or a contenteditable editor. It is a real ARIA toolbar on Base UI: one Tab stop, arrow keys move between buttons. Wire `onAction` to your editor's commands. For a table's search and filter row use TableToolbar.

- Name: `rich-text-toolbar` (component, Forms)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/rich-text-toolbar` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { RichTextToolbar } from "@/components/ui/rich-text-toolbar"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/rich-text-toolbar"`)
- Dependencies: @base-ui/react, lucide-react
- Uses: toggle, toggle-group
- Related: textarea, table-toolbar, markdown-editor
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/rich-text-toolbar (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/rich-text-toolbar.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onAction? | `(action: RichTextAction, pressed: boolean) => void` |  | Fires with the action and its new pressed state whenever a button toggles. |
| aria-label? | `string` |  | Accessible name of the toolbar. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<RichTextToolbar onAction={(action, pressed) => editor.chain().focus().run(action, pressed)} />
```

### RolePermissionMatrix

A permissions table with one checkbox per role and capability, for workspace access settings.

Rows are capabilities, columns are roles; each checkbox is named "<role> <permission>" for screen readers. Seed it with `isChecked` and listen with `onCheckedChange`. For assigning one role to one person use RolePicker.

- Name: `role-permission-matrix` (component, Settings)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/role-permission-matrix` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { RolePermissionMatrix } from "@/components/ui/role-permission-matrix"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/role-permission-matrix"`)
- Uses: checkbox
- Related: role-picker, seat-manager
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/role-permission-matrix (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/role-permission-matrix.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| roles? | `string[]` | `SAMPLE_ROLES` | Column headers. Defaults to Lumen's three workspace roles. |
| permissions? | `string[]` | `SAMPLE_PERMISSIONS` | Row labels, one per capability. |
| isChecked? | `(role: string, permission: string) => boolean` | `sampleChecked` | Starting state of each checkbox. Defaults to everything on except Member, who only reads. |
| onCheckedChange? | `(role: string, permission: string, checked: boolean) => void` |  | Fires when a checkbox changes. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<RolePermissionMatrix
  roles={["Admin", "Member"]}
  permissions={["Read", "Edit"]}
  isChecked={(role, permission) => role === "Admin" || permission === "Read"}
  onCheckedChange={(role, permission, checked) => savePermission(role, permission, checked)}
/>
```

### RolePicker

Labelled radios for choosing one workspace role (Owner, Admin, Member by default).

Use it in invite dialogs and member settings. Built on RadioGroup, so arrow keys move and select. For editing what each role can do use RolePermissionMatrix.

- Name: `role-picker` (component, Settings)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/role-picker` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { RolePicker } from "@/components/ui/role-picker"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/role-picker"`)
- Uses: label, radio-group
- Related: radio-group, role-permission-matrix, seat-manager
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/role-picker (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/role-picker.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| roles? | `RoleOption[]` | `SAMPLE_ROLES` | Roles to offer, in order. |
| value? | `string` |  | Controlled role value. |
| defaultValue? | `string` | `"member"` | Starting role when uncontrolled. |
| onValueChange? | `(value: string) => void` |  | Fires with the picked role value. |
| name? | `string` |  | Form field name, so the picked role is sent with a surrounding form. |
| aria-label? | `string` |  | Accessible name of the group. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<RolePicker value={role} onValueChange={setRole} roles={[{ value: "admin", label: "Admin" }, { value: "viewer", label: "Viewer" }]} />
```

### RowSelection

The select checkbox for a data table row or header, with an indeterminate state.

Put one in each row's first cell and one in the header with `indeterminate` when only some rows are selected. It is a Checkbox with a default "Select row" name; give each row a specific one. Use it with `Table` and `BulkActionsBar`; `DataTable` with `selectable` draws its own checkboxes.

- Name: `row-selection` (component, Tables)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/row-selection` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { RowSelection } from "@/components/ui/row-selection"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/row-selection"`)
- Uses: checkbox
- Related: checkbox, select, table, bulk-actions-bar, data-table
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/row-selection (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/row-selection.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| checked? | `boolean` |  | Whether the row is selected. |
| indeterminate? | `boolean` |  | Shows a dash: some, not all, rows are selected. Use on the header checkbox. |
| onCheckedChange? | `(v: boolean) => void` |  | Fires with the new checked state. |
| disabled? | `boolean` |  |  |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| aria-label? | `string` |  | Accessible name. Defaults to "Select row". |

```tsx
<RowSelection checked={allSelected} indeterminate={someSelected} onCheckedChange={toggleAll} aria-label="Select all rows" />
<RowSelection checked={selected.has(row.id)} onCheckedChange={(on) => toggle(row.id, on)} aria-label={`Select ${row.name}`} />
```

### SankeyChart

A sankey diagram. Columns come from the links themselves, ribbons curve between nodes with a gradient from source to target, and hovering or focusing a node lights its flows while the rest fall back. Nodes are keyboard focusable with a spoken summary; a hidden table carries the data.

- Name: `sankey-chart` (component, Charts)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/sankey-chart` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { SankeyChart } from "@/components/ui/sankey-chart"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/sankey-chart"`)
- Related: funnel-chart
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/sankey-chart (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/sankey-chart.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| links? | `SankeyLink[]` | `SAMPLE_LINKS` | Flows between node ids. Columns are computed from these. |
| nodes? | `SankeyNodeInput[]` | `SAMPLE_NODES` | Optional node order, labels and colours. Unknown ids found in links are added automatically. |
| align? | `"left" \| "justify"` | `"left"` | "left" puts each node one column after its furthest source; "justify" also pushes nodes with no outgoing links to the last column. |
| title? | `string` | `"Where signups come from"` |  |
| caption? | `string` | `"Last 30 days, visitors to paid plan"` |  |
| height? | `number` | `320` | Chart height in px. The width follows the container. |
| nodeWidth? | `number` | `10` |  |
| nodePadding? | `number` | `14` | Vertical gap between nodes in a column, in px. |
| format? | `(value: number) => string` | `defaultFormat` | Formats values in labels, the tooltip text and the table. |
| unit? | `string` | `"visitors"` | Unit word for accessible labels, e.g. "visitors". |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

### SavedViews

A vertical list of saved filters ("My open", "Needs review") with counts, one selected.

Use it in an issue tracker or inbox sidebar. It is a single-select listbox: Tab lands on the selected view, Up and Down arrows move and select, Home and End jump. For top-level page navigation use a sidebar nav; for switching panels in place use Tabs.

- Name: `saved-views` (component, Tables)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/saved-views` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { SavedViews } from "@/components/ui/saved-views"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/saved-views"`)
- Related: tabs, column-visibility-menu
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/saved-views (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/saved-views.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| views? | `View[]` | `SAMPLE_VIEWS` | Views to list, in order. |
| value? | `string` |  | Controlled selected view id. |
| defaultValue? | `string` |  | Starting view id when uncontrolled. Defaults to the first view. |
| onChange? | `(id: string) => void` |  | Fires with the picked view id. |
| aria-label? | `string` |  | Accessible name of the list. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<SavedViews views={[{ id: "mine", name: "My open", count: 12 }, { id: "all", name: "All issues" }]} value={view} onChange={setView} />
```

### ScatterChart

Plots two numbers against each other in SVG; the pointer snaps to the nearest point and the arrow keys walk them.

Use it to show how two measures relate across many items: deal size against win rate, price against rating, latency against payload. Give points a `size` and it becomes a bubble chart. For one measure over time use LineChart or InteractiveAreaChart; for totals by category use BarChart. No chart library: ticks are rounded to 1, 2, 2.5 or 5 steps, and hovering a ChartLegend entry dims the other series.

- Name: `scatter-chart` (component, Charts)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/scatter-chart` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ScatterChart } from "@/components/ui/scatter-chart"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/scatter-chart"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Uses: chart-legend, chart-tooltip-card
- Related: line-chart, interactive-area-chart, bar-chart, chart-legend
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/scatter-chart (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/scatter-chart.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| series? | `ScatterSeries[]` | `SAMPLE` | One or more series of `{ x, y, size?, label? }` points. |
| xLabel? | `string` |  | X axis title, also used in the tooltip and point labels. |
| yLabel? | `string` |  | Y axis title, also used in the tooltip and point labels. |
| xFormat? | `Format` |  | Intl.NumberFormat options (works from Server Components) or a function, for x ticks and values. |
| yFormat? | `Format` |  | Intl.NumberFormat options or a function, for y ticks and values. |
| sizeLabel? | `string` | `"Size"` | What `size` measures, shown in the tooltip in bubble mode. |
| sizeRange? | `[number, number]` | `[8, 40]` | Smallest and largest bubble diameter in px. Bubble area grows with `size`. |
| referenceLines? | `ReferenceLine[]` | `[]` | Dashed lines at fixed values, such as a target or a median. Included in the axis range. |
| height? | `number` | `280` | Plot height in px, not counting the axis labels and legend. |
| locale? | `string` | `"en-US"` | Locale for number formatting. Fixed by default so server and browser render the same text. |
| legend? | `boolean` | `true` | Show a ChartLegend under the chart when there is more than one series. |
| label? | `string` | `"Scatter chart"` | Accessible name of the chart. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ScatterChart
  label="Deal size against days to close"
  xLabel="Deal size"
  yLabel="Days to close"
  xFormat={{ style: "currency", currency: "USD", notation: "compact" }}
  series={[{ name: "Inbound", points: [{ x: 12000, y: 21 }, { x: 48000, y: 64, label: "Northwind" }] }]}
/>
```

### SchemaFieldRow

One row of an API or data schema: field name, required badge, type and description.

Stack several to document a request body, a webhook payload or a database table. Rows are responsive: three columns from `sm`, stacked below. For an interactive table use DataTable.

- Name: `schema-field-row` (component, Dev tools)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/schema-field-row` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { SchemaFieldRow } from "@/components/ui/schema-field-row"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/schema-field-row"`)
- Uses: badge
- Related: stack, data-table
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/schema-field-row (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/schema-field-row.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name | `string` |  | Field name, shown in monospace. |
| type | `string` |  | Type signature, shown in monospace, e.g. "string" or "Invoice[]". |
| required? | `boolean` |  | Adds a "required" badge. |
| description? | `React.ReactNode` |  | What the field means. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<SchemaFieldRow name="amount" type="integer" required description="Amount in cents." />
<SchemaFieldRow name="metadata" type="Record<string, string>" description="Up to 50 keys." />
```

### ScrollArea

A scroll container with thin, themed scrollbars on Base UI; native scrolling underneath.

Give it a fixed height (or max height) and put long content inside. Set `orientation` to "horizontal" or "both" for sideways overflow. The viewport is keyboard focusable so arrow keys scroll it. For a whole page let the body scroll instead.

- Name: `scroll-area` (component, Layout)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/scroll-area` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ScrollArea, ScrollBar } from "@/components/ui/scroll-area"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/scroll-area"`)
- Dependencies: @base-ui/react
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/scroll-area (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/scroll-area.md)

Props (also accepts ScrollAreaPrimitive.Root props):

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| orientation? | `"vertical" \| "horizontal" \| "both"` | `"vertical"` | Which scrollbars to render. |

```tsx
<ScrollArea className="h-72 rounded-xl border border-border">
  <div className="p-4">{longList}</div>
</ScrollArea>
```

### SearchInput

A search field with a magnifier icon and a clear button that appears once there is text.

Use it for list filters, table search and site search. Escape or the clear button empties it and keeps focus in the field; an Escape that clears text does not also close a surrounding dialog. Controlled (`value` + `onChange`) or uncontrolled. Clearing calls `onClear` and an `onChange` whose `target.value` is "". For a field with a result list use SearchWithResults; for a command launcher use CommandPalette.

- Name: `search-input` (component, Forms)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/search-input` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { SearchInput } from "@/components/ui/search-input"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/search-input"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Uses: input-affix
- Related: search-with-results, command-palette, input-affix, input, docs-marketing
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/search-input (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/search-input.md)

Props (also accepts <input>):

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| size? | `"sm" \| "default" \| "lg"` | `"default"` | Field height: 32, 36 or 44px. |
| onClear? | `() => void` |  | Fires after the clear button or Escape empties the field. |
| containerClassName? | `string` |  | Classes for the outer field box; className goes to the inner input. |

```tsx
<SearchInput aria-label="Search invoices" placeholder="Search invoices…" value={q} onChange={(e) => setQ(e.target.value)} />
```

### SearchWithResults

A search field with a result list underneath, for global search and quick lookups.

Without `onSearch` it filters `results` by title and subtitle itself; with it, you fetch and pass back `results`. Pass `onSelect` to make each result a button. The result count is announced to screen readers. For a keyboard-first launcher use CommandPalette; for a field alone use SearchInput.

- Name: `search-with-results` (component, Forms)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/search-with-results` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { SearchWithResults } from "@/components/ui/search-with-results"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/search-with-results"`)
- Uses: search-input
- Related: command-palette, search-input, search-results-page
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/search-with-results (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/search-with-results.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| results? | `SearchResult[]` | `SAMPLE_RESULTS` | Results to list. Defaults to a Lumen search across invoices, customers and deploys. |
| onSearch? | `(q: string) => void` |  | Called on every keystroke. Without it, the list filters itself by title and subtitle. |
| onSelect? | `(result: SearchResult) => void` |  | Makes each result a button and fires with the picked result. |
| placeholder? | `string` | `"Search…"` | Placeholder and accessible name of the field. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<SearchWithResults results={hits} onSearch={setQuery} onSelect={(r) => router.push(`/items/${r.id}`)} />
```

### SeatManager

A card listing workspace members with their roles, a seats-used count and an Invite button.

Use it on billing and team settings pages. The "N of M used" line is computed from `seats` and `limit`. For editing a member's role use RolePicker; for permissions use RolePermissionMatrix.

- Name: `seat-manager` (component, Billing)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/seat-manager` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { SeatManager } from "@/components/ui/seat-manager"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/seat-manager"`)
- Uses: badge, button
- Related: role-picker, role-permission-matrix, invite-members
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/seat-manager (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/seat-manager.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| seats? | `Seat[]` | `SAMPLE_SEATS` | Members holding a seat, keyed by email. |
| limit? | `number` | `10` | Seats the plan includes. |
| onInvite? | `() => void` |  | Fires when Invite is pressed. The button disables once every seat is used. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<SeatManager seats={[{ name: "Maya Chen", email: "maya@lumen.app", role: "Owner" }]} limit={10} onInvite={openInvite} />
```

### SecretReveal

A masked API key or token with Reveal and Copy buttons.

Use it on API key and webhook secret settings. Copy always copies the real secret, even while masked. Pass only `revealedValue` and the mask is generated, keeping the prefix and the last four characters. For a plain copyable value use CodeBlock or CopyButton.

- Name: `secret-reveal` (component, Dev tools)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/secret-reveal` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { SecretReveal } from "@/components/ui/secret-reveal"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/secret-reveal"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Uses: copy-button, icon-button
- Related: code-block, copy-button, api-key-list, copy-id, create-api-key, scratch-to-reveal
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/secret-reveal (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/secret-reveal.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value? | `string` |  | The masked text shown while hidden. Generated from `revealedValue` when omitted. |
| revealedValue? | `string` | `"md_live_8k2m9f2a"` | The real secret, shown when revealed and always used for Copy. |
| label? | `string` | `"secret"` | Names the buttons, e.g. "API key" gives "Reveal API key" and "Copy API key". |
| defaultRevealed? | `boolean` | `false` | Start revealed. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<SecretReveal revealedValue={apiKey} label="Live API key" />
```

### SectionHeader

A section title with an optional description on the left and actions on the right.

Use it to head a settings group, a dashboard panel or a list. It renders an h2 by default; set `level` to keep the document outline correct. For a whole page title use PageHeader.

- Name: `section-header` (component, Layout)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/section-header` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { SectionHeader } from "@/components/ui/section-header"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/section-header"`)
- Related: page-header, heading, hero
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/section-header (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/section-header.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |
| description? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Muted line under the title. |
| actions? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Buttons or links aligned to the right; they wrap under the title on narrow screens. |
| level? | `2 \| 3 \| 4` | `2` | Heading level of the title: 2 renders h2, 3 renders h3, 4 renders h4. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<SectionHeader title="Members" description="People with access to this workspace." actions={<Button size="sm">Invite</Button>} />
<SectionHeader level={3} title="Danger zone" />
```

### SegmentedControl

A row of options with a raised thumb that glides to the selected one.

Use it for two to five mutually exclusive views or modes (Monthly / Yearly, List / Board). It is a radio group: Tab lands on the selected option, arrows move and select, Home and End jump. Controlled with `value` + `onChange` or uncontrolled with `defaultValue`. For form fields use RadioGroup; for switching whole panels use Tabs; for on/off toolbar buttons use ToggleGroup.

- Name: `segmented-control` (component, Forms)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/segmented-control` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { SegmentedControl } from "@/components/ui/segmented-control"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/segmented-control"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Related: radio-group, tabs, toggle-group, button-group, chip-filter, choice-card, density-toggle, env-switcher
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/segmented-control (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/segmented-control.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| options? | `Option[]` |  | Full options. |
| items? | `string[]` |  | Shorthand: plain labels, value = label. |
| value? | `string` |  | Controlled selected value. |
| defaultValue? | `string` |  | Starting value when uncontrolled. Defaults to the first option. |
| onChange? | `(value: string) => void` |  | Fires with the newly selected value. |
| size? | `Size` | `"default"` | Track height: 32, 36 or 44px. |
| fullWidth? | `boolean` |  | Stretch to the container and split space evenly. |
| disabled? | `boolean` |  |  |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| aria-label? | `string` |  | Accessible name of the group. Always set one that says what is being chosen. |
| name? | `string` |  | Submits the selected value in a hidden input under this name. No name by default. |

```tsx
<SegmentedControl items={["Day", "Week", "Month"]} defaultValue="Week" aria-label="Range" />
<SegmentedControl
  aria-label="Layout"
  value={layout}
  onChange={setLayout}
  options={[{ value: "list", label: "List", icon: <ListIcon /> }, { value: "board", label: "Board", icon: <KanbanIcon /> }]}
/>
```

### Select

A styled single or multiple choice dropdown on Base UI, with keyboard typeahead and a check on the chosen item.

Use it for picking one option from five or more in forms and toolbars. For two to four options shown at once use RadioGroup or SegmentedControl; for searchable lists use a Combobox. Pass `items` to `Select` so `SelectValue` shows the label, not the raw value. Base UI's `onValueChange` receives `(value, eventDetails)`. Label the trigger with `aria-label` or a Label whose `htmlFor` matches the trigger `id`.

- Name: `select` (component, Forms)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/select` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { Select, SelectContent, SelectGroup, SelectItem, SelectLabel, SelectScrollDownButton, SelectScrollUpButton, SelectSeparator, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from "@/components/ui/select"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/select"`)
- Dependencies: @base-ui/react, lucide-react
- Related: radio-group, segmented-control, combobox, label, autocomplete, chip-filter, dropdown-menu, filter-bar
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/select (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/select.md)

```tsx
const items = [{ value: "usd", label: "US dollar" }, { value: "eur", label: "Euro" }]
<Select items={items} defaultValue="usd" onValueChange={(v) => setCurrency(v as string)}>
  <SelectTrigger aria-label="Currency" className="w-48">
    <SelectValue placeholder="Pick a currency" />
  </SelectTrigger>
  <SelectContent>
    {items.map((i) => <SelectItem key={i.value} value={i.value}>{i.label}</SelectItem>)}
  </SelectContent>
</Select>
```

### Separator

A 1px hairline that divides content, horizontally or vertically.

Base UI Separator renders `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`. For a purely visual rule inside a list or menu use DropdownMenuSeparator; for a labelled break ("or continue with") put text beside two Separators.

- Name: `separator` (component, Layout)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/separator` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { Separator } from "@/components/ui/separator"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/separator"`)
- Dependencies: @base-ui/react
- Related: dropdown-menu
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/separator (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/separator.md)

Props: SeparatorPrimitive props.

```tsx
<Separator />
<div className="flex h-5 items-center gap-3">Docs<Separator orientation="vertical" />API</div>
```

### ServerErrorState

A 500 error panel: status code, a plain-language headline, a retry button and a copyable request id for support.

Use it where a server call failed and the user can retry. For a missing page use NotFoundState; for an empty list use EmptyState; for an inline field error use FormField `error`.

- Name: `server-error-state` (component, Feedback)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/server-error-state` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ServerErrorState } from "@/components/ui/server-error-state"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/server-error-state"`)
- Uses: button
- Related: not-found-state, empty-state, form-field, error-state, stack-trace
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/server-error-state (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/server-error-state.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Something broke on our side"` | Headline. |
| description? | `React.ReactNode` | `"The request failed on our server. Re...` | One line on what happened and what to do next. |
| code? | `string \| number` | `500` | Status code shown above the headline. |
| onRetry? | `() => void` |  | Called by the Retry button. Without it, no Retry button renders. |
| requestId? | `string` | `"req_8f2c41d0"` | Request id shown in mono and copied by the "Copy request id" button. Defaults to a sample id; pass "" to hide both. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ServerErrorState onRetry={() => refetch()} requestId={error.requestId} />
```

### SessionList

A list of signed-in devices with a revoke action on every session except the current one.

Use it on an account security page so people can sign out a lost or unknown device. Mark the session making the request with `current`: it shows "(this device)" and gets no Revoke button. Revoke does not confirm, so remove the row from `sessions` once your request succeeds. For API keys use ApiKeyList instead.

- Name: `session-list` (component, Settings)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/session-list` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { SessionList } from "@/components/ui/session-list"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/session-list"`)
- Uses: button
- Related: api-key-list
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/session-list (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/session-list.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| sessions? | `Session[]` | `SAMPLE_SESSIONS` | Active sessions, most recent first. Defaults to Maya Chen's Lumen sessions. |
| onRevoke? | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called with the session id when its Revoke button is pressed. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<SessionList sessions={sessions} onRevoke={(id) => revokeSession(id)} />
```

Use SettingsLayout for the page frame and SettingsSection for each titled group of controls; the last section drops its divider. Below `md` the nav stacks above the sections. For app-wide navigation use Sidebar instead; for a ready single-column page use the SettingsPage block.

### Sheet

A side panel that slides over the page from any edge, with a scrim, a title bar and a close button.

Built on Base UI Dialog: focus is trapped inside, the page is inert and scroll-locked, Escape and the scrim close it, and focus returns to the trigger. Use Sheet for secondary tasks beside the page (filters, edit forms, mobile nav); use Dialog for a centred decision, Drawer for a bottom sheet on mobile.

- Name: `sheet` (component, Overlays)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/sheet` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { Sheet } from "@/components/ui/sheet"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/sheet"`)
- Dependencies: @base-ui/react, lucide-react
- Uses: button
- Related: dialog, drawer, app-shell, inline-cell-edit, mobile-nav-drawer, peek-panel, sidebar
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/sheet (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/sheet.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open? | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state. Leave it out and the sheet renders its own "Open sheet" button. |
| onClose? | `() => void` |  | Called when the sheet asks to close: Escape, the scrim or the close button. Set `open` to false here. |
| side? | `"left" \| "right" \| "top" \| "bottom"` | `"right"` | The edge the panel slides in from. |
| title? | `string` |  | Heading in the title bar; also the dialog's accessible name. |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Panel content. Defaults to a Lumen invoice summary. |
| className? | `string` |  | Classes for the panel itself, e.g. `max-w-xl` for a wider sheet. |

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false)
<Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Edit</Button>
<Sheet open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} side="right" title="Edit customer">
  <form>…</form>
</Sheet>
```

### SidebarSection

A titled group inside a Sidebar: a small uppercase label above a stack of SidebarNavItems.

The title names the group for screen readers (`role="group"`). Use one per cluster of links ("Workspace", "Settings"); the Sidebar itself is the outer frame. When the Sidebar collapses to its rail the title becomes screen-reader only, so the group keeps its name. For groups that open and close use NestedNav.

- Name: `sidebar-section` (component, Navigation)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/sidebar-section` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { SidebarSection } from "@/components/ui/sidebar-section"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/sidebar-section"`)
- Related: sidebar, nested-nav

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title? | `string` |  | Group label. Leave it out for an unlabelled group. |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  | The SidebarNavItems in this group. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<SidebarSection title="Workspace">
  <SidebarNavItem active>Inbox</SidebarNavItem>
  <SidebarNavItem>Projects</SidebarNavItem>
</SidebarSection>
```

### Sidebar

An app sidebar frame (224px, or a 56px icon rail when `collapsed`) and its nav items.

Put a `<nav aria-label="Main">` of SidebarNavItems inside, grouped with SidebarSection. When the Sidebar is collapsed, nav item labels become screen-reader only, so items stay named. For a settings page frame use SettingsLayout; for a mobile slide-over use MobileNavDrawer or Sheet.

- Name: `sidebar` (component, Navigation)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/sidebar` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { Sidebar, SidebarNavItem } from "@/components/ui/sidebar"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/sidebar"`)
- Related: sidebar-section, settings-layout, mobile-nav-drawer, sheet, app-shell, collapsible-sidebar, conversation-sidebar, nav-marketing
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/sidebar (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/sidebar.md)

Props (also accepts <aside>):

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| collapsed? | `boolean` | `false` | Narrow icon rail; labels are hidden visually but still read by screen readers. |

```tsx
<Sidebar collapsed={collapsed}>
  <nav aria-label="Main">
    <SidebarNavItem icon={<InboxIcon />} active>Inbox</SidebarNavItem>
  </nav>
</Sidebar>
```

### SignUpForm

A complete sign-up card: GitHub and Google buttons, then name, email and password fields and a submit button.

Fields use browser autofill tokens (`new-password` for the password) and native required checks. Use AuthCard to build your own variant; use SocialAuthRow alone for OAuth-only sign-in.

- Name: `sign-up-form` (component, Auth)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/sign-up-form` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { SignUpForm } from "@/components/ui/sign-up-form"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/sign-up-form"`)
- Uses: auth-card, button, form-field, input, social-auth-row
- Related: auth-card, social-auth-row, magic-link-form
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/sign-up-form (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/sign-up-form.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onSubmit? | `(values: SignUpValues) => void` |  | Called with the field values on submit; the native submit is prevented. |
| signInHref? | `string` | `"#"` | Link target for "Sign in". |
| onGithub? | `() => void` |  | Called by "Continue with GitHub". |
| onGoogle? | `() => void` |  | Called by "Continue with Google". |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<SignUpForm onSubmit={({ name, email, password }) => signUp(name, email, password)} signInHref="/login" />
```

### SignaturePad

A signature field drawn on a canvas with smooth, pressure-aware strokes, undo and clear, a typed-name fallback for keyboard users, and PNG export.

Use it to sign off a contract, a delivery or an approval, where you need an image of the signature rather than a checkbox. Both modes report through one `onChange`: a drawn signature or the typed name rendered in a script face, as a transparent PNG data URL, or null when empty. Store the data URL or upload it as an image. There is no `value` prop, so it always starts empty. For a plain "I agree" use Checkbox; for an uploaded image use ImageUpload.

- Name: `signature-pad` (component, Forms)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/signature-pad` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { SignaturePad } from "@/components/ui/signature-pad"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/signature-pad"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, type
- Uses: button
- Related: checkbox, image-upload
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/signature-pad (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/signature-pad.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onChange? | `(dataUrl: string \| null) => void` |  | Called with a PNG data URL after each stroke or typed change, or null when empty. |
| label? | `string` | `"Signature"` | Visible label; also names the canvas and the typed input. |
| height? | `number` | `180` | Canvas height in px. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
const [sig, setSig] = React.useState<string | null>(null)
<SignaturePad label="Sign to accept" onChange={setSig} />
<Button disabled={!sig}>Accept</Button>
```

### Skeleton

A sunken plate with a hairline sheen that sweeps once per 1.6s, standing in for content while it loads.

Size it with className to match the content it replaces (zero layout shift when the data lands). Skeletons are aria-hidden: mark the loading region `aria-busy="true"` and give it a status label. Use Spinner for a short action in a button; use SkeletonCard for a whole card placeholder.

- Name: `skeleton` (component, Feedback)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/skeleton` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { Skeleton, SkeletonCard } from "@/components/ui/skeleton"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/skeleton"`)
- Related: spinner, loading-overlay, loading-table
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/skeleton (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/skeleton.md)

Props: <div>.

```tsx
<div aria-busy="true" aria-label="Loading invoices">
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-1/3" />
  <Skeleton className="mt-2 h-3 w-full" />
</div>
```

### SkipLink

A "Skip to content" link, visually hidden until it receives keyboard focus, then pinned top-left.

Render it as the first focusable element in the layout. Its `href` must match the id of your main landmark, e.g. `<main id="main" tabIndex={-1}>`, so focus lands there after the skip.

- Name: `skip-link` (component, Navigation)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/skip-link` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { SkipLink } from "@/components/ui/skip-link"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/skip-link"`)
- Related: visually-hidden
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/skip-link (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/skip-link.md)

Props: <a>.

```tsx
<body><SkipLink href="#main" /><Header /><main id="main" tabIndex={-1}>…</main></body>
```

### SlashCommandMenu

A floating list of slash commands filtered by what the user has typed after the slash.

Presentational: you own the editor and pass `query` (text after "/"). The list is a listbox with roving focus: Arrow Up/Down, Home/End move, Enter or click selects, Escape calls `onClose`. For a global action search use CommandPalette; for a menu from a button use DropdownMenu.

- Name: `slash-command-menu` (component, Forms)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/slash-command-menu` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { SlashCommandMenu } from "@/components/ui/slash-command-menu"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/slash-command-menu"`)
- Related: command-palette, dropdown-menu, command-item
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/slash-command-menu (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/slash-command-menu.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items? | `Item[]` | `SAMPLE_ITEMS` | Commands to offer. Defaults to Lumen's composer commands. |
| query? | `string` | `""` | The text typed after the slash; filters the list (case-insensitive substring). |
| onSelect? | `(item: Item) => void` |  | Called with the chosen command. |
| onClose? | `() => void` |  | Called on Escape so you can hide the menu and return focus to the editor. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
{open ? <SlashCommandMenu query={afterSlash} onSelect={(c) => run(c.id)} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} /> : null}
```

### Slider

Hairline rail, keycap thumb and a value bubble while you drag or tab to it.

One value, or a range when `defaultValue`/`value` is an array of two. Use Slider for a continuous or stepped number; use NumberInput when the exact value matters more than the feel, and Switch for on/off. Always name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

Base UI for pointer, keyboard and form behaviour. Hairline rail with an accent fill, a raised keycap thumb whose ring grows on hover, drag and focus, and an ink value bubble that settles in above the thumb while you drag or tab to it. Optional marks sit under the rail. RTL needs Base UI's <DirectionProvider direction="rtl">, not only dir="rtl", or dragging and arrow keys run backwards.

- Name: `slider` (component, Forms)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/slider` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { Slider } from "@/components/ui/slider"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/slider"`)
- Dependencies: @base-ui/react
- Related: number-input, switch, quantity-stepper, range-slider
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/slider (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/slider.md)

Props (also accepts SliderPrimitive.Root props):

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| format? | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions \| ((value: number) => string)` |  | Formats the value in the bubble and for screen readers. |
| marks? | `Mark[]` |  | Ticks under the rail. Pass `{ value, label }` to caption them. |
| showValue? | `boolean` | `true` | Show the value above the thumb while dragging or focused. |

```tsx
<Slider aria-label="Volume" defaultValue={40} />
<Slider aria-label="Price" defaultValue={[20, 80]} format={{ style: "currency", currency: "USD" }} marks={[0, 50, 100]} />
```

### SocialAuthRow

### SortableHeader

A table column header button that shows and toggles sort direction (none, ascending, descending).

Put it inside a `<TableHead>` and set `aria-sort` on that header cell to match ("ascending" | "descending" | "none"); screen readers read sort state from the cell. Use TableToolbar for filters and search above the table.

- Name: `sortable-header` (component, Tables)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/sortable-header` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { SortableHeader } from "@/components/ui/sortable-header"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/sortable-header"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Related: table, table-toolbar, sql-result-table
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/sortable-header (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/sortable-header.md)

Props (also accepts <button>):

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `string` |  | Column name. |
| direction? | `"asc" \| "desc" \| false` |  | Current sort; `false` or undefined means unsorted. |
| onToggle? | `() => void` |  | Called on click; cycle the direction in your state. |

```tsx
<TableHead aria-sort={dir === "asc" ? "ascending" : dir === "desc" ? "descending" : "none"}>
  <SortableHeader label="Amount" direction={dir} onToggle={cycle} />
</TableHead>
```

### SortableList

A drag-to-reorder list: drag the grip handle, or focus it and use the arrow keys; every move is announced and the new order comes back through onReorder.

Use it for short lists people order by hand: priorities, playlist tracks, checklist steps. Every row is rendered, so keep it to a few dozen items. Built on Motion's Reorder. `KanbanBoard` shows cards in columns but cannot drag them; for a fixed order use a plain list.

Keyboard: Arrow Up/Down move one place, Home/End move to the ends; focus stays on the moved handle. Pass a new `items` array (different ids or order) to reset the list from outside.

- Name: `sortable-list` (component, Workflow)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/sortable-list` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { SortableList } from "@/components/ui/sortable-list"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/ui/sortable-list"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Related: kanban-board
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/sortable-list (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/sortable-list.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items? | `Item[]` | `DEMO` | Rows in their starting order. Defaults to a short sample task list. |
| onReorder? | `(items: Item[]) => void` |  | Called with the full list after every drag or keyboard move. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<SortableList items={tasks} onReorder={(next) => saveOrder(next.map((t) => t.id))} />
```

### SourceCard

A citation card for AI answers and RAG results: source title, its URL or path in mono, and a quoted snippet.

Show one per retrieved source under an AI answer, or inside a popover opened from a `CitationChip`. When `href` is set the title becomes a link that opens in a new tab; `url` is display text only. Every prop has a sample default, so pass `title`, `url` and `snippet`. For a numbered inline reference inside the answer text use `CitationChip`.

- Name: `source-card` (component, AI chat)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/source-card` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`

- Uses: badge
- Related: citation-chip, file-reference, link-preview
