### CtaBand

The closing call to action of a landing page: a big lit panel, a headline that catches the light, and an email field whose button morphs into a confirmation.

Use as the last section before the footer when the ask is "leave your email". For a plain row with one button use CtaBanner; for a premium glow panel use CtaGlow. `onSubmit` may return a promise: the button shows "Sending…" until it settles, "Check your inbox" on success, and an error line if it throws. Result is announced to screen readers.

- Name: `cta-band` (block, Landing pages)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/cta-band` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { CtaBand } from "@/components/ui/cta-band"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/blocks/cta-band"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Related: cta-banner, cta-glow, marketing-landing
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/cta-band (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/cta-band.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title? | `React.ReactNode` | `( <> Know what changed <br /> <span c...` | Headline (rendered as h2). Wrap a phrase in `<span className="text-lit">` to make it catch the light. |
| description? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Connect a source and get your first ...` | One or two sentences under the headline. |
| placeholder? | `string` | `"you@company.com"` | Email input placeholder. |
| button? | `string` | `"Start free"` | Submit button label at rest. |
| success? | `string` | `"Check your inbox"` | Button label after a successful submit. |
| onSubmit? | `(email: string) => void \| Promise<void>` |  | Called with the email on submit. Return a promise to show the busy state; throw to show the error line. |
| note? | `React.ReactNode` | `"No card. Cancel in one click."` | Small print under the form. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<CtaBand title="Ship it this week." onSubmit={(email) => fetch("/api/waitlist", { method: "POST", body: email })} />
```

### DeviceFrame

A phone or a browser window around live UI, with a lit bezel edge and a glass sheen that follow the light.

Use in heroes, feature rows and scroll stories to show real product UI instead of a screenshot. The phone is a fixed 300×630px frame (scale it with a transform class); the browser fills its container width. Children render inside the screen and stay interactive. For a static image use a plain <img>; for several overlapping devices use the premium DeviceStack.

- Name: `device-frame` (block, Media)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/device-frame` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { DeviceFrame } from "@/components/ui/device-frame"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/blocks/device-frame"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Related: hero-spotlight, scroll-story
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/device-frame (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/device-frame.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| device? | `"phone" \| "browser"` |  | Which frame to draw. |
| url? | `string` |  | Address bar text (browser only). Not a link. |
| time? | `string` |  | Status bar time (phone only). |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  | The UI shown on the screen. Defaults to a placeholder. |
| className? | `string` |  | Classes for the outer frame, e.g. a scale transform. |
| screenClassName? | `string` |  | Classes for the screen area that holds `children`. |

```tsx
<DeviceFrame device="browser" url="app.lumen.io/revenue"><DashboardHome /></DeviceFrame>
<DeviceFrame device="phone" time="09:41"><NotificationCenter /></DeviceFrame>
```

### FaqSection

A landing-page FAQ: a heading column with a contact line beside a one-open-at-a-time accordion.

Use near the end of a marketing page, before the closing CTA. Answers open by animating grid rows (no measuring) and the plus turns into a cross. Keyboard follows the WAI-ARIA accordion pattern: Enter/Space toggles, Arrow Up/Down move between questions, Home/End jump to the first/last. Closed answers are inert. For an in-app collapsible list use Accordion.

- Name: `faq-section` (block, Landing pages)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/faq-section` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`

- Related: accordion, marketing-landing
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/faq-section (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/faq-section.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| eyebrow? | `string` | `"FAQ"` | Small mono label above the title. Empty string hides it. |
| title? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Questions, answered."` | Section heading (rendered as h2). |
| description? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Something else on your mind? Write t...` | Line under the heading, e.g. how to reach a person. |
| items? | `Faq[]` | `ITEMS` | Questions in order. Defaults to Lumen's FAQ. |
| defaultOpen? | `number \| null` | `0` | Index of the question open on first render; `null` starts all closed. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<FaqSection items={[{ q: "Do you store our data?", a: "Only aggregates, encrypted at rest." }]} />
```

### FloatingNav

A sticky marketing header that tucks into a floating raised pill once you scroll, with a hover highlight that glides between links.

Use at the top of a landing page, above HeroSpotlight. It tracks window scroll. Below md the links move into a menu sheet: the toggle has aria-expanded/aria-controls, Escape closes it and returns focus, and choosing a link closes it. For an app shell with a sidebar use Topbar or Sidebar; for in-page section tabs use Tabs.

- Name: `floating-nav` (block, Navigation)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/floating-nav` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { FloatingNav } from "@/components/ui/floating-nav"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/blocks/floating-nav"`)

- Uses: button

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| brand? | `React.ReactNode` | `( <span className="flex items-center ...` | Logo or wordmark at the left. Defaults to the Lumen wordmark. |
| brandHref? | `string` | `"/"` | Where the brand links to. |
| links? | `NavLink[]` | `LINKS` | Primary navigation links. |
| cta? | `{ label: string; href?: string; onClick?: () => void }` | `{ label: "Start free" }` | Solid button at the right. Renders as a link when `href` is set. |
| secondary? | `{ label: string; href?: string } \| null` | `{ label: "Sign in", href: "#" }` | Ghost link before the CTA, hidden on the smallest screens. Pass null to remove it. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<FloatingNav links={[{ label: "Pricing", href: "#pricing" }]} cta={{ label: "Start free", href: "/signup" }} />
```

### FormWizard

A multi-step form: a stepper, one group of fields per step, Back/Next, a review step and a done state.

Use when a form is long enough to split (connect a data source, create an account). Each step validates with the browser's own `required` checks before moving on, and focus moves to the new step's heading so screen readers hear where they are. For a first-run checklist with progress use OnboardingFlow; for one short form use FormField.

- Name: `form-wizard` (block, Forms)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/form-wizard` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`

- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/form-wizard (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/form-wizard.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onComplete? | `(values: FormWizardValues) => void` |  | Called with every field's value when the review step is submitted. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<FormWizard onComplete={(v) => api.sources.create(v)} />
```

### HeroSpotlight

A launch hero: a staggered h1 that settles in with a blur, a lit second line, two actions, a proof line and a product visual that rises last.

Use as the first section of a landing page (it renders the page's h1, so use it once). Pair `visual` with a DeviceFrame wrapping real UI. Entrance motion is skipped under reduced motion. For a plain hero with no motion use Hero; for premium backgrounds use HeroAurora. Actions render as links when `href` is set, buttons otherwise.

- Name: `hero-spotlight` (block, Landing pages)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |

| title? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Answers from your data,"` | First line of the h1. |
| highlight? | `React.ReactNode` | `"before you ask."` | Second line of the title, lit by the cursor. |
| description? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Lumen watches revenue, churn and pip...` | Paragraph under the title. |
| primary? | `HeroAction` | `{ label: "Start free" }` | Main call to action, solid with an arrow. |
| secondary? | `HeroAction` | `{ label: "Watch the 2 min tour" }` | Second call to action, outline. |
| proof? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Free for 14 days · No card · SOC 2 T...` | Small proof line under the actions. |
| visual? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Product visual (a DeviceFrame, a screenshot, anything). |
| align? | `"center" \| "left"` | `"center"` | Text alignment of the copy block. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<HeroSpotlight
  title="Answers from your data,"

/>
```

### MediaLibrary

A files panel: title with an Upload button that opens the system file picker, then a responsive grid of file rows.

Use for attachments, exports or brand assets shared by a workspace. Picked files are added to the top of the list (no network); wire `onUpload` to send them. For drag-and-drop with progress use FileDropzone; for a single file use FileRow; for a folder hierarchy use FileTree.

- Name: `media-library` (block, Media)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/media-library` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onUpload? | `(files: File[]) => void` |  | Called with the files the user picked. |

### PricingPlans

A public pricing section: a monthly/yearly switch whose prices roll digit by digit, a featured plan in ink, and plain yes/no feature rows.

Use on a marketing or /pricing page with two to four plans. Prices are numbers per month; the yearly figure is the monthly-equivalent price and the "Billed $X yearly" line is derived. A price of 0 reads "Free". For an existing customer's plan and invoices use BillingPage; for a premium animated variant use PricingMotion. Period is uncontrolled by default; pass `period` + `onPeriodChange` to control it.

- Name: `pricing-plans` (block, Billing)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/pricing-plans` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { PricingPlans } from "@/components/ui/pricing-plans"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/blocks/pricing-plans"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Uses: button, number-roll, segmented-control
- Related: billing-page, pricing-motion, commerce-checkout, marketing-landing
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/pricing-plans (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/pricing-plans.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| eyebrow? | `string` | `"Pricing"` | Small mono label above the title. Empty string hides it. |
| title? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Priced like a tool, not a hire."` | Section heading (rendered as h2). |
| description? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Per seat, per month. Change plans an...` |  |
| plans? | `Plan[]` | `DEFAULT_PLANS` | Plans in display order. Defaults to Lumen's Starter, Team and Scale. |
| currency? | `string` | `"USD"` | ISO 4217 code used to format prices, e.g. "USD", "EUR". |
| yearlyBadge? | `string` | `"-20%"` | Discount badge on the yearly option. |
| onSelect? | `(plan: string, period: BillingPeriod) => void` |  | Called with the plan name and the selected period when a plan's button is pressed. |
| period? | `BillingPeriod` |  | Controlled billing period. |
| defaultPeriod? | `BillingPeriod` | `"yearly"` | Initial billing period when uncontrolled. |
| onPeriodChange? | `(period: BillingPeriod) => void` |  | Called when the period switch changes. |
| unit? | `string` | `"/ seat / mo"` | Price suffix, e.g. "/ seat / mo" or "/ mo". |
| per? | `string` | `"per seat"` | Used in "Billed $X per seat yearly". Empty string drops it. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<PricingPlans
  plans={[{ name: "Team", blurb: "For finance teams", monthly: 49, yearly: 39, cta: "Start trial", featured: true, features: ["Unlimited workspaces"] }]}
  onSelect={(plan, period) => router.push(`/signup?plan=${plan}&period=${period}`)}
/>
```

### ScrollStory

A "how it works" section: numbered steps on one side, a pinned visual on the other that swaps as each step reaches mid-screen, with a filling progress rail.

Use for a 3–5 step explanation on a landing page. On large screens the visual is sticky; below lg each step shows its own visual inline, so nothing is lost on mobile. Each `visual` should be a compact panel (a DeviceFrame scaled down, a card). Swaps are instant under reduced motion. For a static grid of features use BentoLive.

- Name: `scroll-story` (block, Landing pages)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/scroll-story` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ScrollStory } from "@/components/ui/scroll-story"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/blocks/scroll-story"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Related: device-frame, bento-live
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/scroll-story (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/scroll-story.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| eyebrow? | `string` | `"How it works"` | Small mono label above the title. Empty string hides it. |
| title? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Live in an afternoon."` | Section heading (rendered as h2). |
| steps? | `Step[]` | `STEPS` | Steps in order. Defaults to Lumen's connect, learn, tell story. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ScrollStory steps={[{ kicker: "01 · Connect", title: "Point it at your tools.", body: "Read-only keys.", visual: <MyPanel /> }]} />
```

### SignInPage

A centred sign-in screen: GitHub and Google buttons, an "or" divider, then email and password in a real form.

Use as the whole /sign-in route. Fields carry `autoComplete` so password managers fill them, and Enter submits. For just the card use AuthCard; for one-time codes use OtpInput. Wire `onSubmit` to your auth call.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/sign-in-page` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`

- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/sign-in-page (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/sign-in-page.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onSubmit? | `(values: { email: string; password: string }) => void \| Promise<void>` |  | Called with the entered credentials when the form is submitted. If the promise rejects, a danger InlineAlert shows above the button. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<SignInPage onSubmit={({ email, password }) => signIn(email, password)} />
```

### SocialProofWall

A customer section: a logo marquee that fades at the edges, then a wall of quotes in up to three columns drifting at different speeds.

Use once on a landing page, after the product sections. Motion pauses on hover and with the "Pause motion" button (WCAG 2.2.2), and stops entirely under reduced motion; duplicated copies used for the loop are hidden from screen readers. The default logos and quotes are fictional samples: always pass your own real customers. For a single featured quote use a Testimonial; for a static logo row use LogoCloud.

### WorkflowBoard

An approvals page: the request in focus with key, due date and priority, its approval card, and the queue behind it.

Use for finance or ops sign-off flows (refunds, credits, price changes). Approving or rejecting moves the queue on. For a kanban of many tasks use a board of Cards; for a one-off confirmation use AlertDialog. Composes IssueKey, DueDateChip, PriorityPicker and ApprovalCard.

- Name: `workflow-board` (block, Workflow)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/workflow-board` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { WorkflowBoard } from "@/components/ui/workflow-board"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/blocks/workflow-board"`)
- Uses: approval-card, due-date-chip, issue-key, page-header, priority-picker, status-badge
- Related: alert-dialog, issue-key, due-date-chip, priority-picker, approval-card
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/workflow-board (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/workflow-board.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onDecision? | `(key: string, approved: boolean, priority: string) => void` |  | Called with the request key, the decision and the priority set for it when Approve or Reject is pressed. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<WorkflowBoard onDecision={(key, approved, priority) => api.approvals.decide(key, approved, priority)} />
```

### AnimatedBeam

Light that travels along curved paths between elements, showing data flowing from sources into a hub and out to a result.

Paths are measured from the real DOM, so the diagram reflows with its container. `AnimatedBeam` is a ready-made "inputs → hub → output" diagram; `Beam` is the primitive that connects any two refs in your own layout. Use it for integration and pipeline diagrams; for a lit box outline use BorderBeam instead. Reduced motion keeps the static path and drops the light.

- Name: `animated-beam` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/animated-beam` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { AnimatedBeam, Beam } from "@/components/ui/animated-beam"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/animated-beam"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Related: border-beam, orbiting-circles
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/animated-beam (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/animated-beam.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| inputs? | `Node[]` | `[ { icon: MailIcon, label: "Email" },...` | Sources on the left, each joined to the hub by a beam. Labels must be unique. |
| hub? | `Node` | `{ icon: BotIcon, label: "Agent" }` | The centre node, drawn larger in ink. |
| output? | `Node` | `{ icon: UserIcon, label: "Customer" }` | The node on the right that the hub flows into. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<AnimatedBeam hub={{ icon: BotIcon, label: "Agent" }} output={{ icon: UserIcon, label: "Customer" }} />
```

```tsx
// Your own layout: the container must be position: relative.
<div ref={box} className="relative">… <Beam container={box} from={a} to={b} curvature={-24} /></div>
```

### AnimatedFeatureRow

A row of feature cards that rise into view one after another as the row scrolls on screen.

### AnimatedList

A live activity feed where new items drop in at the top on a spring and older ones slide down and fall off the end.

Use it for "happening now" sections, notification previews and activity streams on marketing pages. Items cycle through `items` on a timer while the list is on screen, and pause while the pointer is over it or it has keyboard focus (the list is a tab stop, named by `label`). Reduced motion shows the first `max` items, still. For a static list of notifications use a plain list; for a one-off reveal use BlurFade.

- Name: `animated-list` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/animated-list` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { AnimatedList } from "@/components/ui/animated-list"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/animated-list"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Related: blur-fade
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/animated-list (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/animated-list.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items? | `ListItem[]` | `DEFAULT` | Items to cycle through, newest first. |
| interval? | `number` | `1800` | Milliseconds between arrivals. |
| max? | `number` | `4` | How many items to keep on screen. |
| label? | `string` | `"Live activity"` | Accessible name for the list, which is a tab stop so keyboard users can pause it. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<AnimatedList max={4} interval={2000} items={[{ title: "Payment received", detail: "Acme paid $2,400", time: "now" }]} />
```

### AnimatedTabs

Tabs with a pill that slides between triggers and panels that cross-fade in the direction of travel.

Follows the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: roving focus, Arrow keys, Home and End, automatic activation. Pass `tabs` as data (id, label, content). Works uncontrolled (`defaultValue`) or controlled (`value` + `onValueChange`). Use it for a marketing or overview panel with a few views; for app navigation tabs built from parts use Tabs, and for a compact toggle between options use SegmentedControl.

- Name: `animated-tabs` (motion, Navigation)

- Dependencies: motion
- Related: tabs, segmented-control, before-after-wipe
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/animated-tabs (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/animated-tabs.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tabs? | `Tab[]` | `DEMO` |  |
| value? | `string` |  | Active tab id when controlled. |
| defaultValue? | `string` |  | Initial tab id when uncontrolled. Defaults to the first tab. |
| onValueChange? | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called with the new tab id on click or arrow key. |
| label? | `string` | `"Sections"` | Accessible name of the tab list. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<AnimatedTabs
  label="Account"
  tabs={[
    { id: "overview", label: "Overview", content: <p>Revenue is up 12.4%.</p> },

  ]}
/>
```

### AnimatedTooltip

A row of overlapping avatars where hovering or focusing one pops up a name and role card that leans and slides with the pointer.

The card rises on a spring, tilts a few degrees toward the pointer as it crosses the face, and settles back when it leaves. Keyboard focus opens the same card centred; Escape closes it; a tap toggles it on touch. Reduced motion shows and hides the card instantly with no tilt. Use it for team, contributor or "who's online" rows; for a tooltip on any trigger use Tooltip, and for a plain stacked row use AvatarGroup.

- Name: `animated-tooltip` (motion, Overlays)

- Dependencies: motion
- Related: tooltip, avatar-group

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| people? | `AnimatedTooltipPerson[]` |  | People to show, left to right. Defaults to a five-person sample team. |
| size? | `number` | `44` | Avatar diameter in pixels. |
| defaultActive? | `number` |  | Index of a card to show before any hover. Defaults to the second person for the built-in sample only. |
| onSelect? | `(person: AnimatedTooltipPerson, index: number) => void` |  | Called when an avatar is clicked or activated with the keyboard. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<AnimatedTooltip people={[{ name: "Maya Chen", role: "Founder", src: "/maya.jpg" }, { name: "Theo Okafor", role: "Engineering" }]} />
```

### AuroraBackground

Soft northern-lights curtains that drift and sway across the panel behind your content. Three blurred bands of accent colour move at different periods, so the motion never reads as a loop. The light sits behind the content, ignores the pointer, pauses off screen and holds still for reduced motion.

Use it as a hero or CTA backdrop; children render on top. For a static glow use HeroGradientMesh, for a pointer-reactive grid use BackgroundBoxes.

- Name: `aurora-background` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/aurora-background` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { AuroraBackground } from "@/components/ui/aurora-background"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/aurora-background"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Uses: button
- Related: hero-gradient-mesh, background-boxes, hero-aurora, light-field, wavy-background
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/aurora-background (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/aurora-background.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| intensity? | `number` | `1` | Strength of the light, 0 to 1. |
| speed? | `number` | `1` | Speed multiplier. 2 is twice as fast, 0.5 half as fast. |
| blur? | `number` | `28` | Softness of the bands in pixels. |
| colors? | `string[]` | `["var(--accent)", "var(--accent-2)", ...` | Colours of the bands. Any CSS colour, including var(--token). |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |

```tsx
<AuroraBackground intensity={0.8} className="h-[480px]">
  <h1 className="text-4xl text-fg">See your runway in a new light</h1>
</AuroraBackground>
```

### BackgroundBoxes

A skewed grid of hairline boxes behind your content where the box under the pointer lights up in colour and fades out behind it. One pointer handler maps the cursor into the skewed grid with a little matrix maths and writes the colour straight to the box, so React never re-renders a box. Neighbours catch a softer glow. It works through the content on top and with touch. Left alone, a box lights now and then so the panel looks alive; that idle flicker pauses off screen and stops for reduced motion, and the fade is instant for reduced motion too.

Use it as an interactive hero backdrop; children render on top. For quiet ambient motion use FlickeringGrid or AuroraBackground instead.

- Name: `background-boxes` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/background-boxes` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { BackgroundBoxes } from "@/components/ui/background-boxes"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/background-boxes"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Uses: button
- Related: flickering-grid, aurora-background, dot-pattern, retro-grid
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/background-boxes (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/background-boxes.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| density? | `number` | `1` | Box density. 1 draws 64px boxes, 2 draws them half the size. |
| colors? | `string[]` | `["var(--accent)", "var(--accent-2)", ...` | Colours the boxes light up in. Any CSS colour, including var(--token). |
| fade? | `number` | `1.6` | Seconds a lit box takes to fade back. |
| idle? | `number` | `2` | Boxes that light on their own each second while nobody hovers. 0 turns the idle flicker off. |
| skew? | `[number, number]` | `[-24, 12]` | Tilt of the grid in degrees: skew along x, then along y. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |

```tsx
<BackgroundBoxes density={1.5} idle={0}>
  <h1 className="text-4xl text-fg">Built on a grid you can feel</h1>
</BackgroundBoxes>
```

### BeforeAfterWipe

A before and after comparison: drag the divider (or use the arrow keys) to wipe between two layers.

The divider is a real range input under the hood, so it is keyboard and screen reader operable (Arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up/Down). Pass any content as `before` and `after` (screenshots, mockups, two renders of a component); with neither it shows a sample dashboard. Works uncontrolled (`defaultValue`) or controlled (`value` + `onValueChange`). Use it for redesigns, filters and "with vs without" proof; for flipping between more than two states use AnimatedTabs.

- Name: `before-after-wipe` (motion, Media)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/before-after-wipe` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { BeforeAfterWipe } from "@/components/ui/before-after-wipe"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/before-after-wipe"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Related: animated-tabs, filmstrip-scrub, scratch-to-reveal
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/before-after-wipe (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/before-after-wipe.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Content of the left (before) layer. |
| after? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Content of the right (after) layer, revealed as the divider moves left. |
| beforeLabel? | `string` | `"Generic dashboard"` | Name of the before layer, shown on the sample and read to screen readers. |
| afterLabel? | `string` | `"Redesigned"` | Name of the after layer. |
| value? | `number` |  | Divider position in percent (0 shows only after, 100 only before) when controlled. |
| defaultValue? | `number` | `50` | Initial divider position in percent when uncontrolled. |
| onValueChange? | `(value: number) => void` |  | Called with the new divider position in percent. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<BeforeAfterWipe
  beforeLabel="Before"
  afterLabel="After"
  before={<img src="/old.png" alt="" className="size-full object-cover" />}
  after={<img src="/new.png" alt="" className="size-full object-cover" />}
/>
```

### BlurFade

Reveals its children as they scroll into view, rising out of a soft blur and settling into focus on a spring. Wrap each item of a list and grow the `delay` to stagger them. Reduced motion shows everything in place at once.

Use it for scroll reveals of cards, sections and images on marketing pages. Product UI should not animate on load (law 5), so keep it out of app chrome. With no children it renders a sample grid of six feature cards.

- Name: `blur-fade` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/blur-fade` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { BlurFade } from "@/components/ui/blur-fade"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/blur-fade"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Related: animated-feature-row, animated-list, scroll-reveal, text-reveal
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/blur-fade (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/blur-fade.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |
| delay? | `number` | `0` | Seconds to wait before the reveal starts; grow it per item to stagger a list. |
| duration? | `number` | `0.5` | Seconds the reveal takes. |
| direction? | `"up" \| "down" \| "left" \| "right" \| "none"` | `"up"` | Which way the content travels as it settles. |
| offset? | `number` | `16` | Pixels of travel. |
| blur? | `number` | `8` | Blur in pixels the content starts from. |
| once? | `boolean` | `true` | Reveal once, or again every time it enters the viewport. |
| amount? | `number` | `0.3` | How much of the element has to be visible before it reveals, 0 to 1. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
{features.map((f, i) => (
  <BlurFade key={f.id} delay={i * 0.08} direction="up">
    <FeatureCard {...f} />
  </BlurFade>
))}
```

### BorderBeam

A short beam of light that travels around the border of any box to mark the one thing that matters.

Wrap a card, input or pricing tier with it. The beam is a rotating conic gradient masked to the border ring, so the content inside is untouched; it animates transform only and holds still for reduced motion. Set `radius` to match the child's corner radius. For light flowing between elements use AnimatedBeam; for a static highlight use a `border-accent` ring.

- Name: `border-beam` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/border-beam` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { BorderBeam } from "@/components/ui/border-beam"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/border-beam"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Related: animated-beam, shimmer-button, shine-border
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/border-beam (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/border-beam.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |
| duration? | `number` | `6` | Seconds per lap. |
| width? | `number` | `1.5` | Border width in pixels. |
| length? | `number` | `0.18` | Beam length, as a fraction of the lap, 0 to 1. |
| radius? | `number` | `18` | Corner radius in pixels; match the wrapped element. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<BorderBeam radius={12} duration={8}>
  <Card className="w-80">…</Card>
</BorderBeam>
```

### BrowserMockup

A browser window frame with traffic lights, back and forward buttons, an address bar and optional tabs, wrapping your screenshot or any children. PhoneMockup, exported from the same file, is the matching handset with a dynamic island and rounded screen. Both are built from tokens, so they follow light, dark and every material. With no content, the browser shows a Lumen dashboard made of plain divs, with a phone over its corner on wide screens and below it on narrow ones. With your own content, `phone` shows `phoneContent` on the handset.

Use it to frame product screenshots on landing pages, docs and changelogs. For several tilted frames at once use DeviceFrameStack.

- Name: `browser-mockup` (motion, Landing pages)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/browser-mockup` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { BrowserMockup, PhoneMockup } from "@/components/ui/browser-mockup"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/browser-mockup"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Related: device-frame-stack, aspect-ratio, window-chrome, hero-split-showcase, product-os-mock
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/browser-mockup (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/browser-mockup.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| url? | `string` | `"https://app.lumen.dev/overview"` | Address shown in the URL bar. |
| tabs? | `string[]` | `[]` | Tab labels. The strip is hidden when empty. |
| activeTab? | `number` | `0` | Index of the active tab. |
| src? | `string` |  | Screenshot to show instead of children. |
| alt? | `string` | `""` |  |
| appearance? | `"auto" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Stay dark in both themes, or follow the page theme. |
| phone? | `boolean` |  | Render a PhoneMockup beside the window. Defaults to on for the built-in sample only. |
| phoneContent? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Screen for the phone when `phone` is on. Defaults to the sample screen with no `src` or children, and an empty screen otherwise. |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx

```

```tsx

```

### CardTilt

A card that tilts in 3D toward a mouse pointer, with an accent glare that follows it.

Tilt and glare run on motion values, so moving the pointer never re-renders React. Mouse only: touch and keyboard see a flat card, and reduced motion keeps it flat too. Pass `children` for your own content, or `title` and `body` for the built-in layout. Use it for a featured card or showcase tile on marketing pages; for a flat spotlight panel use CursorSpotlightPanel, and keep it out of product UI.

- Name: `card-tilt` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/card-tilt` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`

### CommandWaitlist

A terminal-styled waitlist card with a monospace email field and a Join button that springs into view as it scrolls on screen.

Handles its own pending, success and error states and announces them to screen readers. Pass `onSubmit` to send the address anywhere; it may return a promise, and a thrown error shows `errorMessage` and keeps the address so nothing typed is lost. Use it for a launch or beta waitlist; for a newsletter row in a footer use a plain Input and Button.

- Name: `command-waitlist` (motion, Landing pages)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/command-waitlist` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { CommandWaitlist } from "@/components/ui/command-waitlist"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/command-waitlist"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Uses: button
- Related: input, button, waitlist-hero
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/command-waitlist (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/command-waitlist.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| product? | `string` | `"Lumen 2.0"` | Product name in the title bar. |
| onSubmit? | `(email: string) => void \| Promise<unknown>` |  | Called with the trimmed email. Return a promise to show a pending state; throw to show the error. |
| successMessage? | `string` | `"Queued. We will ping you."` | Line shown after a successful submit. |
| errorMessage? | `string` | `"Could not join. Check the address an...` | Line shown when onSubmit throws. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<CommandWaitlist product="Lumen 2.0" onSubmit={(email) => fetch("/api/waitlist", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ email }) })} />
```

### ConfettiButton

A button that bursts confetti from itself on click, for celebrating a finished action.

A few dozen paper pieces with gravity, drag and spin are drawn on a throwaway canvas and cleaned up when they land; physics are time based, so 60 and 120Hz screens fall at the same speed. No library. Reduced motion skips the burst and keeps the click. It takes every native button prop. Use it for "you did it" moments (first invoice sent, plan upgraded), not for routine saves; for a normal action use Button.

- Name: `confetti-button` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/confetti-button` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ConfettiButton } from "@/components/ui/confetti-button"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/confetti-button"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Related: button, sparkles-text
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/confetti-button (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/confetti-button.md)

Props (also accepts <button>):

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| count? | `number` | `70` | Number of pieces per burst. |
| colors? | `string[]` |  | Piece colours, any CSS colour. Defaults to the accent, accent-2, success, warning and info tokens. |

```tsx
<ConfettiButton onClick={publish}>Publish</ConfettiButton>
```

### CursorSpotlightPanel

A sunken panel with a soft accent spotlight that follows the pointer across it.

The spotlight runs on motion values over the panel's own surface, so it never re-renders React and the material still reaches the background. Touch and reduced motion get a still glow. ### Dock

A macOS style dock where icons swell as the pointer passes over them, with a label above the one under the pointer.

Every item is a real button (with `onClick`) or link (with `href`), reachable and labelled for keyboard and screen reader users; focus shows the label too. Magnification is pointer only and off for reduced motion. Use it for an app launcher or a playful bottom nav on marketing pages; for product navigation use a sidebar or Tabs.

- Name: `dock` (motion, Navigation)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/dock` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`

| label? | `string` | `"Dock"` | Accessible name of the dock's nav landmark. |
| size? | `number` | `44` | Resting icon size in pixels. |
| magnify? | `number` | `68` | Size under the pointer. |
| distance? | `number` | `130` | How far the swell reaches, in pixels. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<Dock items={[{ label: "Home", icon: HomeIcon, href: "/", active: true }, { label: "Mail", icon: MailIcon, onClick: openMail }]} />
```

### DotPattern

A background of dots or grid lines drawn as one SVG pattern, faded at the edges, with an optional glow that lights the pattern under the pointer.

The pattern sits behind your children with pointer-events off. The glow writes CSS variables on pointer move, so React never re-renders while it follows; it is off for reduced motion. Use it as a quiet section or hero backdrop; for animated texture use FlickeringGrid, for a reactive grid of boxes use BackgroundBoxes.

- Name: `dot-pattern` (motion, Layout)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/dot-pattern` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { DotPattern } from "@/components/ui/dot-pattern"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/dot-pattern"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Related: flickering-grid, background-boxes, particles, retro-grid
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/dot-pattern (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/dot-pattern.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| variant? | `"dots" \| "grid"` | `"dots"` | Dots at each cell centre, or hairline grid lines. |
| gap? | `number` | `18` | Cell size in pixels. |
| weight? | `number` | `1` | Dot radius or line width. |
| glow? | `boolean` | `true` | Light the pattern under the pointer. |
| fade? | `boolean` | `true` | Fade the edges with a radial mask. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |

```tsx
<DotPattern variant="grid" gap={24} className="h-[420px]">
  <h2 className="text-3xl text-fg">Every pixel, accounted for</h2>
</DotPattern>
```

### FaqAccordionMotion

A single-open FAQ accordion whose answers spring open and close faster, with a plus that turns into a minus.

Follows the WAI-ARIA accordion pattern: each question is a button inside a heading, with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at a labelled region. One answer is open at a time; clicking the open one closes it. Reduced motion opens and closes instantly. Use it for a marketing FAQ; for multi-open disclosure in product UI use Accordion.

- Name: `faq-accordion-motion` (motion, Landing pages)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| rows? | `Row[]` | `SAMPLE_ROWS` | One row per feature. A boolean renders a check or a dash, a string renders as text. |
| label? | `string` | `"Free and Premium features compared"` | Accessible name of the table. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<FeatureComparison rows={[{ feature: "Team seats", free: "2", premium: "Unlimited" }, { feature: "SSO", free: false, premium: true }]} />
```

### FilmstripScrub

A frame viewer with a strip of thumbnails and a scrub slider below it; pick a thumbnail or drag the slider to change the frame.

The slider is a native range input (arrow keys, Home, End) and the strip keeps the current thumbnail scrolled into view. Pass `renderFrame` to draw your own frame (a video still, a step of an animation); without it the viewer shows the frame number. Works uncontrolled (`defaultValue`) or controlled (`value` + `onValueChange`). Use it to step through a sequence; for comparing two states use BeforeAfterWipe.

- Name: `filmstrip-scrub` (motion, Media)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/filmstrip-scrub` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { FilmstripScrub } from "@/components/ui/filmstrip-scrub"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/filmstrip-scrub"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Related: before-after-wipe
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/filmstrip-scrub (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/filmstrip-scrub.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| frames? | `number` | `12` | Number of frames. |
| value? | `number` |  | Selected frame index (0-based) when controlled. |
| defaultValue? | `number` | `3` | Initial frame index when uncontrolled. |
| onValueChange? | `(index: number) => void` |  | Called with the new frame index. |
| renderFrame? | `(index: number) => React.ReactNode` |  | Draws the selected frame in the viewer. Defaults to the frame number. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<FilmstripScrub frames={24} renderFrame={(i) => <img src={`/frames/${i}.jpg`} alt={`Frame ${i + 1}`} />} />
```

### FlickeringGrid

A canvas grid of small squares whose brightness flickers at random behind your content, like a board of quiet signals. Colour comes from the accent token and an optional radial mask fades the edges. The canvas is sharp on high density screens, resizes with its box, sleeps off screen and draws one still frame for reduced motion.

Use it as a calm, living hero or status backdrop; children render on top. For a pointer-reactive backdrop use BackgroundBoxes, for a still pattern use DotPattern.

- Name: `flickering-grid` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/flickering-grid` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { FlickeringGrid } from "@/components/ui/flickering-grid"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/flickering-grid"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Uses: button
- Related: background-boxes, dot-pattern, particles
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/flickering-grid (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/flickering-grid.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| squareSize? | `number` | `4` | Side of one square in pixels. |
| gap? | `number` | `6` | Space between squares in pixels. |
| flickerChance? | `number` | `0.4` | Chance per second that any one square changes brightness, 0 to 1. |
| maxOpacity? | `number` | `0.4` | Brightest a square can get, 0 to 1. |
| color? | `string` | `"var(--accent)"` | Any CSS colour, including var(--token). Defaults to the accent. |
| mask? | `"radial" \| "none"` | `"radial"` | Fade the grid toward the edges. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |

```tsx
<FlickeringGrid squareSize={4} gap={6} maxOpacity={0.3} className="h-[420px]">
  <h1 className="text-4xl text-fg">All systems normal</h1>
</FlickeringGrid>
```

### FlipStatBoard

A row of stat tiles whose digits count up on split-flap cards when the board scrolls into view.

Each digit is its own card that springs up as it changes, set in tabular mono so nothing shifts. Counting runs once, when the board is 60% on screen. Screen readers get the final value and label, never the count. Reduced motion shows the final numbers at once. Use it for a few headline metrics on a marketing or investor page; for a live number that changes in place use NumberRoll, and for a KPI card with trend use a stat card.

- Name: `flip-stat-board` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/flip-stat-board` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`

- Related: number-roll, investor-update, launch-countdown, metric-ticker-board
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/flip-stat-board (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/flip-stat-board.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| stats? | `FlipStat[]` | `[ { value: 1284, label: "Invoices pai...` | Stats to show, left to right. Two to four read best. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<FlipStatBoard stats={[{ value: 1284, label: "Invoices paid" }, { value: 312, label: "Teams" }]} />
```

### Globe

A dotted globe drawn on a plain canvas, no WebGL, that turns on its own and spins under your finger. Two thousand points sit on a sphere, rotate with simple trig and draw with depth shading. Markers take latitude and longitude, carry labels and are joined by arcs with a pulse travelling along each one. Drag to rotate with inertia, or focus the globe and use the arrow keys. Colours resolve through the cascade; the canvas is sharp on high density screens, sleeps off screen and draws one still frame for reduced motion. Content ignores the pointer where it is empty, so the globe stays draggable beside it.

Use it for "global reach" or "where your users are" sections. For a lighter decorative sphere of logos use IconCloud.

- Name: `globe` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/globe` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { Globe } from "@/components/ui/globe"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/globe"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Uses: button
- Related: icon-cloud
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/globe (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/globe.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| markers? | `GlobeMarker[]` | `DEFAULT_MARKERS` | Places to mark, in degrees. Consecutive markers are joined by arcs. |
| dots? | `number` | `2000` | Number of dots on the sphere. |
| speed? | `number` | `6` | Idle spin in degrees per second. 0 holds still until dragged. |
| arcs? | `boolean` | `true` | Join consecutive markers with arcs. |
| align? | `"left" \| "center" \| "right"` | `"right"` | Where the globe sits on wide panels. The demo content takes the other side. |
| color? | `string` | `"var(--fg-muted)"` | Dot colour. Any CSS colour, including var(--token). Defaults to the muted foreground. |
| accent? | `string` | `"var(--accent)"` | Marker, arc and glow colour. Any CSS colour. Defaults to the accent. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |

```tsx
<Globe markers={[{ lat: 51.51, lng: -0.13, label: "London" }, { lat: 40.71, lng: -74.0, label: "New York" }]} speed={4}>
  <h2 className="text-3xl text-fg">Settled locally, everywhere</h2>
</Globe>
```

### GradientText

Headline text filled with a slowly drifting gradient built from the accent tokens, so it follows your theme.

Stays a real text node for SEO and screen readers, and holds still for reduced motion. Marketing only: the design law bans gradient text in product UI. Use it for one hero word or line; for a scramble-in effect use HyperText.

String children get the display size (text-4xl, 5xl from sm); pass a `className` text size to override it.

- Name: `gradient-text` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/gradient-text` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { GradientText } from "@/components/ui/gradient-text"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/gradient-text"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Related: hyper-text, masked-gradient-headline, sparkles-text
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/gradient-text (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/gradient-text.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Ship the whole product"` |  |
| as? | `"span" \| "h1" \| "h2" \| "h3" \| "p"` | `"span"` | Element to render. Use a heading tag when the text is the heading itself. |
| duration? | `number` | `8` | Seconds per drift, one way. |
| colors? | `string[]` |  | Extra colour stops; defaults to accent, accent-2 and back. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<GradientText as="h2" duration={12}>Every pixel, accounted for</GradientText>
```

- Dependencies: motion

- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/horizontal-product-rail (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/horizontal-product-rail.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items? | `Item[]` | `[ { title: "AI Studio", blurb: "Compo...` |  |
| title? | `string` | `"Product surfaces"` | Visible heading above the rail. |
| ariaLabel? | `string` |  | Accessible name of the scrolling region. Defaults to the title. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<HorizontalProductRail title="Explore Lumen" items={[{ title: "Billing", blurb: "Plans, invoices, seats.", tag: "Commerce" }]} />
```

### HyperText

Text that decodes itself: every character cycles through random glyphs and locks into place from left to right. A violet scanning head marks the letter about to settle. It runs once when it scrolls into view and again on hover, set in monospace so nothing shifts while it runs. Screen readers only ever get the final text, and reduced motion shows it at once.

Use it for short headline moments (a tagline, a stat line); keep it under a line or two. For a headline that types word by word use HeroTypedHeadline, for a gradient fill use GradientText.

- Name: `hyper-text` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/hyper-text` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { HyperText } from "@/components/ui/hyper-text"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/hyper-text"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Related: text, hero-typed-headline, gradient-text, text-scramble, word-rotate
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/hyper-text (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/hyper-text.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| text? | `string` | `"Close the books in 24 hours"` |  |
| duration? | `number` | `1100` | Milliseconds for the whole line to settle. |
| characters? | `string` | `"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789...` | The pool of glyphs characters cycle through before they lock. |
| trigger? | `"mount" \| "hover" \| "both"` | `"both"` | When to run: the first time it is in view, on hover, or both. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<HyperText text="Close the books in 24 hours" trigger="both" className="text-4xl" />
```

### IconCloud

A sphere of icons that turns slowly in 3D, scales and fades with depth, and can be dragged to spin with inertia. Items sit on a Fibonacci sphere so they spread evenly, and each is a real element (lucide icons by default, or your children), so they stay crisp and take token colours. The sphere turns on its own, keeps spinning after a flick, pauses off screen and holds still for reduced motion. Arrow keys turn it when it has focus.

Use it for "works with everything" integration and stack sections. Items are decorative (hidden from screen readers), so say what they are in nearby text. For a world map of places use Globe.

- Name: `icon-cloud` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/icon-cloud` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { IconCloud } from "@/components/ui/icon-cloud"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/icon-cloud"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Related: globe, orbiting-circles
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/icon-cloud (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/icon-cloud.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Items to place on the sphere. Defaults to 30 lucide icons. |
| size? | `number` | `360` | Diameter in pixels. Shrinks to fit a narrower container. |
| speed? | `number` | `1` | Idle spin speed. 1 is one turn every 25 seconds, 0 holds still until dragged. |
| itemSize? | `number` | `48` | Size of each tile in pixels. |
| interactive? | `boolean` | `true` | Allow pointer drag and arrow keys to turn the sphere. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<IconCloud size={360} speed={0.8}>
  {logos.map((Logo) => <Logo key={Logo.name} className="size-6" />)}
</IconCloud>
```

### InvestorUpdate

| summary? | `string` | `"Lumen is invoicing and payments for ...` | Paragraph under the headline. |

### LampEffect

A glowing strip light at the top of a dark panel that switches on and widens to light the headline beneath it. The lamp is a thin bright line with a soft trapezoid of light falling from it. On first view the line stretches open and the light follows a beat later, with springs. The panel stays dark in both themes by default so the light has something to fall on; reduced motion shows the lamp already on.

Use it for one launch or release headline that should feel lit from above. Reach for CursorSpotlightPanel when the light should follow the pointer, and RetroGrid or Meteors when the backdrop itself should move.

- Name: `lamp-effect` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/lamp-effect` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { LampEffect } from "@/components/ui/lamp-effect"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/lamp-effect"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Uses: button
- Related: cursor-spotlight-panel, retro-grid, meteors
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/lamp-effect (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/lamp-effect.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| width? | `number` | `440` | Width of the lamp line in pixels. The light scales with it and never exceeds the panel. |
| color? | `string` | `"var(--accent)"` | Any CSS colour, including var(--token). Defaults to the accent. |
| glow? | `number` | `1` | Strength of the glow, 0 to 2. |
| dark? | `boolean` | `true` | Keep the panel dark in both themes. Turn off to follow the page theme. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Content lit by the lamp. Defaults to a sample Lumen release headline. |

```tsx
<LampEffect width={480} glow={1.2}>
  <h2 className="text-4xl font-medium text-fg">Close the books in minutes</h2>
</LampEffect>
```

### LaunchCountdown

A launch countdown in days, hours, minutes and seconds whose digits roll like an odometer, above a magnetic call to action. Pass `target` for a real launch date; without it the clock counts down `targetOffsetMs` from mount, which suits demos. Each digit springs to its place instead of swapping. The clock is a `timer` region: screen readers read the time left when they reach it but are not interrupted every second. Reduced motion swaps digits instantly.

Use it for a pre-launch or waitlist page. Reach for FlipStatBoard or StatsCounter for figures that do not tick, and NumberRoll for one number.

- Name: `launch-countdown` (motion, Landing pages)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/launch-countdown` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { LaunchCountdown } from "@/components/ui/launch-countdown"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/launch-countdown"`)
- Uses: magnetic-cta, number-roll
- Related: flip-stat-board, stats-counter, number-roll, waitlist-hero
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/launch-countdown (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/launch-countdown.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title? | `string` | `"Opens in"` | Label above the clock. |
| target? | `Date \| string \| number` |  | The moment the clock reaches zero: a Date, an ISO string or epoch milliseconds. Overrides `targetOffsetMs`. |
| targetOffsetMs? | `number` | `1000 * 60 * 60 * 36` | Without `target`, count down this many milliseconds from mount. |
| cta? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Join the waitlist"` | Call to action under the clock. Pass null to hide it. |
| onComplete? | `() => void` |  | Called once when the clock reaches zero. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<LaunchCountdown target="2026-12-01T09:00:00Z" title="Lumen 3.0 opens in" cta="Join the waitlist" />
```

### LightField

A living WebGL background of slow colour silk with a soft light that follows the cursor and fine film grain. Warped noise drifts slowly, the cursor carries a soft light through it, and fine grain keeps it from looking digital. It starts when the browser is idle, compiles its shader off the main thread where the GPU allows, renders at half resolution and 30 fps, fades in on its first frame, sleeps when off screen or in a background tab, stays empty without a real GPU (put a still behind it), and draws a single still frame for reduced motion. Glass surfaces placed over it frost it beautifully.

It fills its parent: put it in a sized, `relative` box with your content layered above. Reach for AuroraBackground or HeroGradientMesh for a CSS-only backdrop, and WavyBackground or Particles for a lighter canvas effect.

- Name: `light-field` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/light-field` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { LightField } from "@/components/ui/light-field"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/light-field"`)
- Related: aurora-background, hero-gradient-mesh, wavy-background, particles
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/light-field (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/light-field.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| palette? | `{ light?: Palette; dark?: Palette }` |  | Three RGB colours (0 to 1 per channel) per theme: base, partner and highlight. |
| fps? | `number` | `30` | Frames per second. The silk drifts slowly, so 30 looks the same as 60 for half the GPU work. |
| resolution? | `number` | `0.5` | Render scale in CSS pixels. The field is soft, so 0.5 (scaled up by the browser) is indistinguishable from full size. |

```tsx
<div className="relative h-[480px] overflow-hidden rounded-2xl">
  <LightField className="absolute inset-0" />
  <div className="relative z-10">…</div>
</div>
```

Cards rise with the morph spring as the rail scrolls into view; reduced motion shows them in place.

### LogoWallMotion

An endless, slowly scrolling strip of customer logos or names with soft faded edges, for social proof under a hero. The strip runs on the compositor (a CSS transform loop), pauses on hover and with the "Pause motion" button (WCAG 2.2.2), and holds still for reduced motion. Screen readers get the list once; the looping copy is hidden from them.

Use it for a "trusted by" row. Reach for LogoCloud for a static grid, HeroMarqueeBrands for a hero with a built-in brand strip, and MarqueeQuotes for scrolling testimonials. Pass your real customers: never invent logos.

- Name: `logo-wall-motion` (motion, Landing pages)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/logo-wall-motion` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { LogoWallMotion } from "@/components/ui/logo-wall-motion"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/logo-wall-motion"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react
- Uses: button
- Related: logo-cloud, hero-marquee-brands, marquee-quotes, live-component-rail, orbit-logo-cluster, typographic-marquee
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/logo-wall-motion (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/logo-wall-motion.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| logos? | `React.ReactNode[]` | `["Acme", "Globex", "Initech", "Umbrel...` | Names or logo elements, in order. Elements need their own accessible name (an img alt). |
| title? | `string` | `"Trusted by product teams"` | Label above the strip. Pass an empty string to hide it. |
| duration? | `number` | `28` | Seconds for one full loop. Higher is calmer. |
| reverse? | `boolean` | `false` | Scroll left to right instead. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<LogoWallMotion title="Trusted by finance teams" logos={["Northwind", "Contoso", <img key="a" src="/acme.svg" alt="Acme" className="h-6" />]} />
```

### MagneticCta

A call-to-action button that leans toward the pointer while the pointer is over it, like a magnet, and springs back when it leaves. It is the kit Button inside a wrapper that moves on a spring, so every Button prop (variant, size, render, onClick, disabled) works unchanged. Only a mouse or pen pulls it; touch and keyboard use it as a normal button, and reduced motion keeps it still.

Use it for the one primary action on a marketing section. Reach for Button everywhere in product UI, and ShimmerButton when the action should glow rather than move.

- Name: `magnetic-cta` (motion, Buttons)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/magnetic-cta` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { MagneticCta } from "@/components/ui/magnetic-cta"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/magnetic-cta"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Uses: button
- Related: button, shimmer-button, brand-kit-page, pricing-kinetic
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/magnetic-cta (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/magnetic-cta.md)

Props (also accepts Button props):

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| strength? | `number` | `28` | Furthest the button travels toward the pointer, in pixels. |

```tsx
<MagneticCta size="lg" strength={20} onClick={startTrial}>Start free trial</MagneticCta>
<MagneticCta render={<a href="/signup" />}>Get started</MagneticCta>
```

A large headline filled with an ink-to-violet gradient that wipes in from left to right as it scrolls into view. ### Meteors

Meteor streaks with fading tails that fall diagonally behind your content at random intervals. Each meteor takes a fresh path every time it comes round. The streaks sit behind the content, ignore the pointer, pause off screen and hold still for reduced motion.

Use it behind a dark, quiet hero or release announcement. Reach for Particles when the backdrop should react to the pointer, and RetroGrid or Ripple for a steadier geometric backdrop.

- Name: `meteors` (motion, Motion)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| count? | `number` | `16` | How many meteors are in flight at once. |
| angle? | `number` | `140` | Direction of travel in degrees. 0 points right, 90 falls straight down. |
| speed? | `number` | `1` | Speed multiplier. 2 is twice as fast, 0.5 half as fast. |
| tail? | `number` | `110` | Tail length in pixels. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |

```tsx

  <h2 className="text-4xl font-medium text-fg">Invoices that close themselves</h2>
```


### MorphPrice

A price card with a Monthly / Yearly toggle whose price digits roll to the new amount instead of swapping. Only the digits that change move, on the roll spring, so $49 to $39 turns one column. The new price and billing note are announced politely to screen readers; reduced motion swaps instantly.

Use it for one plan, or above a comparison table. Reach for PricingMotion for a row of plan cards, and the free PricingTable or PlanCard inside product billing screens.

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| currency? | `string` | `"USD"` | ISO 4217 currency code. |
| unit? | `string` | `"/ seat"` | Text after the price. |

### MorphingText

A headline that cycles through phrases by melting each one into the next with a blur and crossfade on two stacked layers. The old words blur and spread like wet ink while the new ones condense into focus. It holds the tallest phrase's height so nothing below it jumps, pauses off screen, and shows the first phrase for reduced motion. Screen readers get the whole list once.

Use it for one hero headline that cycles a few phrases. Reach for WordRotate to swap a single word inside a sentence, TypingText for a typewriter, and TextScramble for a one-off decode.

- Name: `morphing-text` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/morphing-text` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`

- Related: word-rotate, typing-text, text-scramble
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/morphing-text (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/morphing-text.md)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| words? | `string[]` | `["Invoices that close themselves", "R...` |  |
| interval? | `number` | `2600` | Milliseconds each phrase is held before it melts into the next. |
| duration? | `number` | `1` | Seconds one morph takes. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx

```

### OnboardingMotion

A short onboarding card that slides between steps, with a segmented progress bar you can click, Back and Continue, and a magnetic finish button. Each step slides in on the morph spring and leaves faster than it came. The progress segments are real buttons with `aria-current="step"`, and the step text is announced politely as it changes. Reduced motion swaps steps instantly.

Use it for a three-to-five step welcome on a marketing or signup page. Reach for the free OnboardingWizard for multi-step forms inside a product, OnboardingChecklist for a task list, and ProductTour to walk through features beside a preview.

- Name: `onboarding-motion` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/onboarding-motion` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { OnboardingMotion } from "@/components/ui/onboarding-motion"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/onboarding-motion"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Uses: button, magnetic-cta
- Related: onboarding-wizard, onboarding-checklist, product-tour
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/onboarding-motion (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/onboarding-motion.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| steps? | `OnboardingStep[]` | `SAMPLE_STEPS` | Steps in order. |
| finishLabel? | `string` | `"Open gallery"` | Label of the button on the last step. |
| onFinish? | `() => void` |  | Called when the finish button is pressed. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<OnboardingMotion
  steps={[{ title: "Connect your bank", body: "Transactions sync every hour." }, { title: "Send an invoice", body: "Numbering and reminders are handled." }]}
  finishLabel="Open Lumen"
  onFinish={() => router.push("/app")}
/>
```

### OrbitLogoCluster

A ring of logo or name pills slowly orbiting a centre badge, each pill staying upright as it travels. The orbit is a pair of CSS transform loops (the ring turns, each pill turns back), so it runs on the compositor and costs nothing on the main thread. It pauses while the pointer is over it and holds still for reduced motion. Screen readers get the names as a plain list.

Use it for "connects with" or partner sections with text names. Reach for OrbitingCircles for icons on several rings, and LogoWallMotion for a scrolling strip. Pass real partners: never invent logos.

- Name: `orbit-logo-cluster` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/orbit-logo-cluster` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { OrbitLogoCluster } from "@/components/ui/orbit-logo-cluster"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/orbit-logo-cluster"`)
- Related: orbiting-circles, logo-wall-motion
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/orbit-logo-cluster (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/orbit-logo-cluster.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| center? | `React.ReactNode` | `"MD"` | Content of the centre badge: your mark or a short name. |
| logos? | `React.ReactNode[]` | `["Acme", "Nova", "Orbit", "Pulse", "S...` | Names or logo elements on the ring. Elements need their own accessible name. |
| duration? | `number` | `40` | Seconds for one full orbit. |
| label? | `string` | `"Integrations"` | Accessible name for the list of logos. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<OrbitLogoCluster center="Lumen" logos={["Acme Bank", "Northwind CRM", "Globex Pay", "Contoso HR"]} duration={48} />
```

### OrbitingCircles

Icons orbiting a centre on hairline rings, each ring at its own speed and direction, for integration sections. Each ring sets its own radius, speed and direction; icons stay upright as they travel. Static for reduced motion. Everything is hidden from screen readers, so name the integrations in nearby text.

Use it for an integrations or "works with your stack" section. Reach for OrbitLogoCluster for text logos on one ring, IconCloud for a 3D sphere of icons, and AnimatedBeam to show data flowing between named tools.

- Name: `orbiting-circles` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/orbiting-circles` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { OrbitingCircles } from "@/components/ui/orbiting-circles"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/orbiting-circles"`)

- Related: orbit-logo-cluster, icon-cloud, animated-beam, ripple
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/orbiting-circles (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/orbiting-circles.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| rings? | `Ring[]` | `DEFAULT` |  |
| center? | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |
| size? | `number` | `340` | Box size in pixels. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<OrbitingCircles size={320} rings={[{ radius: 80, duration: 20, icons: [MailIcon, DatabaseIcon] }]} center={<Logo />} />
```

### ParallaxPanel

A sunken panel whose text and soft accent glow drift at different speeds as the page scrolls, giving the section depth. Both layers move with transforms tied straight to scroll position, so nothing lays out again and nothing lags. Reduced motion holds both still.

Use it for a quiet feature or manifesto section between busier ones. Reach for ScrollReveal to bring any block in once, StickyFeatureStory for a pinned multi-step story, and TiltCard for depth under the pointer instead.

- Name: `parallax-panel` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/parallax-panel` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |

| title? | `string` | `"Depth without blur shadows"` |  |
| body? | `string` | `"Scroll-linked motion stays Hairline-...` |  |
| depth? | `number` | `36` | Pixels the text travels across the full scroll through the panel. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ParallaxPanel eyebrow="Reconciliation" title="Every payment, matched" body="Lumen pairs deposits with invoices as they land." />
```

### Particles

A canvas particle field that drifts behind your content and parts around the pointer, or gathers toward it. Colour comes from the accent token and follows theme and material changes. The canvas is sharp on high density screens, resizes with its box, sleeps off screen and in background tabs, and draws one still frame for reduced motion.

Use it behind a hero or CTA panel that should feel alive under the pointer. Reach for Meteors for streaks, LightField for a soft WebGL glow, and DotPattern or FlickeringGrid for a static or barely moving texture.

- Name: `particles` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/particles` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { Particles } from "@/components/ui/particles"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/particles"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Uses: button
- Related: meteors, light-field, dot-pattern, flickering-grid, ripple, wavy-background
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/particles (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/particles.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| quantity? | `number` | `110` | Number of particles. |
| size? | `number` | `2` | Radius of the nearest particles in pixels. Farther ones are smaller. |
| color? | `string` | `"var(--accent)"` | Any CSS colour, including var(--token). Defaults to the accent. |
| mode? | `"repel" \| "attract"` | `"repel"` | Push particles away from the pointer, or pull them toward it. |
| radius? | `number` | `120` | Reach of the pointer in pixels. |
| drift? | `number` | `1` | Drift speed multiplier. 0 holds the field still apart from the pointer. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |

```tsx
<Particles quantity={140} mode="attract" className="h-[420px]">
  <h2 className="text-4xl font-medium text-fg">Every invoice, accounted for</h2>
</Particles>
```

### PinScrollGallery

A gallery that pins to the viewport and slides its frames sideways as you scroll down, then releases. The section is as tall as the frames need; vertical scroll drives a horizontal transform, so nothing lays out again while it moves. Reduced motion shows the frames as a plain grid instead of hijacking the scroll.

Use it for three to five big product moments on a launch page. Reach for HorizontalProductRail for a rail the visitor scrolls themselves, StickyFeatureStory for pinned steps beside one preview, and ScrollChapterStory for stacked chapters.

- Name: `pin-scroll-gallery` (motion, Motion)

| className? | `string` |  |  |


### PricingMotion

Pricing tiers that rise into view one after another as they scroll in. Each card rises on the morph spring with a short stagger, once. The featured plan gets the accent border, a "Most popular" badge and the solid button. Reduced motion shows every card in place.

### ProductOsMock

A mock product window with a sidebar of workspaces that cycles on its own, each view rising in with its rows and KPI bars. It auto-advances every few seconds to show the product breathing, pauses while the pointer or keyboard focus is inside, and stops for good once the visitor picks a view. Reduced motion never auto-advances and shows every view in place.

### ProductTour

A step list beside a stage that fades to the selected step, with Back and Next. On the last step Next becomes Done and calls `onFinish`. The list items are buttons marked `aria-current="step"`; the stage rises in on the morph spring and is announced politely as it changes. Optional `media` per step fills the stage. Reduced motion swaps steps instantly.

Use it to walk visitors through four or five features in order. Reach for OnboardingMotion for a compact welcome card, StickyFeatureStory when scroll should drive the steps, and the free OnboardingWizard for real forms.

- Name: `product-tour` (motion, Landing pages)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/product-tour` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ProductTour } from "@/components/ui/product-tour"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/product-tour"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Uses: button
- Related: onboarding-motion, sticky-feature-story, onboarding-wizard, product-os-mock
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/product-tour (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/product-tour.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| steps? | `TourStep[]` | `SAMPLE_STEPS` | Steps in order. |
| onStepChange? | `(index: number) => void` |  | Called with the index of the step the visitor moves to. |
| onFinish? | `() => void` |  | Called when the visitor presses Done on the last step. Without it, Done is disabled. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ProductTour steps={[{ title: "Connect your bank", body: "Transactions sync every hour.", media: <img src="/bank.png" alt="" /> }]} />
```

### RetroGrid

A retro perspective grid floor that recedes to a glowing horizon and scrolls slowly toward you. Lines are tinted with the accent and fade out before they reach the horizon, so they never shimmer. The floor sits behind the content, ignores the pointer, pauses off screen and holds still for reduced motion.

Use it behind a launch, deploy or developer-tool hero. Reach for DotPattern or BackgroundBoxes for a flat grid, and LampEffect when the headline should be lit rather than grounded.

- Name: `retro-grid` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/retro-grid` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { RetroGrid } from "@/components/ui/retro-grid"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/retro-grid"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Uses: button
- Related: dot-pattern, background-boxes, lamp-effect, meteors
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/retro-grid (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/retro-grid.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| angle? | `number` | `68` | Tilt of the floor in degrees. Higher is flatter and longer. |
| cellSize? | `number` | `48` | Size of one grid cell in pixels, at the front of the floor. |
| speed? | `number` | `0.7` | Cells per second travelled toward the viewer. |
| horizon? | `number` | `56` | Where the floor meets the sky, as a percent of the height from the top. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |

```tsx
<RetroGrid angle={70} cellSize={56}>
  <h2 className="text-4xl font-medium text-fg">Every release, right on schedule</h2>
</RetroGrid>
```

### Ripple

Concentric rings behind your content with a soft pulse that travels outward ring by ring, like a sonar ping. Clicking or tapping the panel sends an extra ripple out from the pointer. The rings sit behind the content, pause off screen and hold still for reduced motion.

Use it behind a "live", "listening" or "connected" message. Reach for OrbitingCircles to show integrations around a centre, and Meteors or Particles for a looser, less centred backdrop.

- Name: `ripple` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/ripple` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { Ripple } from "@/components/ui/ripple"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/ripple"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Uses: button
- Related: orbiting-circles, meteors, particles
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/ripple (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/ripple.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| count? | `number` | `7` | Number of rings. |
| spacing? | `number` | `44` | Gap between neighbouring rings in pixels. |
| size? | `number` | `128` | Diameter of the innermost ring in pixels. |
| origin? | `{ x: number; y: number }` | `{ x: 50, y: 50 }` | Centre of the rings, in percent of the panel width and height. |
| duration? | `number` | `4` | Seconds for one pulse to travel out and settle. |
| interactive? | `boolean` | `true` | Send a ripple out from the pointer on click or tap. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |

```tsx
<Ripple count={6} origin={{ x: 50, y: 40 }}>
  <h2 className="text-4xl font-medium text-fg">Lumen hears every payment</h2>
</Ripple>
```
