### ScratchToReveal

A scratch card: a foil you rub away with the pointer or a finger to reveal what is underneath, which clears itself once enough is gone. The foil is a canvas painted with a gradient from your tokens. Progress is tracked on a coarse grid, so there is no pixel reading on every move. Past the threshold the rest lifts away on its own and onComplete fires. A Reveal button serves keyboard users, and reduced motion skips the fade.

Use it for a playful reward, promo code or launch teaser. Reach for SecretReveal to show a sensitive value behind a click, and BeforeAfterWipe to compare two images.

- Name: `scratch-to-reveal` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/scratch-to-reveal` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ScratchToReveal } from "@/components/ui/scratch-to-reveal"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/scratch-to-reveal"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Related: progress, secret-reveal, before-after-wipe
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/scratch-to-reveal (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/scratch-to-reveal.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| threshold? | `number` | `50` | Percent of the foil that must be scratched before the rest clears itself. |
| brush? | `number` | `24` | Brush radius in pixels. |
| gradient? | `string[]` | `DEFAULT_GRADIENT` | Colours of the foil gradient. CSS colours and var(--token) both work. |
| label? | `string` | `"Scratch to reveal"` | Hint printed on the foil. |
| onComplete? | `() => void` |  | Called once the card is fully revealed. |
| onProgress? | `(percent: number) => void` |  | Called with the scratched percentage as it changes. |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ScratchToReveal threshold={45} onComplete={() => track("reward_revealed")}>
  <p className="p-8 text-center text-2xl text-fg">20% off Lumen Pro</p>
</ScratchToReveal>
```

### ScrollChapterStory

A long-form story told in numbered chapters that rise in as you reach them, under a sticky progress bar that fills with your reading. The progress bar is a scaleX transform tied straight to scroll, so it never lays out again. Each chapter rises once on the morph spring. Reduced motion shows chapters in place and the bar still tracks progress, without motion.

Use it for a narrative "how it works" or manifesto section. Reach for StickyFeatureStory for steps beside one pinned preview, TracingBeam for a changelog-style timeline, and ScrollProgress for a page-wide reading bar.

- Name: `scroll-chapter-story` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/scroll-chapter-story` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ScrollChapterStory } from "@/components/ui/scroll-chapter-story"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/scroll-chapter-story"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Related: sticky-feature-story, tracing-beam, scroll-progress, pin-scroll-gallery, stack-reveal-story
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/scroll-chapter-story (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/scroll-chapter-story.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| chapters? | `Chapter[]` | `CHAPTERS` | Chapters in order. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ScrollChapterStory chapters={[{ kicker: "01 · Send", title: "Invoices go out on time.", body: "Schedules and reminders are automatic." }]} />
```

### ScrollProgressRail

A sticky top rail with a thin bar that fills as the page scrolls and a row of section labels underneath. The bar is a scaleX transform smoothed by the release spring, so it glides with the scroll; reduced motion tracks the scroll exactly. Labels are plain text by default, or pass `href`s to make them in-page links.

Use it at the top of a long launch or story page. Reach for ScrollProgress for a bare bar or a percent ring, and the free TableOfContents for a full side navigation that highlights the current section.

- Name: `scroll-progress-rail` (motion, Navigation)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/scroll-progress-rail` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ScrollProgressRail } from "@/components/ui/scroll-progress-rail"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/scroll-progress-rail"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Related: scroll-progress, table-of-contents
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/scroll-progress-rail (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/scroll-progress-rail.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| labels? | `RailLabel[]` | `["Intro", "Product", "Proof", "Pricing"]` | Section labels, left to right. Strings render as text; `{ label, href }` renders a link. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ScrollProgressRail labels={[{ label: "Intro", href: "#intro" }, { label: "Pricing", href: "#pricing" }]} />
```

### ScrollProgress

Reading progress as a thin bar that fills along the top edge and a ring with the percent inside, for the page or any scrollable element. Pin it to the viewport with `fixed`, point it at a scroller with `container`, or give it children and it becomes its own scrolling panel. The spring gives the bar a little weight as you scroll; reduced motion tracks the scroll position exactly.

Use it on long articles, docs and changelogs. Reach for ScrollProgressRail for a sticky rail with section labels, and the free Progress for task progress that is not tied to scrolling.

- Name: `scroll-progress` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/scroll-progress` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ScrollProgress } from "@/components/ui/scroll-progress"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/scroll-progress"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Related: scroll-progress-rail, progress, scroll-chapter-story
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/scroll-progress (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/scroll-progress.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| variant? | `"bar" \| "circle" \| "both"` | `"both"` | Which indicators to show. |
| container? | `React.RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` |  | A scrollable element to track instead of the window. The indicators render where you put them, inside a `relative` wrapper. |
| fixed? | `boolean` | `false` | Pin the indicators to the viewport and track the page (or `container`). Nothing else renders. |
| height? | `number` | `3` | Bar thickness in pixels. |
| size? | `number` | `40` | Ring diameter in pixels. |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Without `fixed` or `container`, the component scrolls this content in its own panel. |
| title? | `React.ReactNode` | `"What is new in Lumen 3.0"` | Panel header title. |
| subtitle? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Release notes · 4 min read"` | Panel header line under the title. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ScrollProgress fixed variant="bar" />
<ScrollProgress variant="both" title="Release notes">{longContent}</ScrollProgress>
```

### ScrollReveal

A wrapper that lifts any block into place on a spring the first time it scrolls into view. Only transform moves, so the content is visible and readable from the first paint (no hidden text for search engines or screen readers) and nothing lays out again. It plays once; reduced motion shows the block in place.

Use it on marketing sections that should arrive as you reach them; stagger siblings with `delay`. Reach for BlurFade for a blur-and-fade entrance, TextReveal for word-by-word paragraphs, and nothing at all inside product UI, where content should simply be there.

- Name: `scroll-reveal` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/scroll-reveal` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ScrollReveal } from "@/components/ui/scroll-reveal"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/scroll-reveal"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Related: blur-fade, text-reveal, parallax-panel
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/scroll-reveal (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/scroll-reveal.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| y? | `number` | `18` | Pixels the block rises from. |
| delay? | `number` | `0` | Seconds to wait after it enters view. Use small steps (0.06 to 0.1) to stagger siblings. |

```tsx
<ScrollReveal delay={0.08}>
  <FeatureCard />
</ScrollReveal>
```

### ShimmerButton

A call-to-action button with a slow band of light sweeping across its face, a lit top edge and a soft bloom. The sweep is not rendered for reduced motion. Renders a button with `type="button"`, or pass `render` to make it a link.

Use it for the single most important action on a marketing page. Reach for Button in product UI, MagneticCta when the action should move toward the pointer, and BorderBeam or ShineBorder to light a whole card.

- Name: `shimmer-button` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/shimmer-button` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ShimmerButton } from "@/components/ui/shimmer-button"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/shimmer-button"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Related: button, magnetic-cta, border-beam, shine-border
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/shimmer-button (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/shimmer-button.md)

Props (also accepts <button>):

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| duration? | `number` | `2.6` | Seconds for one sweep. |
| tone? | `"ink" \| "accent"` | `"ink"` | Ink is the kit's primary action; accent spends the brand violet. |
| size? | `"default" \| "lg"` | `"lg"` | `lg` (the default) is 48px tall, `default` is 40px. |
| render? | `React.ReactElement<Record<string, unknown>>` |  | Render as another element, e.g. <a href="/signup" /> or a router Link. Props and handlers are passed through. |

```tsx
<ShimmerButton tone="accent" onClick={startTrial}>Start free trial</ShimmerButton>
<ShimmerButton render={<a href="/signup" />}>Get started</ShimmerButton>
```

### ShineBorder

A card whose border is a band of coloured light sweeping around it, masked to the border ring so the content is untouched. A conic gradient of your colours turns on a registered CSS angle behind a mask that keeps only the ring, so it stays crisp at any radius. It holds still for reduced motion.

Use it to single out one card: a featured plan, a new release, an invite. Reach for BorderBeam for a short travelling beam instead of a band, and CtaGlow for a whole glowing call-to-action section.

- Name: `shine-border` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/shine-border` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { ShineBorder } from "@/components/ui/shine-border"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/shine-border"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Uses: button
- Related: border-beam, cta-glow, shimmer-button, tilt-card
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/shine-border (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/shine-border.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |
| colors? | `string[]` | `["var(--accent)", "var(--accent-2)", ...` | Colours in the band, in order. Any CSS colour; tokens like var(--accent) work. |
| duration? | `number` | `8` | Seconds per lap. |
| borderWidth? | `number` | `2` | Border width in pixels. |
| radius? | `number` | `18` | Corner radius in pixels. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<ShineBorder radius={16} duration={6}>
  <div className="rounded-[inherit] bg-surface p-6">Lumen Pro</div>
</ShineBorder>
```

### SoftStack

A small stack of cards that fan up into a tidy, receding pile on a spring when it scrolls into view. Each card sits a little lower and smaller than the one in front, so the pile reads as depth without blurred shadows. It plays once; reduced motion shows the settled pile.

Use it as a light visual beside feature copy ("your workspaces", "every account"). Reach for StackRevealStory for readable stacked cards with body text, and DeviceFrameStack for stacked screenshots.

### SparklesText

Text with small four-point stars that twinkle in and out around it at random. Stars are placed at random and replaced as they fade, only while the text is on screen. They are decorative and hidden from assistive tech; the text stays a normal text node.

Numbered cards that rise on a spring and overlap into a stack on wider screens, telling a short three-step story. From md up each card tucks under the one before it; on phones they sit as a plain list so nothing overlaps text. Each card plays once; reduced motion shows the stack in place.

### StatsCounter

A single stat whose digits roll up from zero, odometer style, when it scrolls into view, for stats sections. The digits spring into place with the roll preset rather than counting through every value. Screen readers and search engines get the final value as plain text from the first paint; reduced motion shows it straight away.

Use it for one figure in a row of stats. Reach for MetricTickerBoard for a ready-made board of several, and NumberRoll for a live value that changes.

- Name: `stats-counter` (motion, Motion)

- Related: metric-ticker-board, number-roll, launch-countdown

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value? | `number` | `12400` | The final value. Use a real figure: never invent stats. |
| label? | `string` | `"invoices paid this month"` | What the number counts, shown under it. |
| suffix? | `string` | `""` | Text after the number, like "%" or "+". |
| format? | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` |  | Intl.NumberFormat options, e.g. { style: "currency", currency: "USD" }. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<div className="grid grid-cols-3 gap-4">
  <StatsCounter value={12400} label="invoices paid this month" />

</div>
```

### StickyCtaBar

A floating call-to-action bar that springs up from the bottom of the screen once the visitor has scrolled past the hero, and tucks away again at the top. While hidden it is inert, so keyboard and screen-reader users never land on buttons they cannot see. It moves on the snappy spring; reduced motion shows and hides it instantly.

Use it on long marketing pages where the hero CTA scrolls away. Reach for the free StickyBar or PublishBar for in-product action bars, and AnnouncementBar for a message pinned to the top.

- Name: `sticky-cta-bar` (motion, Landing pages)


### StickyFeatureStory

A pinned two-column story: as you scroll, each step on the left lights up in turn while a mock preview on the right follows along. The section is as tall as its steps need and works for any number of them. The active step nudges into place on the snappy spring and is marked `aria-current="step"`. Reduced motion drops the pinning and shows every step as a plain list.

Use it to explain three to five features in order on a launch page. Reach for ScrollChapterStory for full-width chapters, PinScrollGallery for big sideways frames, and ProductTour when the visitor should click through.

### Terminal

An animated terminal window that types each command and prints its output line by line, with a blinking cursor and a replay button. Five line kinds (command, output, success, error, info) each get their own token colour and glyph. Typing pauses while the window is off screen and picks up where it left off; reduced motion prints the whole transcript at once. The box reserves its full height, so nothing below it shifts.

Use it to show an install command or CLI flow on a docs or launch page. Reach for the free TerminalWindow for a static transcript, CodeBlock for copyable code, and ConsoleOutput for streaming logs inside product UI.

- Name: `terminal` (motion, Dev tools)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/terminal` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { Terminal } from "@/components/ui/terminal"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/terminal"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Related: terminal-window, code-block, console-output
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/terminal (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/terminal.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| lines? | `TerminalLine[]` | `SAMPLE_LINES` |  |
| title? | `string` | `"Terminal"` |  |
| prompt? | `string` | `"❯"` | Prompt printed before each command. |
| typingSpeed? | `number` | `26` | Milliseconds per typed character. |
| lineDelay? | `number` | `160` | Milliseconds before each output line prints. |
| commandDelay? | `number` | `600` | Milliseconds before a command starts typing. |
| loop? | `boolean` | `false` | Start over after the last line, with a pause. |
| replay? | `boolean` | `true` | Show the replay button in the title bar. |
| appearance? | `"dark" \| "auto"` | `"dark"` | Stay dark in both themes, or follow the page theme. |
| onComplete? | `() => void` |  | Called once the last line has printed. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<Terminal title="zsh" lines={[{ kind: "command", text: "npx shadcn@latest add https://ui.minidev.pro/r/button.json" }, { kind: "success", text: "Created 1 file" }]} />
```

### TestimonialCarousel

One large customer quote at a time that rotates on its own, with dot and Previous / Next controls. It follows the WAI-ARIA carousel pattern: a labelled region, slide buttons with `aria-current`, rotation that pauses while the pointer or keyboard focus is inside and stops once the visitor takes control, and a polite announcement only when the visitor changes the slide. Quotes rise on the morph spring and leave faster; reduced motion never auto-rotates.

Use it for three to six longer testimonials. Reach for MarqueeQuotes for many short quotes at once, and the free Testimonial or PressQuote for a single static quote. Use real customer words: never invent testimonials.

- Name: `testimonial-carousel` (motion, Landing pages)

- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/testimonial-carousel (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/testimonial-carousel.md)

| interval? | `number` | `4500` | Milliseconds each quote stays while auto-rotating. 0 turns rotation off. |
| label? | `string` | `"Customer testimonials"` | Accessible name of the carousel region. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<TestimonialCarousel interval={6000} items={[{ quote: "Month-end close went from four days to one.", name: "Maya Patel", role: "Controller, Northwind" }]} />
```

### TextScramble

A short monospace line that decodes from random glyphs into the real text, left to right, the first time it scrolls into view. The real text is in the page from the first paint and is what screen readers and search engines read; the scrambled glyphs are hidden from them. Monospace keeps the width steady while it decodes. It plays once; reduced motion shows the text straight away.

Use it for a short label, eyebrow or code-flavoured headline (two or three words). Reach for HyperText for a scramble on hover, TypingText for a typewriter, and WordRotate or MorphingText for cycling phrases.

- Name: `text-scramble` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/text-scramble` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { TextScramble } from "@/components/ui/text-scramble"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/text-scramble"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Related: hyper-text, typing-text, word-rotate, morphing-text
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/text-scramble (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/text-scramble.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| text? | `string` | `"PREMIUM MOTION"` | The final text. Short, uppercase lines decode best. |
| glyphs? | `string` | `GLYPHS` | Characters drawn while decoding. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<TextScramble text="RECONCILED" />
```

### TiltCard

A card that tilts toward the pointer in 3D, with a sliding glare and parallax children, and springs flat when the pointer leaves. The glare moves across the face like light on a foil print. Children marked `data-depth` float at their own parallax rate. Touch scrolls straight through it; reduced motion keeps it flat.

Use it for a showcase card, a pricing hero or a product shot. Reach for CardTilt for a simpler tilt without glare or depth, and ShineBorder to draw the eye without motion.

- Name: `tilt-card` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/tilt-card` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { TiltCard } from "@/components/ui/tilt-card"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/tilt-card"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Uses: button
- Related: card-tilt, shine-border, parallax-panel
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/tilt-card (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/tilt-card.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |
| maxTilt? | `number` | `12` | Maximum rotation in degrees on either axis. |
| glare? | `number` | `0.6` | Glare strength from 0 (off) to 1. |
| perspective? | `number` | `900` | Perspective distance in pixels; smaller is more dramatic. |
| parallax? | `number` | `10` | Pixels of travel for a child with `data-depth="1"`; scale the number for more or less. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<TiltCard maxTilt={10}>
  <div className="rounded-xl bg-surface p-6"><h3 data-depth="1">Lumen Pro</h3></div>
</TiltCard>
```

### TracingBeam

A vertical beam beside long content that grows as you scroll, with a glowing tip and a node that lights for each entry. The beam is an SVG path driven by scroll progress through the section and smoothed with a spring, so it glides rather than jumps. Each direct child of the content gets a node on the track that fills the moment the beam passes it. Reduced motion drops the spring and follows the scroll exactly.

Use it for changelogs, timelines and long step-by-step stories. Reach for the free Timeline for a static list, and StickyFeatureStory or ScrollChapterStory for full-screen scroll chapters.

- Name: `tracing-beam` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/tracing-beam` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { TracingBeam } from "@/components/ui/tracing-beam"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/tracing-beam"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Related: timeline, sticky-feature-story, scroll-chapter-story
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/tracing-beam (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/tracing-beam.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items? | `TracingBeamItem[]` | `DEFAULT_ITEMS` | Entries to trace. Each one gets a node on the beam. |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Your own content in place of the entries. Each direct child gets a node. |
| color? | `string` | `"var(--accent)"` | Beam colour. Any CSS colour, including var(--token). Defaults to the accent. |
| rail? | `number` | `40` | Width of the rail the beam runs in, in pixels. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<TracingBeam items={[{ version: "v3.2", date: "14 Oct 2026", title: "Auto-reconcile", body: "…" }]} />
```

### TypingText

A typewriter line that types a phrase, holds, deletes it and moves to the next, with a blinking caret. Starts when it scrolls into view, and screen readers get the phrases as plain text instead of the keystrokes. Reduced motion shows the first phrase in full.

Use it for a short hero line that types a few phrases. Reach for WordRotate to swap one word in a sentence, MorphingText for a softer melt, and HeroTypedHeadline for a complete typed hero.

- Name: `typing-text` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/typing-text` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { TypingText } from "@/components/ui/typing-text"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/typing-text"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Related: word-rotate, morphing-text, hero-typed-headline, text-scramble
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/typing-text (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/typing-text.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| phrases? | `string[]` | `["Build the MVP.", "Ship it in 30 day...` |  |
| speed? | `number` | `55` | Milliseconds per typed character. |
| hold? | `number` | `1400` | Milliseconds to hold a finished phrase. |
| loop? | `boolean` | `true` |  |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<TypingText phrases={["Send the invoice.", "Get paid on time."]} speed={50} />
```

### TypographicMarquee

Big display phrases separated by accent dots, scrolling endlessly across a band, for a bold typographic break between sections. The band loops on the compositor (a CSS transform), pauses while the pointer is over it, and holds still for reduced motion. Screen readers read the phrases once; the looping copy is hidden from them.

Use it as a loud divider or a list of selling points. Reach for LogoWallMotion for logos, MarqueeQuotes for testimonials, and the free Marquee for a small, quiet ticker.

- Name: `typographic-marquee` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/typographic-marquee` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { TypographicMarquee } from "@/components/ui/typographic-marquee"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/typographic-marquee"`)
- Related: logo-wall-motion, marquee-quotes, marquee, pricing-kinetic
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/typographic-marquee (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/typographic-marquee.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| phrases? | `string[]` |  | Phrases in order. Keep them short: two or three words each. |
| text? | `string` |  | Deprecated. |
| duration? | `number` | `28` | Seconds for one full loop. Higher is calmer. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<TypographicMarquee phrases={["Bank sync", "Auto reminders", "One-click close"]} duration={24} />
```

### WaitlistHero

A "coming soon" hero with a breathing accent glow, a one-field email form that handles loading, success and error, and a social-proof row. `onSubmit` may return a promise: the button shows progress, success replaces the form with a confirmation, and a thrown error keeps the typed email and shows the message. Results are announced to screen readers. The glow holds still for reduced motion.

Use it for a pre-launch page or a gated beta. Reach for CommandWaitlist for a command-palette styled signup, the free NewsletterSignup for a small inline form, and LaunchCountdown to add a clock.

- Name: `waitlist-hero` (motion, Landing pages)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/waitlist-hero` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { WaitlistHero } from "@/components/ui/waitlist-hero"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/waitlist-hero"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Uses: button, input, social-proof
- Related: command-waitlist, newsletter-signup, launch-countdown
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/waitlist-hero (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/waitlist-hero.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onSubmit? | `(email: string) => void \| Promise<void>` |  | Called with the email. Return a promise to show progress; throw to show an error. |
| eyebrow? | `string` | `"Coming soon"` | Small label above the title. |
| title? | `string` | `"Join the waitlist"` |  |
| description? | `string` | `"Be first to the motion pack, landing...` |  |
| submitLabel? | `string` | `"Request access"` | Submit button label. |
| successMessage? | `string` | `"You are on the list. We will email y...` | Shown in place of the form after a successful submit. |
| proof? | `React.ReactNode` |  | Social proof under the form. Defaults to a sample avatar row; pass null to hide it. Never invent numbers. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<WaitlistHero
  title="Lumen 3.0 is almost here"
  onSubmit={async (email) => { await fetch("/api/waitlist", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ email }) }) }}
  proof={null}
/>
```

### WaveformHero

A hero with a headline over a row of thin accent bars that rise and fall like a live audio waveform, and a magnetic call to action. The bars breathe with compositor-only CSS transforms, each at its own pace, pause while off screen, and hold still for reduced motion. The waveform is decorative and hidden from screen readers.

Use it for audio, voice, AI-call or "live" products. Reach for WavyBackground for soft rolling waves behind any hero, and the free AudioPlayer when the waveform must reflect real audio.

- Name: `waveform-hero` (motion, Landing pages)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/waveform-hero` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { WaveformHero } from "@/components/ui/waveform-hero"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/waveform-hero"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Uses: magnetic-cta
- Related: wavy-background, audio-player
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/waveform-hero (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/waveform-hero.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title? | `string` | `"Sound without the noise"` |  |
| description? | `string` | `"A kinetic waveform drawn in hairline...` |  |
| cta? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Start free"` | Label of the call to action. Pass null to hide it. |
| bars? | `number` | `48` | Number of bars. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |

```tsx
<WaveformHero title="Every call, transcribed" description="Lumen listens to supplier calls and logs every promise to pay." cta="Try it free" />
```

### WavyBackground

Layered canvas waves that roll across the bottom of the panel behind your content, each at its own pace. Every wave is two sine harmonics with its own phase, so the layers breathe against each other instead of marching in step. Colours resolve through the cascade, so var(--accent) follows theme and material changes. The canvas is sharp on high density screens, resizes with its box, sleeps off screen and in background tabs, and draws one still frame for reduced motion.

Use it behind a hero, footer or sign-up panel. Reach for AuroraBackground for a CSS-only gradient, LightField for a WebGL glow, and Meteors or Particles for small moving points.

- Name: `wavy-background` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/wavy-background` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { WavyBackground } from "@/components/ui/wavy-background"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/wavy-background"`)
- Dependencies: lucide-react, motion
- Uses: button
- Related: aurora-background, light-field, meteors, particles, waveform-hero
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/wavy-background (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/wavy-background.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| colors? | `string[]` | `["var(--chart-2)", "var(--info)", "va...` | Colours of the waves, back to front. Any CSS colour, including var(--token). |
| speed? | `number` | `1` | Speed multiplier. 2 is twice as fast, 0.5 half as fast. |
| amplitude? | `number` | `26` | Height of the swell in pixels. |
| blur? | `number` | `8` | Softness in pixels. 0 draws crisp edges. |
| coverage? | `number` | `0.46` | Share of the panel the waves rise to, from the bottom, 0 to 1. |
| opacity? | `number` | `0.46` | Opacity of each wave, 0 to 1. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| children? | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |

```tsx
<WavyBackground coverage={0.5}>
  <h2 className="text-4xl font-medium text-fg">Cash flow, smoothed out</h2>
</WavyBackground>
```

### WordRotate

A sentence with one word that rotates through a list in place, lifting and blurring out as the next rises in. The slot holds every word invisibly, so it is always as wide as the widest one and the sentence around it never jumps. The new word arrives on the morph spring and the old one leaves faster than it came. It pauses off screen, shows the first word for reduced motion, and screen readers hear the full list once.

Use it for a hero line like "Interfaces for <rotating word>". Reach for MorphingText to cycle whole phrases, TypingText for a typewriter, and HyperText or TextScramble for a one-off decode.

- Name: `word-rotate` (motion, Motion)
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add @minidev/word-rotate` or `npm i minidev-ui-kit`
- Import: `import { WordRotate } from "@/components/ui/word-rotate"` (npm: `"minidev-ui-kit/premium/word-rotate"`)
- Dependencies: motion
- Related: morphing-text, typing-text, hyper-text, text-scramble
- Docs: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/word-rotate (Markdown: https://ui.minidev.pro/docs/word-rotate.md)

Props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| words? | `string[]` | `["startups", "agencies", "fintech", "...` | Words to cycle through, in order. |
| interval? | `number` | `2200` | Milliseconds each word stays. |
| className? | `string` |  |  |
| prefix? | `React.ReactNode` | `"Interfaces for"` | Text before the rotating word. |

```tsx
<WordRotate prefix="Invoicing for" words={["agencies", "studios", "consultants"]} interval={2400} />
```
